Sports.title: 'Let's go one more time' - Taylor bows out from boxing at 'dream' venue
Sports.content:
Katie Taylor's glittering boxing career will draw to a close on Saturday night at her "dream venue" and with the message a simple one: "Let's go one more time".

Taylor will aim to retire as a three-time undisputed world champion when she takes on unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

The 40-year-old, who weighed in at 139.6lbs for the super-lightweight showdown compared to Pili's 139.9lbs, has pretty much done it all in boxing.

Her accolades including winning Olympic gold in London in 2012 and, along with Amanda Serrano, becoming the first woman to headline a fight card at New York's iconic Madison Square ‌Garden.

She also avenged her sole pro defeat, against Chantelle Cameron.

But she has never fought at Croke Park before - until now.

Image: Pili (right) has a 12-0 record as a pro

'This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for'

While fight week, quite rightly, has seen the great and good of boxing and beyond praise Taylor's career, hail the inspiration she has been and discuss the legacy she will leave, the woman herself is not looking beyond Pili.

Speaking shortly after hitting the scales on Friday evening, the Bray Bomber, said: "My mind is focused on the fight. I have a job to do against a very tough challenger.

"I have built my reputation on always taking the tough fights, so why treat my last fight any differently? This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for. Let's go one more time."

Taylor did, though, turn to address her fans at the weigh-in, many of whom will also be rooting for her inside the stadium this weekend.

"I am blown away. I want to put on a performance worthy of the support I have had these last few years

"You guys have carried me throughout the Olympics and my whole career. Thank you so much. I am so grateful.

"I am so excited. I have been dreaming about this for the last few years and I am one day away from ending my career in a dream venue in front of all these amazing people."

Image: Katie Taylor has only lost once as a pro, a defeat to Chantelle Cameron that she went on to avenge

'Katie is an absolute hero to so many people'

Former world champion Carl Frampton, speaking on DAZN, feels the lure of a bout at Saturday's prolonged Taylor's time as an active fighter.

He said: "She has completed the sport but I think one of the reasons she held on was the dream of fighting at Croke Park. She has finally got it.

"Katie is an absolute hero to so many people, an inspiration. It is a perfect way to finish - but she has to win first and we can't rule out Pili who is a very good fighter."

But is it definitely it for Taylor - or is a return to the ring possible?

Three-weight world champion Mikaela Mayer added: "Katie has always been very true to her word.

"If she says this is her last fight, I believe it to be. If she wants to come back, I would not be upset about it. We'd love to see her again.

"I am benefitting off of her hard work and everything she has helped create for the women in this sport. I am sad as I had always hoped to share the ring with Katie."

Sports.title: Sabalenka complains of cannabis smell during win as Alcaraz progresses
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka complained to the umpire about a strong ​smell of cannabis that was present duing her third-round win over Kamilla Rakhimova at the US Open.

The world No 1 came through in straight sets, beating her unseeded opponent 6-3 6-4 on Louis Armstrong Stadium, but after racing into a 3-0 lead in the opening set, Sabalenka complained to umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore at the first changeover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player World number one Aryna Sabalenka stopped her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova due to a 'strong' smell of cannabis

"I was like, 'Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around ‌the tennis courts'," Sabalenka told reporters afterwards. "It's a bit tricky to handle that smell while you're trying to compete at your best."

No fans were found to be smoking and ejected from the tennis grounds.

Sabalenka added: "I don't know if it was coming from the crowd or was from the outside, because the wind blows it into the stadium. I don't know. I just hope they're going to be a bit more aware of that stuff."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka' spoke about the 'disruption' following her brief halt of play during her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova due to a 'strong' smell of cannabis

US Tennis Association spokesman Brendan McIntyre said in a statement: "While we can't control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this facility as a smoke free environment."

The distraction didn't affect Sabalenka's form in the slightest as she didn't miss a single first serve until the seventh game of the match, in which Rakhimova would three times take her to deuce.

That would prove to be Rakhimova's only real opening in the first set, Sabalenka taking it 6-3, but she'd prove much more competitive in the second.

Rakhimova came from behind four-straight times to hold serve, saving four break points along the way, before Sabalenka finally ended her resolve in the ninth game of the second set.

On this occasion, Rakhimova let a 40-0 lead slip as the four-time Grand Slam champion battled back to secure the crucial break before serving things out to book her spot in the last 16.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Naomi Osaka, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff weigh in on influencers disrupting matches at the US Open

Sabalenka 'shuts down outside noise' to book Townsend meeting

After Sabalenka's second-round win, she cut short questions about her pre-tournament activities in an excruciating exchange with a reporter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka was quick to highlight that everything she does off-court is worked around her tennis schedule

A regular poster on social media at the various events she attends and with the brands she works, Sabalenka fired back that her off-court appearances had not come at the expense of her preparations ​for Flushing Meadows.

Referencing that further after her victory over Rakhimova, Sabalenka added: "I completely shut down noise from outside.

"I focus on myself, and I know if I do that and work really hard I will have my chances and be able to play a great level of tennis."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka was left furious over questions during her press conference at the US Open following her round-two victory, as one reporter asked her about her pre-tournament 'partying'

Trying to become the first player to win three-straight US Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14, Sabalenka will face American Taylor Townsend in the last 16 after she beat 13th seed Diana Shnaider 6-2 6-7 (3-7) 6-3

Jessica Pegula kept alive her bid ‌for a maiden Grand Slam title when the third seed rallied from behind ‌to beat fellow former US Open finalist Leylah Fernandez 1-6 ​6-4 6-3.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Jessica Pegula vs Leylah Fernandez against from the US Open

The American will face Romania's Sorana Cirstea ​in the last 16 after the 16th seed defeated Italy Jasmine Paolini in straight sets 6-3 6-3.

Alcaraz overcomes mid-match wobble to reach fourth round

Defending men's champion Carlos Alcaraz continued his impressive comeback after more than four months out to a wrist injury, as he beat Wu Yibing in straight sets, 6-3 6-4 6-1, on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open match between Carlos Alcaraz and Yibing Wu

The seven-time Grand Slam champion was made to work harder than the scoreline suggests, however, as he was broken back in both the first two sets by his 113th-ranked opponent.

The second set, in particular, was cause for frustration for the Spaniard as he appeared to be cruising along at 2-0 up after winning five games in a row, only to again be pegged back by Wu.

Alcaraz would finally earn another break of serve in the 10th game to clinch a two-set lead before he finally pulled clear in the third.

"In the toughest moments I did everything good, which I'm really happy about," Alcaraz said in his on-court interview. "Could it be better? Yes. But overall I'm just really proud and happy with the performance today.

"To be honest, I'm playing better than I thought [after wrist injury]. Physically, I thought I was going to be dead after the first match. But I'm recovering really well.

"My level right now is really good, I've got the rhythm of the competition every time I step on the court."

Alcaraz will face American 20th seed Tommy Paul ‌in the last 16 after he emerged victorious from a five-set thriller against Kazakhstan's 15th seed Alexander Bublik, winning 6-4 3-6 6-7 (4-7) 6-1 6-3 in a match that lasted three hours and 13 minutes.

Elsewhere, seventh seed, and 2021 US Open champion, Daniil Medvedev overpowered Frenchman Arthur ‌Rinderknech with a 6-4 6-4 6-4 victory.

Sports.title: Isak’s rapid double sinks Ipswich to give Andoni Iraola first Liverpool win
Sports.content:
A first win for Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, the introduction of the latest star signing in Bradley Barcola making for a successful Friday night. Better yet, continuing signs that Alexander Isak, last year’s model, is coming back to life, his two, well-taken early goals securing the three points. That Cody Gakpo, Isak’s supplier, might have been at Manchester City or Tottenham had the transfer runes been right, added further to a sense of renewal. Liverpool’s attackers were full of the speed and invention sorely lacking for much of last season.

Once Barcola arrived in the second half, those velocity levels increased yet further, Liverpool playing the attacking style, high on risk and entertainment, the appointment of Iraola promised. “We are starting to get to the way we want to play,” said Isak afterwards.

Travelling Liverpool fans were made to wait for their first glimpse of £123m Barcola, his being on the bench adding further suspense to a deal that took an entire summer to complete.

If Ipswich looked to show the “emotional discipline” their manager, Gary O’Neil, said they lacked in losing 5-2 at Old Trafford, little was in evidence in a ruinous opening spell that betrayed the decent performance they went on to put in.

How long will Iraola’s doctrines take to embed? Perhaps not as long as feared. Isak, the most expensive player signed under the outgoing sporting director Richard Hughes, looks – at last – to be flowering. To follow his strike against Nottingham Forest, he had scored twice by the 10th minute. “If Alex is fit and is available, he will produce the numbers,” said Iraola.

Assisted for both by Gakpo, the finishes were of the gold standard Liverpool invested so heavily in. “Cody was outstanding,” said Virgil van Dijk, sharing the credit. “I said it before the transfer window had closed, he’s important for us, and he will be important this season.” Iraola joined the appreciation society: “I had no doubt with Cody … he knows how much we value him.”

“The level is ruthless,” said O’Neil, otherwise exalted by his team’s response to adversity beyond those opening nine minutes. “If you make mistakes against players like Gakpo, Wirtz and Barcola, there’s a chance you will get punished.”

Just as at Old Trafford, two Ipswich goals were conceded in quick, damaging succession, the defence far too open and chaotic. After Víctor Muñoz had set off on a long run stopped only by Issa Diop’s last-man tackle, Julio Enciso controlled the ball, taking a beat by standing on the ball, as if calling for calm.

Isak, who had a third first-half goal disallowed for offside, made the runs into scoring positions that made his reputation, nothing like the sorry figure of his debut, lost season. Meanwhile, a no-look pass from Ipswich’s captain, Dara O’Shea, straight to Gakpo, betrayed a collective cognitive dissonance.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola beats Dara O’Shea on his Liverpool debut. Photograph: Dave Shopland/AP

Florian Wirtz becoming involved with the tricks and flicks offered another pointer that last summer’s huge Liverpool outlay may not be so wasteful as it appeared in Arne Slot’s dog days. Iraola’s appointment came with a reputation for improving players. Should the Basque get the best from the German, in a similar price bracket to Barcola and Isak, then this week’s pronouncement he is happy with his squad will ring truer.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

An obvious gap in the Liverpool squad left by Hughes is a commanding defensive midfielder. Enciso often located space, though suffered for a lack of quality around him. Beyond the break, with O’Neil in full flow, barking at players and officials alike, Ipswich were more confrontational, less admiring of their opponent’s higher skill levels. “I hate having to talk about good performances when you don’t get points because you need to maximise them,” said O’Neil, painting a picture that will not match many other summations of the match.

Muñoz, stocky and adventurous, might well prove the answer to the right-wing vacancy left by Mohamed Salah, showing off a ready work ethic before departing in the double substitution that brought Barcola on. Isak also departed, returning after full time to an ovation from fans finally seeing something close to his potential.

With Gakpo pushed to centre-forward, Barcola’s first touches came off the left flank, one drop of the shoulder and sprint beyond O’Shea lifting the volume among the away supporters. “He hadn’t played a single minute since the World Cup so we had to be careful,” said Iraola. “He was always a threat.”

That burst of Barcola preceded another loss of Ipswich faculties as Leif Davis first pulled Dominik Szoboszlai, and then knocked him over for what appeared a clear penalty. Only an offside ruled by the video assistant protected the Ipswich defender’s modesty. The announcement of that decision brought the loudest cheer of the night from the home contingent.

Barcola, even amid the warp speed of the Premier League, showed lightning acceleration when creating a late chance for Gakpo. An impressive cameo and the expectation of far more to come from the player and his new team.

Sports.title: Alexia Putellas begins WSL ride as London City outclass Manchester United
Sports.content:
There are few scenarios since Millwall Lionesses broke away from Millwall and became London City Lionesses that would have felt more surreal than the idea of Alexia Putellas captaining the side to a statement win in a WSL season-opener in Bromley just seven years later.

Here we are though: referees have to get used to the formerly talismanic Barcelona captain stooping to pick up the coin after the toss, as is her custom; players must get used to eyes and cameras looking past them to focus in on the influential No 11; and the two-time Ballon d’Or winner has to get used to playing with teammates not drilled in a very specific style of play from such an early age that it becomes an inherent part of them.

Of course it is a step down to go from the three-time European champions to a team embarking on their second season in the WSL, but off the pitch, with the owner, Michele Kang, committed to giving female athletes the best of everything, the difference will be more negligible, even before the approved new world-class training facility is built.

Regardless of what you think of her movements in women’s football, or about private finance investment in it, Kang, who walked the perimeter of the stadium prior to kick-off taking photos with fans in her ‘Kang 27’ emblazoned home shirt, is the antithesis of the owner of last night’s opposition, Jim Ratcliffe, and his dismal references to his women’s teams.

View image in fullscreen Michele Kang did the rounds at a sold-out stadium, the first time London City Lionesses have done that since starting to play at Bromley. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Putellas led the team out to a ­raucous welcome at the sold-out home of Bromley FC, her steely stare only broken to crack a quick smile and share some words with the mascot gripping her hand.

In this corner of London’s outskirts, the midfielder experienced her first proper taste of her new reality. At 32 and with her very best years likely behind her, it was a solid rather than showstopper performance. She was outshone by teammates such as Rosa Kafaji and Lucía Corrales, who unfortunately went off on a stretcher late on after overstretching for the ball.

“Everybody knows what [Putellas] can create and bring to us,” said the London City manager, Eder Maestre. “It’s not just the things she’s capable of doing, it’s the things she facilitates for other players too.

“Having this kind of player in the squad is very important because she represents the highest standards and having her involved in it is not only because of her performance, but also because of the leadership she can bring in terms of helping us to reach that standard. But it is not only about Alexia, she is only one player, and I think the most impactful thing was the way everybody connected, the chemistry that we are building around the players.”

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas was solid rather than spectacular on her WSL debut. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Maestre has been tasked with gelling a squad stacked with new players, including the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps, who was on the bench with Elene Lete starting.

Maestre explained: “Mary had some issues in pre-season so that was why there was inconsistency in game involvement. We have two strong goalkeepers. Today, Elene deserved to be in the lineup. She was very strong in her actions.”

Maestre has said the identity he wants to create for the side is “related to all those things we felt when we were playing football as children”.

That ethos was evident in their play, with London City on the front foot from the off. Despite not always being pretty, they looked like they were having fun as they pressed and attacked aggressively, and when they broke the deadlock nine minutes in it was not surprising.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Alanna Kennedy provided the pressure, rising above a hunkered-down Julia Zigiotti Olme who could only turn the ball into her own net.

View image in fullscreen Delphine Cascarino (left), who set up London City Lionesses’ second goal, was named player of the match. Photograph: John Walton/PA

It was a cruel introduction to life in the WSL, and its spotlight, for the new Manchester United manager, Eva Olid, particularly with Chelsea and Arsenal up next, but on this showing and after a lacklustre summer transfer window, few games would have offered a kind introduction. United were outclassed in Bromley, conceding 60% possession.

They did at least manage three shots, but by the time they did any hopes of a leveller were crushed by the home side, when Mapi León’s corner was worked towards Delphine Cascarino and the French forward’s cross was delightfully flicked into the far corner by Daniëlle van de Donk.

“It’s a process,” said Olid. “I think it was something more mental in the first half, we could feel like the players were not believing.

“At half-time I say that this is not us, we need the ball to be ourselves … in the second half, we were building through the middle, finding the free player, playing between the lines. That is us, and I can feel my team in the second half. It’s my job to help them to believe that we can always be the team of the second half.”

There was a late consolation for Olid’s humbled charges deep into added time, when Simi Awujo powered in the loose ball after a free-kick was cleared into empty space, but it could not dampen the enthusiasm of an emphatic performance from Maestre’s side – a performance that is a very solid foundation to build on.

Sports.title: José Mourinho sick as a Parrott as Real Madrid sunk by Real Betis and Irish supersub
Sports.content:
Real Madrid’s perfect start in La Liga ⁠ended on Friday when Real Betis beat them 1-0, with the ⁠substitute Troy Parrott ⁠scoring ​nine minutes from time and goalkeeper Álvaro Valles saving a stoppage-time ⁠penalty from Kylian Mbappé.

The clash began at a high tempo but the pace ⁠dropped after the interval in the heat in ​Seville. The Republic of Ireland star Parrott, introduced ‌in the 68th ‌minute, broke the deadlock in the 81st when ‌he reacted quickly after Thibaut Courtois parried a header into his path.

Mbappé struck the crossbar four minutes later before the substitute Carlos Espí met a cross from Vinícius Júnior with a spectacular bicycle kick, only for the equaliser to be ruled ​out for offside following a VAR review.

Nelson Deossa then nearly sealed the victory for hosts Betis with a long-range effort after spotting Courtois ⁠off his line, but the goalkeeper recovered to ​make ​the save.

José Mourinho’s Madrid got one ​final opportunity when Natan brought down ​Vinícius inside ‌the area, ​deep ​into stoppage time, but Valles saved Mbappé’s spot-kick to preserve Betis’s lead and secure the three points.

“My team played a great game, and sometimes you lose and you don’t know why,” Mourinho said. “We dominated, controlling everything, lots of attacks, lots of chances. If we had drawn we would have been left frustrated, so imagine how we feel after losing.

“I don’t know how we lost because we played very well collectively. I cannot fault the attitude of any of my players. We deserved to win but deserving to win does not ⁠give you points. I’m very happy with ​my players, all ​of them. I cannot fault ​any of them individually. As for the penalty, when ​one of us ‌steps up to ​take it, ​we all stand together.

“The Betis players are more streetwise than the Madrid players, who are very honest. With the backing of a fantastic crowd, they manage to gain these kinds of advantages.”

Paris Saint-Germain looked to be on their way to their first Ligue 1 win of the season when Marquinhos put the hosts ahead in the 31st minute, but Monaco rallied with goals from Flavio Nazinho in the 58th minute and Stanis Idumbo in the 72nd. Monaco lead the table as the only team to win their opening three games.

“We clearly deserved to win. That is my opinion,” said Luis Enrique.

“I saw the game and it was the typical game in which we were better than the opposition and created a lot more chances, but the opposition goalkeeper was the best player on the pitch.”

The US striker Folarin Balogun was left out of Monaco’s squad after the collapse of his proposed transfer to Everton this week, while Lamine Camara played after his move to Chelsea was called off at the last minute.

View image in fullscreen PSG’s Fabián Ruiz (left) challenges for the ball with Monaco’s in-demand Lamine Camara. Photograph: Aurélien Morissard/AP

PSG had already drawn 2-2 with Rennes and Lille in their first two games and also lost the French Super Cup to Lens 1-0 last month.

The first league defeat came hours after PSG announced contract extensions for coach Luis Enrique and several players. João Neves, Lucas Beraldo, Senny Mayulu and Willian Pacho all signed new deals through to 2031, while Fabián Ruiz had his contract extended until 2028.

Lyon beat Auxerre 3-1 earlier on Friday and are second in the league, two points behind Monaco and level on points with Lille, who won 1-0 at Toulouse on Thursday thanks to an Ayase Ueda goal.

Assane Diao bagged a brace as Como rolled to a 4-1 win at Genoa in Serie A. Nico Paz and Martin Baturina also added goals. Cesc Fabregas’ side lead the Italian standings by one point ahead of a pack of six teams who have yet to play this weekend.

Como will make their Champions League debut against Leipzig on 10 September, with Manchester United to visit in October and PSG in January.

In Germany, Stuttgart romped to a 4-1 win over Köln in the Bundesliga.

Sports.title: Chelsea hit bullseye with Morgan Rogers as Arsenal rue what might have been
Sports.content:
Chelsea thought they had little chance of signing Morgan Rogers at the start of the summer. Xabi Alonso and the club’s recruitment team had the England international as a priority target but a deal seemed unlikely. Chelsea had endured a disappointing season, missing out on European football after finishing 10th, and their expectation was that Rogers would leave Aston Villa for Arsenal.

It was towards the end of the World Cup that Chelsea were made aware of a window of opportunity. Although Arsenal could claim to be London’s top dogs after winning the Premier League they dithered in talks with Villa, raising the prospect of another club stepping in.

Mikel Arteta talked about being bold in the market after Arsenal’s defeat by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final. Arteta wanted more in attack. A new option on the left was a priority; Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli were up for sale and everything pointed towards Arsenal making their move for Rogers at the end of June.

Yet the lines became blurred. Arsenal had a fee of £80m in mind, while Villa wanted more, particularly after Nottingham Forest sold Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for £116m. Time dragged on. How serious were Arsenal? There was also interest in Julián Alvarez, Vinícius Júnior and Bradley Barcola. Villa waited and the price for Rogers went up. Arsenal, beaten to the punch in the end, will have a look at what they could have won when Chelsea and Rogers visit the Emirates Stadium on Sunday.

Chelsea were decisive. They were tracking Rogers before he left Middlesbrough for Villa in February 2024. Joe Shields, one of Chelsea’s five sporting directors, worked with Rogers at Manchester City’s academy. The signing was not done on a whim. Chelsea have a good relationship with Villa’s owners and moved quickly after opening club-to-club talks a day after Rogers played in England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina. The fee was £117m and Chelsea did not struggle to convince Rogers. Alonso wooed him and the deal was confirmed five days after negotiations began.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has put a lot of smiles back on faces at Chelsea after last season’s player rebellions. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Crystal Pix/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

There was no last-ditch move from Arsenal. They signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m two days later and focused on other targets. When the window closed, though, Arteta’s options on the left looked a little light. Martinelli and Trossard left but only Tzolis arrived. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are alternatives. It is hard not to feel that Arsenal could have done with Rogers, even though Chelsea have paid a high price for him.

It remains to be seen whether the 24-year-old can prove he merits becoming the third-most expensive player in English football history. For context, the fee is the consequence of the market threatening to rise out of control and the money spent on many players starting to feel meaningless. It is worth pointing out, too, that money flowed back and forth between Chelsea and Villa all summer. Even so the price will follow Rogers around, so it is just as well he has made an excellent start.

Rogers has been involved in four of Chelsea’s seven goals in their first two league games. He scored in the 3-2 win at Fulham and later combined with João Pedro to set up Cole Palmer’s goal. He created Pedro Neto’s goal in last weekend’s 4-3 win over Brighton and played a key role when Jorrel Hato played in João Pedro to score.

Chelsea have thrilled in attack so far, João Pedro, Rogers and Palmer combining to devastating effect. Alonso, an adaptable manager, wants more control but his transitional football has been a delight. Chelsea were mannered and controlled during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge. It is felt that Alonso has recognised the Premier League’s shift towards power and athleticism. Rogers fits into the Spaniard’s system. Thomas Tuchel loves Rogers for his connectivity and pressing. It is significant that England’s energy levels rose in their quarter-final against Norway after the introduction of Rogers and Djed Spence late in the second half.

Chelsea needed more strength, more speed. Rogers, able to play anywhere in attacking midfield or as a No 8, looks a better fit in Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 than Enzo Fernández, sold this week to Manchester City for £125m. He has played with Palmer as one of the No 10s but has a responsibility to drift left, a role that is unlikely to have suited Fernández. Arsenal’s impeccable defence will be tested by Chelsea’s front three.

The Rogers-Palmer partnership has clicked. They are old friends and banter over the “ice cold” celebration. Rogers is a bubbly character and can get on with anyone. Chelsea are keen to improve the culture in the dressing room. It is felt that Alonso has shifted the mood after last year’s rebellions. The squad are united. It is one of the reasons why Chelsea decided to sell Fernández on deadline day. They did not need the headache of reintegrating the Argentinian.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, pictured celebrating Chelsea’s fourth goal against Brighton, have forged a promising relationship. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

This is a fresh start. The signing of Rogers, who was the Professional Footballers’ Association’s young player of the year in 2025, was a sign of Chelsea’s intent. Rogers was one of the best players in the Premier League last season. He grew under Unai Emery and scored when Villa beat Freiburg in the Europa League final in May.

It was one of Rogers’ less eye-catching goals: a clever jab at the near post from a low cross. There was a period last season when he could not stop scoring from long range but Rogers has spoken about wanting scruffier goals and he arrived at the far post to open his Chelsea account against Fulham.

Rogers is embracing the challenge. At Arsenal he would have been slotting into the finished article. Arsenal have reached the summit. Chelsea are beginning their climb under Alonso. Rogers, who has played in the Championship and had a loan in League One, rather liked the idea of starting lower down.

Sports.title: Moyes reveals he has never spoken to Everton owner but is defiant after transfer blows
Sports.content:
David Moyes has not spoken to the Everton owner and chair, Dan Friedkin, in the 20 months since he returned to the club as manager. Moyes also issued a defiant response on Friday to Everton’s calamitous end to the transfer window, claiming it could galvanise players and fans to achieve “something special” this season.

Moyes exposed an astonishing disconnect at the club when confirming he has had no contact with Friedkin, founder and chief executive of The Friedkin Group, since replacing Sean Dyche as manager in January 2025. TFG president, Marc Watts, is Everton’s executive chair and Rishi Majithia, Friedkin’s son-in-law, is the owner’s day-to-day representative at the club. But with TFG’s ambition for Everton under scrutiny after the transfer window, and amid claims they are looking for fresh investment or even to sell the club, Moyes’s revelation raises further questions over the company’s commitment.

The Everton manager admitted any successful club “needs to be aligned” at the top and added: “We’ve got new owners in who are still feeling their way in the club. I think if we get to know each other more it will get better.” Moyes, whose main point of contact at Everton is the chief executive, Angus Kinnear, was later asked whether he had ever had a conversation with Dan Friedkin. “Er, no,” he replied. So you’ve never met him? “No,” said Moyes.

It was TFG’s decision to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest last weekend that started Everton’s dreadful end to the transfer window. They U-turned after a backlash from Evertonians over the deal but Moyes was ultimately left with a weaker squad after the sales of Iliman Ndiaye, Beto, Tim Iroegbunam and Nathan Patterson.

“We don’t have a huge squad but sometimes you need to do something special in football and we will attempt to do something special,” Moyes said. “It’s not going to be easy. You know what happens in these situations, there’s only one person who tends to get called out at the end [the manager].

“But Everton’s different. I wouldn’t have come back for anybody but Everton. People saw the face of Evertonians last week and it can be really powerful. I would expect them to be really powerful now. Powerful for the team, powerful for the players. We’re going to need extra from them because we’re short. We need them. If they’re not with us, then it’s terrible.

“But they are with us. I believe they are with us. I love Everton and always have done. It’s reinvigorated me being back and now there’s a little bump in the road. I need to get over the bump quickly and start looking at how I can make it go smoothly.”

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest’s Liam Delap: ‘I play at my best on the edge of being horrible’
Sports.content:
“You can imagine it: he’s a centre-back, I’m a striker,” says Liam Delap, Nottingham Forest’s £45m club-record signing, smiling as he sets the scene. He is reliving taking on his younger brother, Finn, in the garden. These days, they are each other’s biggest supporters – Liam attended Finn’s victory for third-tier Burton on Wednesday – but as kids there was a friendly rivalry. The elder brother says: “There were probably a lot of tears, a lot of fights … whether it was playing Monopoly or football, it always ended in either the table being flipped or kicking the shit out of each other.”

It is a competitive streak that has stuck and Delap is determined to make his presence felt at Forest, for whom he could make his full debut against Tottenham on Saturday. It has been a testing 16 months; he left Chelsea a season into a six-year contract and after one goal in 28 top-flight appearances, a dozen of those starts. “It is never a linear path straight to the top,” Delap says, his right hand taking flight in the City Ground boardroom, the 1979 and 1980 European Cups shimmering behind him. “I just want to get my head down, focus and keep improving because I’m still so young and I have so much to learn. I even at times probably think I’ve been in football a lot longer than I have. I’ve still, hopefully, got a long career ahead.

“I think you just have to accept that sometimes things go bad, things happen … it might [prove to] be a good thing, I think. My first loans to Stoke and Preston [from Manchester City, across 2022-23] didn’t really go well at all and it was probably one of the best things that happened because I learnt so much from that season and went to Hull [for 2023-24] and kicked on from there. I’m still young, I’ve still got a lot of learning to do. Sometimes injuries happen, sometimes you don’t play. I don’t think anything is lost … Everyone has rocky moments. I’ve just got to use them to learn and kick on.”

Last summer, Delap was hot property. Oliver Glasner tells a story of Delap having proposals from 18 Premier League clubs and jests that the 23-year-old knows every top-flight manager owing to the various Zoom calls he held while deciding his next move. After all, one of those was with Glasner, then at Crystal Palace. Forest wanted him then, too. “It was a tough decision,” recalls Delap. “I remember the conversation we had, I was really impressed and I thought: ‘This guy [Glasner] is really good.’ He spoke incredibly well and you can see he has done really well with the strikers he has had in the past. That definitely stuck in my mind.”

Glasner wants Delap to play to his strengths: physicality, power and finishing. He doesn’t mean the forward’s hidden talent: cube roots. At the start of the year a clip of Delap showing off his maths skills went viral. “I didn’t enjoy maths one bit but I was always quite good at it. One of my friends taught me in school how to do it and I didn’t forget it. I hated school, [the] work, but I was always quite intelligent.”

The Austrian head coach said it was apparent in conversations with Delap this summer that the player had learnt lessons from a trying year: “I think it shows his attitude and his character that he said: ‘Yeah, I want a team and a club that values my strengths and wants to play to my strengths.’ Because I never want to change a player: it doesn’t make sense to say: ‘OK, now you should play like Messi: false nine, drop into midfield and combine play with one or two touches.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap scored once in 28 league appearances for Chelsea. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

A tally of 12 goals in the Ipswich side relegated in 2024-25 triggered widespread interest. At that point Delap was talked up as a potential heir to Harry Kane as England’s No 9. He has been capped by his country at every age group and was in the same under-16s team as Jude Bellingham. “As a little kid, all you want to do is play for your country,” Delap says. “So, of course, in my mind that’s where I want to get to. But it’s not as easy as that. I have to work hard and improve and that’s all I can do.”

An imposing 6ft 2in striker, Delap has long been viewed as the next big thing. He spearheaded Manchester City to FA Youth Cup victory over Chelsea in 2020, a couple of months after Pep Guardiola handed him his senior City debut aged 17. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, now teammates at Chelsea, were part of that same under-18s side, together with the new Aston Villa defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis and James McAtee, one of his best friends and now a clubmate again.

“He was a No 10 and quite often he would give me the ball and we just had that really good relationship off the pitch and it translated on to the pitch,” Delap says of McAtee. “If we didn’t win, we’d all be fuming. It probably instilled that winning mentality into us early. I think it’s worked because you can see from that team that almost everyone is playing somewhere in the Premier League, abroad, the Championship and that is probably because we pushed each other so much.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Delap made his Forest debut as a substitute at Anfield last weekend, his first notable action a quick throw-in that led to the penalty scored by Morgan Gibbs-White to earn a second-half lead. Only after the 2-2 draw did Glasner discover that Delap’s father, Rory, who played for Southampton and Stoke among others, knew a thing or two about throws. “I said: your father will be proud of you,” says Forest’s head coach. So, has Liam got a mammoth throw in his armoury? “No, I don’t think so,” he replies. “I would never, anyway: I’m a striker, I need to be in the box.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap was much in demand after impressing with a 12-goal league season at Ipswich. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images

Delap relishes the blood and thunder of battle. Glasner loves how Forest’s marquee signing stands up to centre-backs, making the point that defenders are hardly “hugging and kissing you all the time” in the heat of duels. But Delap, who spent a decade at Derby before joining City, says he has learned to harness his aggression on the field, after periods of getting into trouble when he was a youngster.

“You have to be careful, but not shy away from who you are,” he says. “I’m always going to fight for everything, always be aggressive, determined. It goes back to the point about my brother, being little kids in the garden, going at each other: that’s me. Sometimes you need to control it and sometimes you need to be careful, but I think I play at my best when I’m on that edge of being … being horrible.”

Sports.title: Chaotic Crystal Palace transfer window leaves Pierre Sage to run the gamut of emotions
Sports.content:
At least Pierre Sage did his research before joining Crystal Palace in June. Having stepped into Oliver Glasner’s shoes after the most successful era in the club’s history, it has not been the easiest transition for the engaging Frenchman following defeats against Everton and Manchester City to start the new campaign, and amid uncertainty surrounding the futures of some of the Conference League winners’ key players.

Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta ended up staying at Selhurst Park despite interest from Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively, while Palace brought in four new players after missing out to Sunderland for Malick Fofana in one of deadline day’s most dramatic storylines. But Sage is sanguine about experiencing a typically chaotic first transfer window in south London, and relieved to be able to concentrate on events on the pitch before Saturday’s trip to Fulham.

“I knew that and I had to deal and adapt to that,” Sage said when asked about Palace’s reputation for doing late deals, a trend that has led to them signing 10 players on the final day in the past three summer windows. “But at the end the most important thing is to have the player or the profile we choose and that’s the case. I think we are in line with what we need.”

Glasner, who has been joined at Nottingham Forest from Palace by Daniel Muñoz, made no secret of his dissatisfaction at having to wait until deadline day to bring in players after Palace signed four in his first summer at the club in 2024. It’s not Sage’s style to make a similar fuss, even if he is understood to have expressed frustration over their efforts to recruit a top-class replacement for Maxence Lacroix when the France defender was sold to Chelsea in July.

His favoured target was Ismaëlo Ganiou from Lens, the 21-year-old a key competent in the team that won the Coupe de France and finished second in Ligue 1 under Sage last season. However, Lens were reluctant to sell one of their prized assets and Ganiou signed a new deal at the start of August, forcing Palace to explore other targets.

A deal for Joel Ordóñez of Club Brugge broke down as the Ecuador defender is still recovering from a broken foot, while attempts to sign Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima and Raphaël Le Guen of Brest also came to nothing. The arrival of Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor on loan will help plug the gap, yet there remain major doubts over whether Lacroix’s leadership at the back has been fully replaced.

View image in fullscreen One that got away: Malick Fofana chose Sunderland over Palace on deadline day. Photograph: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images

Having failed to lure Mamadou Sangaré from Lens, with the Mali midfielder opting to join Brentford instead, Sage was the driving force in Palace’s attempt to bring in Fofana from another of his former clubs, Lyon. That ultimately proved futile despite a series of phone calls to the Belgium forward on deadline day. “I’m really proud and happy with what the club did for that,” Sage insisted. “We fight a lot and sometimes you cannot give more than this, but we give our best in this situation. At the end, the player chooses.” It remains to be seen whether the signing of the Chile forward Dario Osorio from the Danish club Midtjylland on an initial loan with an obligation to buy next summer for £26m makes up for the disappointment given he plays mainly on the right flank.

Palace are well stocked in attacking areas having also signed Dwight McNeil and Evann Guessand – who has been left out of the squad for the Europa League – and kept hold of Sarr. The return of Ben Chilwell and late addition of Quinten Timber to midfield will add depth and are believed to have gone some way to satisfying Sage, not to mention Palace’s rejection of bids from unnamed sides for Adam Wharton. Manchester City and Chelsea were believed to be among those who showed an interest. “The club was strong with the situation, and I think the player is completely in line with that,” he said.

But after breaking their transfer record twice in January, for Jørgen Strand Larsen and Brennan Johnson – who was swapped for McNeil, with Everton – Palace’s summer net spend of almost £40m in profit was the second lowest in the division behind Aston Villa. Over the past five seasons, Hull and Coventry have both invested more than Palace’s £90m despite being in the Championship.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sage was quick to reject suggestions he is unhappy with Palace’s summer signings and instead drew on his experiences from watching his parents run their brasserie in Belley, a town in the Ain region of eastern France. “I’m not frustrated – we are not a bank,” he said. “We do with what we have. My parents had a restaurant and I prefer every day there’s a lot of clients but it was not the case sometimes and we have to deal with that every day. In football it’s the same.”

View image in fullscreen Pierre Sage said of Palace’s transfer window: ‘I’m not frustrated, we’re not a bank.’ Photograph: Malcolm Fell/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

The absences of Sarr and Mateta, the latter of which had his hopes of leaving scuppered by a hamstring injury that will keep him out for another three weeks, will not help Palace’s chances against Fulham. Sage expects Sarr back from a groin injury for the game against Ipswich next Saturday but said the Senegal forward “needs time” after being affected by Liverpool’s interest, which led to his agent releasing a statement criticising the player’s treatment.

It will not have escaped Sage’s attention that Glasner won three times at Craven Cottage in 2025, including a quarter-final victory on the way to winning the FA Cup. After the week he has had, more of the same would do against another team who have yet to get off the mark in the league this season.

Sports.title: WSL transfer talking points: three things we learned from the data
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League’s summer transfer window has closed before the start of the 2026-27 season. The finances involved are microscopic compared with the £3.4bn that Premier League clubs spent on new players but the data provides three key points of interest: which club has made the biggest improvement to their squad, who is banking on stability, and how the women’s game has outsmarted its male equivalent.

Arsenal have the most improved squad

Many transfers in women’s football occur without the fee being disclosed, which deprives us of the conventional shorthand for assessing player quality. Thankfully there is Soccerdonna, the arm of Transfermarkt that covers women’s football. It carries estimated market values of players in euros. Using these, we can see by how much clubs have improved their squads.

Arsenal’s new additions have a combined value of €3.9m, slightly more than the €3.5m of talent that London City Lionesses have gained this summer. The entire squads of eight of the 14 teams in the 2026-27 WSL are worth less than these figures, which highlights the impact the new players should have. Indeed, London City’s new two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas is valued at €1.15m, which is more than the entire Charlton squad and not far behind the roster at Crystal Palace.

West Ham could argue they have added the most to their squad as the combined market value of their new players (€1.02m) is more than the corresponding amount for the players who remain from last season (€0.96m). Having finished 10th after winning only three of their opening 19 matches, improvements were clearly required.

Clubs have kept more settled squads

While supporters are most excited by new signings, departees are just as relevant to the health of a squad. Or at least they are if they made significant contributions in the previous season.

West Ham had to make additions as they lost players that contributed 6,322 minutes in the 2025-26 WSL, 29% of their total. Chief among those leaving was the goalkeeper Kinga Szemik, who started 19 of 22 games. Only Martina Fernández (1,950 minutes for Everton) and Keira Flannery (1,891 at Charlton) left current WSL clubs and played more minutes last season.

Teams may have learned from 12 months ago. Brighton lost 9,584 minutes of playing time from their 2024-25 squad in the summer 2025 window and went on to finish two places lower last season. Liverpool also said goodbye to a higher share of their playing time than anyone has in this transfer window (6,406 minutes), and started the campaign very slowly.

Output could be a greater issue than time played. Manchester City and Aston Villa have both lost players who contributed at least 13 combined goals and assists last season in Kerolin and Kirsty Hanson respectively. The difference between these clubs is that the champions can absorb the cost of that exit far more easily. The 17 goal contributions Villa have lost from last season through players leaving constitute 36.2% of their total, the highest proportion of the teams who were in the WSL in 2025-26.

The WSL is far better prepared for transfer windows than the Premier League

The Premier League endured a ridiculous deadline day on Tuesday. Around a sixth of players signed by clubs in the latest transfer window completed their deals on 1 September. Just over a third of the money that went on transfer fees this summer was spent after the 2026-27 season had already begun.

Things have been rather more organised in the WSL. Granted, its window closed before the new campaign gets under way and they didn’t have a World Cup clogging up the summer this year. But where the Premier League had completed only 83% of eventual total signings when deadline day began, the WSL made that proportion four weeks ago.

The obvious explanation would be that lower-finance deals are easier to complete. Yet Fifa recently revealed global spending on transfer fees in women’s football had increased by 83.6% year-on-year. Spending on agents fees by WSL clubs grew by 75% in the year up to 3 February 2026 too. The transfer business remains efficient even while the sums involved are rapidly increasing.

Men’s football will always have much more money but it could benefit from the transfer expertise and planning in the women’s game.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho handed first defeat of second Real Madrid spell by ex-Tottenham player he gave debut to
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho handed first defeat of second Real Madrid spell by ex-Tottenham player he gave debut to

Troy Parrott came back to haunt Jose Mourinho seven years after the Portuguese manager gave the striker his Premier League debut.

In 2019, Parrott was introduced for his top-flight Tottenham Hotspur bow during a 5-0 win over Burnley.

4 Parrott has enjoyed a brilliant last year or so Credit: Getty

At the time, he was 17, and Mourinho, after the game, gave him the match ball and hugged the forward.

But he came back to haunt Mourinho on Friday evening as Betis shocked Los Blancos.

Parrott came off the bench to score in the 81st minute as Betis beat Real Madrid at home.

The 24-year-old is a recent arrival from AZ Alkmaar, and this was his first goal for his new club.

He had only been on the pitch for four minutes, and the goal came from a corner.

The ball was swung into the box, and the initial header was saved by Thibaut Courtois, but there was Parrott to tap home.

Real Madrid had a late equaliser ruled out, and Kylian Mbappe missed a penalty, but it was the man who Mourinho saw some talent in all those years ago who scored the winner.

Parrott haunts Mourinho

Despite giving him his Premier League debut, Mourinho was soon demanding more from Parrott.

Speaking in 2020 about Parrott playing in the Under-21s, he said: “I was so happy with the way he performed, and I’m not speaking about his goal. I told him before the game: ‘Every time you play with the kids of your age, you have to show your colleagues why you are the privileged one.’

4 Parrott was handed his senior Spurs debut by Mourinho Credit: AFP

"Because it was something he was not doing. Every time he was playing with the kids, he was playing with the mentality of, ‘I shouldn’t be here’ or, ‘I am too good to be here.’

“I had exactly the same words with Scott McTominay. He was not loved in his age group because he was not there with the right frame of mind. The moment we started changing that lots of things started changing for him.

“Troy cannot go there [the under‑age teams] with discontent, contempt. It is a process. So everything goes very, very well.

"But this is a world where lots of people don’t even know if Troy has long hair or short hair, or is blond or is dark.

"They don’t even know that, and they speak about Troy, Troy, Troy. There was a guy behind me on the bench the other day: ‘Play Troy, play Troy.’ I don’t think he knows Troy.”

In the end, they both departed the club, with Parrott thriving in the Netherlands after some unsuccessful loan spells in the UK.

4 Parrott is off the mark for Betis Credit: Getty

Mourinho reacts to Real Madrid defeat

After the game, Mourinho couldn't believe that his side didn't win.

He said: "We did a great job tonight. We were very good, unbelievable offensive work, so many chances created, the CBs were imperious. We did a great job.

"Sometimes you lose, and you don't even know why. There's no explanation.

"Tonight was all Madrid. We shouldn't even be happy with a draw tonight; this should've been a win.

"We were completely dominant. So many shots on target, so many chances created; it's a shame.

"I don't know why we lost tonight. I genuinely don't. We played so well, so well.

"The players' attitude was fantastic, and we did everything to win. Congrats to Betis; they won the lottery."

4 Mourinho has suffered his first defeat as Real Madrid boss in his second tenure Credit: Getty

The statistics show that Real Madrid racked up an xG of 3.16 with eight shots on target.

Alvaro Valles enjoyed a stunning game, including a penalty save very late on.

However, it was controversial as there was a Betis player encroaching in the area.

Before that, Carlos Espí had a goal chalked off; Barcelona now have the chance to go three points clear at the top of the table when they play Valencia on Sunday.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak tipped to rival Erling Haaland for Golden Boot but MOTM handed to shock Liverpool teammate
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak tipped to rival Erling Haaland for Golden Boot but MOTM handed to shock Liverpool teammate

Alexander Isak was handed the Premier League player of the match award for his two-goal showing in Liverpool's win at Ipswich Town.

But talkSPORT's Dean Ashton went against the grain and snubbed the Swede in favour of his Reds teammate, who he instead believed deserved the honour.



4 Isak has now scored three goals in the Premier League this season Credit: Getty

Isak scored twice inside nine minutes to help Andoni Iraola register his first win as Liverpool head coach.

The British record £125million signing had bagged a hat-trick on his last visit to Portman Road with Newcastle.

'Looks like the Isak who was at Newcastle'

Speaking on talkSPORT's live commentary from the game, Ashton said: "I've been watching Alexander Isak…



"Last season, you could tell he was just never fit, and he was never sharp.

"He didn't look fresh at all, but he looks like the Isak who was at Newcastle.



"He looks really sharp in the way that he plays, and the runs he's making are so clever for this level because he runs towards the defender before he makes his own run.

"From a defender's point of view, it looks like you've got him, but he's running at you, but he is running off you.



"Then, he just takes that little step, and that is what happened for the first goal.

"He ran towards [Jacob] Greaves, so he thought he had him, but he then just dipped away to give him that yard, and it is just such clever movement that gets you thinking as a defender.

"If he can continue in this way, and he looks as fresh and fit, then Liverpool have got the striker they thought."

4 Isak has now already equalled his Premier League goal tally from last season in just three games



Isak for Golden Boot?

Since the 2022-23 season, only Erling Haaland (19) has more Premier League goals against newly promoted clubs than Isak (18).

The Norwegian clinched the Golden Boot award again after a 27-goal campaign last season for the third time in four years.

The only year in which he failed to top the Premier League goal standings was his third-placed finish in the 2024-25 season, in which Isak finished above him in his last year at Newcastle.

The latter's teething issues in his first 12 months at Anfield eliminated any chance of a Golden Boot battle last season, but Ashton was asked whether it'll be a different story this time around.



"Well, we know when he's at his best, he can [challenge Haaland for the Golden Boot], Ashton added to talkSPORT.

4 Isak netted a double inside the first nine minutes Credit: Getty

"We know what a fantastic striker he can be, and he's fit. You can tell he's fit, even though he's taken off slightly earlier.

"So maybe there's more. Maybe there's more to come from Isak, but he's a deadly finisher when he's at his best.



"If you get him the ball in the right areas, which Liverpool have already this season For the start of this season, then he'll get you goals. So I think that's a real positive."

But not Man of the Match?

Ashton said: "It's not Isak because [Kjell] Scherpen threw the first one in. Yes, the second one was good, but he left after 63 minutes or whatever it was.

"I'm going to give it to Ronald Araujo because he's come in; he's taken Jeremie Frimpong's place, they've changed something in the set-up of the backline, and he's given that role in that area.

4 Araujo was named Ashton's player of the match on his first Premier League start Credit: Getty



"That's a problem area, freeing up [Dominik] Szoboszlai.

"I thought he was excellent, and actually he looks so suited to the Premier League - so physical, brilliant in the air, really aggressive in his defensive work, good on the ball.

"I was really impressed with how he came in and adapted Liverpool's backline."

Sports.title: Matteo Guendouzi and Mason Greenwood banned and fined five-figure fees after mass brawl
Sports.content:
Matteo Guendouzi and Mason Greenwood banned and fined five-figure fees after mass brawl

Matteo Guendouzi and Mason Greenwood have both been hit with UEFA punishments following the chaotic scenes that marred Fenerbahce's win over Lyon.

The pair's Turkish side booked their place in the league phase of the Champions League after a 2-1 victory against Lyon 2-1 last month.

3 Greenwood and Guendouzi were both disciplined for their antics Credit: Getty

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Guendouzi - who also used to play for Marseille - later sparked chaotic scenes as he celebrated by baiting the fans of his former Ligue 1 rivals.

talkSPORT's Simon Jordan argued that the Frenchman must feel the weight of the football laws for his 'antagonistic' behaviour.

And now UEFA have confirmed that both Guendouzi and fellow Marseille alum Greenwood have both been hit with punishments.

Guendouzi and Greenwood banned after brawl

UEFA have announced that Guendouzi has received a four-match European ban - with two of those games suspended.

Additionally, the 27-year-old has been fined 50,000 euros (£43,000).

UEFA revealed that he was punished for 'insulting others present at the match, provoking spectators and for violating the basic rules of decent conduct'.

Meanwhile, Greenwood - who only arrived at Fenerbahce from Marseille this summer - was penalised for 'violating the basic rules of decent conduct'.

The 24-year-old Englishman was handed a one-match suspended ban which, like Guendouzi's, is subject to a probationary period of one year', and he was also fined 30,000 euros (£26,000).

Furthermore, both Fenerbahce and Lyon were fined 50,000 euros for their respective teams 'violating the general and basic rules of conduct'.

3 Lyon's Tolisso wasn't having any of Guendouzi's antics Credit: Getty

3 The midfielder was all too happy to wind up Lyon's fans Credit: Getty

Why did Guendouzi taunt Lyon fans?

Guendouzi, who played for Marseille between 2021 and 2024, claimed Lyon fans were taunting him with 'insults' about his family.

"If we can't celebrate the way we want afterward, I find that disappointing," he added.

"When you have 60,000 people insulting your family, your mother, your children, even before the game and no-one on the referee's side tells the crowd to be quiet.

"I know that in France, when this kind of thing happens, there comes a point where they'll talk to the fans to stop and maybe stop the match."

Guendouzi will now miss Fenerbahce's opening two Champions League league phase fixtures against Roma and Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Ex-Man United man now playing in seventh tier has second career nothing to do with football
Sports.content:
Ex-Man United man now playing in seventh tier has second career nothing to do with football

Joe Riley once played in the same Manchester United team as Marcus Rashford; now he works in a different world altogether.

The 29-year-old is still playing football — he's made over 200 career appearances — but he also has another career.



2 Riley played a total of 134 first-team minutes for Man United Credit: Getty

Juggling two jobs

In an interview with BBC Sport, Riley revealed how he retrained as a financial protection advisor, which he now does alongside turning out for non-League side Warrington Rylands.

Born in Blackpool, Riley joined Man United as a teenager.

He went on to make two first-team appearances under Louis van Gaal.

Having debuted in a February 2016 FA Cup tie against Shrewsbury, he made his one and only start for United later that month in a Europa League clash against Midtjylland.

Notably, that was the game in which Rashford, who has just been reintroduced to the United fold, made his senior debut.



The likes of current United boss Michael Carrick and Juan Mata were also in the starting line-up that night.

Reflecting on his time at Old Trafford, Riley said: "Of course I would have liked to have played more games for United, but things didn't work out like that.



"I don't dwell on the past — I'm just happy that it happened. I've now got my foot in the door for the next chapter of my life.

"I'm progressing with another career that's setting me up for the rest of my life."



Life after United

After a brief loan spell with Sheffield United that was cut short by a dislocated shoulder he sustained in a 'freak' training accident, Riley left Man United permanently in 2018.

He subsequently played for Bradford City, Carlisle United and Walsall in the EFL.

2 Riley's most recent EFL club was Walsall Credit: Getty

Since leaving Walsall in 2024, he's had stints with non-League AFC Fylde, Tamworth and, now, Warrington Rylands.



Riley captains the side that finished fourth in the Northern Premier League Premier Division, the seventh tier of English football, last season.

And he admits he's enjoying life away from the professional game after recovering from a chronic foot problem.

"Moving from full-time football to part-time was something I once feared, like many players do," he explained.

"Instead, my job is rewarding, while I joined Warrington Rylands in the summer — a club I thoroughly enjoy being at."



Worlds apart

While Riley gears up for an FA Cup first qualifying round clash against Hyde United on Saturday, his old club are preparing for Sunday's Premier League trip to Everton.

Man United got their season up and running in style last time out, bouncing back from their shock defeat to Hull by thumping Ipswich 5-2.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez changes Chelsea shirt number after just one game despite phone call with legend
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez changes Chelsea shirt number after just one game despite phone call with legend

Emiliano Martinez has changed his Chelsea shirt number already despite getting John Terry's approval to wear the number 26.

The Argentine completed a late transfer to Stamford Bridge from Aston Villa and claimed Terry's iconic number, which he wore on his debut against Brighton last Sunday.



4 Martinez donned the iconic Chelsea number for his debut against Brighton Credit: Getty

Now, with Robert Sanchez gone, the number one is free, and he's grabbed it.

However, the Blues aren't offering to change any shirts already bought.

But Martinez is offering to personally sign any of them in a warm gesture from the Argentine number one.



Emi Martinez changes Chelsea shirt number

In a statement on the club's website, Chelsea said: "Emiliano Martinez has switched to the No.1 shirt for Chelsea.

"Our summer signing originally took the No.26 shirt for the Blues and wore it in our 4-3 victory over Brighton & Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge.



"However, due to Robert Sanchez’s loan move to Como, the No.1 shirt has since become vacant, and our Argentinian international has opted to take that number.

"In recognition of the change, and those impacted, Emi has kindly offered to sign all “Martinez 26” shirts that had been obtained via the official Club Megastore or official Club website.



"In order to arrange this, supporters will be required to bring this shirt to Stamford Bridge along with proof of purchase by October 4.

"The 2026/27 Nike home shirt is now on sale to fans with early access via our Megastore at Stamford Bridge and our online store."

4 Martinez has made a unique gesture to Chelsea fans after changing to the No.1 Credit: Getty

John Terry's approval

Martinez has joined the Blues from Villa in a £7.5million deal after a very successful spell in the Midlands.



He was part of the team that won the Europa League last year and also represented the Villans in the Champions League.

But after another poor display from Sanchez in the 3-2 win over Fulham, Chelsea decided that it was time for a new goalkeeper.

Martinez is in and made several saves as the Blues scraped past Brighton at the weekend 4-3.

And during his unveiling, the 34-year-old said he and Terry had a conversation in which the former Chelsea captain gave his blessing to wear the number 26.



4 Martinez offers an immediate upgrade on Sanchez Credit: Getty

4 The number 26 is synonymous with Terry

He said: "I remember using the 26 on loan a few times with previous clubs, and of course I knew John Terry famously had the 26 here.

"John was someone I spoke to before I joined, and he said he was over the moon to have me here.



"From our time together at Aston Villa, he knows how hard I work and what I can bring to Chelsea.

"The morning I signed, I texted him and said, 'I'm wearing your shirt, and I'm going to do it with pride'."

Martinez did wear it with pride for one game, and he has switched to the traditional number one for a first-choice goalkeeper.

He will hope to get one over former club Arsenal this weekend as the Blues head across London to the Emirates to take on the Gunners in an early-season belter.

Sports.title: Alexandre Pato has takeover deal ratified as EFL club hail ‘important milestone’
Sports.content:
Alexandre Pato is about to enter into the world of EFL football ownership, with the former striker set to become the majority shareholder of Northampton Town.

Pato is part of a consortium that has agreed a deal to buy a controlling stake in the League Two side.

3 Pato has tried to buy one other EFL club and now has his hands on Northampton Town Credit: Getty

The deal involves Pato and Sports Alpha Capital, and it has been passed by the Independent Football Regulator.

Alexandre Pato has takeover deal approved

In a statement, Northampton Town's chairman Kelvin Thomas said: “The successful completion of both the IFR and EFL processes represents an important milestone for the club and should provide supporters and stakeholders with further confidence in the proposed investment and the foundations being put in place for the club’s future.

“As one of the first football clubs to be considered under the new regulatory framework, the proposed investors have been required to successfully navigate both the EFL clearance and IFR approval processes.

“This has been a detailed and rigorous process, involving significant scrutiny of the proposed investment, the ownership structure, financial sustainability and the suitability and financial standing of those involved.

“The successful completion of both the IFR and EFL processes represents an important milestone for the club and should provide supporters and stakeholders with further confidence in the proposed investment and the foundations being put in place for the club’s future.

“We would like to thank both the EFL and the IFR for their professionalism, diligence and thoroughness throughout their respective processes.

“During this time, we have also enjoyed getting to know the investors and principals behind Sports Alpha Capital and are excited about what they can bring to Northampton Town.

“As supporters will see from their varied backgrounds, there is a genuine passion for football within the group.

“A number of the investors have already visited Northampton, spent time at the club and attended matches.

3 A consortium is set to purchase a majority stake in Northampton Credit: Reuters

“They will bring a strong blend of football, corporate and financial expertise to the club and with significant Brazilian representation within the group, we also hope they might bring a little Brazilian excitement and flair with them.

“Now the regulatory processes have been completed, we move towards completing the remaining documentation and finalising the investment.

“Full details regarding the investment, structure and the principal investors involved will be announced upon completion.

“We thank the fans for their patience, but it is reassuring that these in-depth processes are in place for football.”

The club stressed that the remaining documentation must now be completed before the investment is finalised.

Pato getting his hands on the Cobblers is a lesson in persistence.

3 Former Brazil striker Pato was part of the consortium during their talks to buy Colchester Credit: Getty

That is because his consortium had been initially set to buy Colchester United.

The former Chelsea and AC Milan striker even went and watched the U's in action, and talks were at an advanced stage.

But they were unable to come to an agreement, and Pato moved for the Cobblers instead.

At the time, they had just been relegated to League Two.

They haven't made a great start to the league, failing to win any of their first four.

That is made up of three draws and one defeat, with the club sitting 18th, and the one thing Pato won't want is for them to drop into the National League.

Sports.title: Harry Kane’s former Tottenham manager reveals how every EFL loan club got it wrong about Ballon d’Or favourite
Sports.content:
Harry Kane’s former Tottenham manager reveals how every EFL loan club got it wrong about Ballon d’Or favourite

Former Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood says none of the clubs Harry Kane went on loan to thought he'd become a superstar.

Sherwood handed Kane his first Premier League start back in 2014, having previously worked with him while coaching Spurs' Under-21 team.

3 Kane began to establish himself in the Spurs first team under Sherwood Credit: Getty

And it was following Sherwood's suggestion that the 33-year-old striker got his first loan spell away from Spurs, joining London neighbours Leyton Orient in 2011.

Stints with Millwall, Norwich and Leicester followed – but Kane's immense talent didn't seem to be picked up on, at that burgeoning stage of his career.

Kane's potential not spotted

Speaking to Hawksbee and Jacobs on talkSPORT, Sherwood said of Kane that 'every manager I loaned him to, not one of them said he'd be a player'.

The England skipper is now the frontrunner to win this year's Ballon d'Or after enjoying a career-best 51-goal season for Bayern Munich last term – picking up the European Golden Shoe as a result – and captaining his country to their best World Cup finish since 1966.

Backing Kane for the game's most prestigious individual accolade, Sherwood said: "If he can't win it this year, he's not going to win it, is he?

"He can't do any more than what he's done, and there's no one out there who's won the World Cup, for instance, who's had an outstanding club season either – so I think Harry should win it."

Michael Owen was the last English player to scoop the Ballon d'Or back in 2001, following Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979), Bobby Charlton (1966) and inaugural recipient Stanley Matthews (1956).

Those formative loan spells laid the foundations for Kane's journey to becoming arguably the best striker on the planet.

Sherwood says he'd 'probably be decent' at Under-21 level

And Sherwood stressed the importance of young players getting experience of 'real' football, explaining: "I'm a firm believer that after Under-18s, they shouldn't be at your club. They should be out playing competitive football.

"Because the ideal way to develop a player like [Manchester City's] Phil Foden is to keep him around; play 10 games; train with world-class players. But if they're not going to play the games, it's pointless playing Under-21 football. I could play in it now and probably be decent. It's like a chess match, the game.

3 Kane scored his first five career goals on loan with League One Leyton Orient in 2011 Credit: Getty

"It's not real football. Get them out playing competitive football."

Sherwood also discussed Will Lankshear, the 21-year-old striker who left Spurs on a permanent basis for Middlesbrough this summer.

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham told Spurs they'd made a big mistake in letting Lankshear leave.

But Sherwood acknowledged he would have had a lack of opportunities in North London.

Lankshear finds his groove

"He's got to get regular game time, which he wouldn't have done at Spurs," he continued.

"We probably are going to see a lot more of him, simply because he's playing week after week and getting a bit of rhythm, which he wouldn't have got at Tottenham.

3 Will Lankshear has made a blistering start to life at Middlesbrough, scoring five goals in six games in all competitions Credit: Getty

"But the trouble you're going to have with Will is he's always going to be judged against Championship opposition, and everyone will say, 'Well, he's not playing in the Premier League'.

"That's why a loan to your league is always the best option, but perhaps there was no one putting their hand up for him.

"Obviously, there wasn't, so he's done the best thing. He wasn't going to get an opportunity.

Sherwood then delivered a damning verdict on the Spurs players he believes are preventing youngsters from breaking into the first team.

Spurs spent more than £200m adding to their squad in the summer transfer window.

"Tottenham are signing all these players, and they're not all superstars, let me tell you," Sherwood added. "They might be superstar money, but they're not, and they're blocking up pathways for the academy kids.

"If I had a kid and I wanted to put him in any academy, it certainly wouldn't be Tottenham's at the moment."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher brutally tells Liverpool they should have let ‘cult hero’ go
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher brutally tells Liverpool they should have let ‘cult hero’ go

Jamie Carragher has insisted Liverpool should have released Wataru Endo, claiming he is 'never going to play' under Andoni Iraola.

The Japanese midfielder has been a fan favourite since his arrival at Anfield in 2023, but has struggled for minutes in recent years amid injuries and managerial preferences.

5 Wataru Endo is set to miss Liverpool's first eight European games after being left out of their Champions League league phase squad Credit: Getty

Endo made just 12 appearances in all competitions for Arne Slot last term, with an ongoing ankle issue hampering his progress.

This looks set to continue under new Reds boss Iraola, who is yet to use the 33-year-old off the bench after his first two games in charge.

Endo has now been handed a fresh blow in his Liverpool career, after he was left out of their 25-man squad for the Champions League league phase.

With UEFA squads requiring at least eight 'homegrown' players to be included, this left Iraola with some tough decisions to make.

As well as Endo, Federico Chiesa was another notable omission from the squad, who is yet to establish himself since his arrival in 2024.

He and Endo were overlooked in favour of Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike, all of whom are recovering from long-term injuries and are not expected back until later this year.

Also included was 21-year-old midfielder James McConnell, despite him making no first-team appearances since the 2024/25 season.

Carragher questions Liverpool move

With Endo and Chiesa both being overlooked for the start of Liverpool's European campaign, club legend Carragher admitted the move doesn't bode well for the pair in their Anfield careers.

Speaking on The Overlap, Carragher said : "Liverpool have got two players in the squad who are never going to play.

"And there are all these quotas, you can only have 17 (non-homegrown) players and all that.

5 Chiesa has played just 66 minutes in the Premier League this calendar year Credit: Getty

5 Andoni Iraola looks unlikely to use either Chiesa or Endo in his first season as Liverpool boss Credit: Getty

"They have got Chiesa and Endo. It's like they are never going to kick a ball."

Carragher was particularly sympathetic towards Endo, insisting a summer exit would have been in his best interests.

He added: "Endo should have been moved on. He has done great, a bit of a cult hero."

Endo's Liverpool career

Endo moved to Anfield in the summer of 2023 under Jurgen Klopp, and was a regular fixture in his first season at Anfield, quickly making himself a fan favourite for his solid displays.

The Japanese star made 44 appearances in all competitions - 34 of which were starts - scoring three goals and tasting League Cup glory.

But the arrival of Arne Slot in 2024 saw his role reduced, as Endo started just one of his 20 appearances in Liverpool's Premier League-winning 2025/26 campaign.

5 Endo tasted Carabao Cup glory in his first season at Liverpool Credit: Getty

5 Andoni Iraola looks unlikely to use either Endo this term, despite his cult hero status at Anfield Credit: Getty

Last season proved the utility player's most challenging year in Red, as injuries restricted him to just 12 outings altogether.
