Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:

Semi-final: Ukraine vs Sweden

Semi-final: Poland vs Albania

Final: Ukraine/Sweden vs Poland/Albania

Play-off Path C:

Semi-final: Turkey vs Romania

Semi-final: Slovakia vs Kosovo

Final: Slovakia/Kosovo vs Turkey/Romania

Play-off Path D:

Semi-final: Denmark vs North Macedonia

Semi-final: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland

Final: Czech Republic/Republic of Ireland vs Denmark/North Macedonia - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: Sugar Ray Leonard's 'violent' son was arrested for alleged possession of dangerous cocktail of drugs just weeks after trying to break into boxing icon's home
Sports.content:
Sugar Ray Leonard's 'violent' son was arrested for alleged possession of dangerous cocktail of drugs just weeks after trying to break into boxing icon's home

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The troubled 25-year-old son of boxing legend Sugar Ray Leonard was arrested with several dangerous illegal drugs earlier this summer, according to Santa Monica Police.

As first revealed by The California Post on Wednesday, an officer witnessed Daniel Leonard and another man 'walking with an inflated balloon and a large cylindrical container believed to be a nitrous oxide tank' in the early morning hours of July 7.

'As the officer approached, one man attempted to conceal the balloon behind him before dropping it to the ground,' the SMPD rep told the Post. 'The second man appeared to conceal the container at his side. Officers detained both men and confirmed the container was a nitrous oxide tank.'

The pair was arrested for possessing nitrous with the intent to inhale before Daniel was additionally charged with possession of methamphetamine and sedatives/benzodiazepines. In total, he was charged with four misdemeanors for possession of nitrous oxide, a substance containing nitrous oxide, MDMA, alprazolam and dextroamphetamine.

He is due back in court in LA County on October 12, according to the Post.

The Daily Mail has submitted a records request with the SMPD for further information. Daniel did not immediately respond to The Daily Mail's requests for comment on Wednesday night.

Daniel Leonard (left) is seen alongside his father, former Olympic gold medalist Ray Leonard

Daniel Ray Leonard is pictured with his dad Sugar Ray and mom Bernadette back in 2017

This marks the latest arrest for the son of Ray Leonard, a former five-division world champion and Olympic gold medalist, who served as America's most popular boxer in the immediate aftermath of Muhammad Ali's retirement.

In May, TMZ reported Daniel was arrested for violating a restraining order at the family's home, although that protective order was later dropped.

According to the Post, it was a 'violent' incident involving Daniel and Ray that led the father to file a protective order against his son.

The Post later produced Ray's restraining order request in which he describes his youngest son as an addict and thief, who steals 'every day.' In a handwritten declaration, Sugar Ray wrote: 'He has overdosed 4 times. They had to bring him back to life 2 times at the hospital!

'He has stolen extreme amounts of money valuable items! He [illegible] steals every day for years! My son Daniel Leonard has been a drug addict for 7 or 8 years at least. His behavior has gotten worse over the years!'

'I love my son but he has become a danger not only [to] himself but to his family! My wife is extremely afraid along with [my] daughter Camille!' Sugar Ray continued. 'His behavior has gotten worse every day. We haven't had a day of peace in 9 years which is the reality of his addiction! Scared for my family!'

More recently, Daniel (R) was pictured alongside the family - and Magic Johnson - last August

The Leonards live in a sprawling $46.5 million estate in the Pacific Palisades, California

Daniel is the youngest son of Sugar Ray Leonard and his second wife Bernadette Robi, and his third son overall.

Sugar Ray, now 70, had his first son - Ray Jr - with his first wife Juanita Wilkinson in 1973, before adding a daughter - Camille - with Bernadette.

In February of last year, Daniel's mother Bernadette posted a cryptic caption on Instagram alongside a photograph of Sugar Ray and Daniel - her husband and son.

A photo showed the pair standing together on a beach with Sugar Ray's arm around Daniel's shoulder, and the caption read: 'Happy Valentine's to my hearts!!! Love you both beyond and we will get through this faze (sic)!'

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley launches impassioned defence of Moses Itauma's trainer after heavy criticism over his crushing world title defeat by Filip Hrgovic
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley launches impassioned defence of Moses Itauma's trainer after heavy criticism over his crushing world title defeat by Filip Hrgovic

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Fabio Wardley has sprung to the defence of trainer Ben Davison against the barrage of criticism which followed his stablemate Moses Itauma's crushing world heavyweight title defeat on Saturday night.

Davison has been eviscerated for 21-year-old Itauma subsiding with exhaustion in the ninth round against Croatia's first world heavyweight champion Filip Hrgovic.

Davison may find himself fighting to keep Itauma on his roster at an imminent council of war with promoter Frank Warren

But Wardley - who is in training for the October 17 rematch of the slugfest in which Daniel Dubois took his WBO belt - says: ‘I just can’t believe so much hostility and so much stick being thrown at Ben. He’s been my trainer for seven years and he’s brought me through from my unusual background (white collar boxing) to winning a world title.

‘He doesn’t become a bad trainer because Moses had his first defeat against a really tough opponent.

‘Ben has shown there’s so much more to boxing at the higher levels than just my power to knock people out. Taught me so much. It wasn’t his fault I lost to Daniel. I beat myself,

Fabio Wardley (above) has sprung to the defence of trainer Ben Davison after 21-year-old Moses Itauma's crushing world heavyweight title defeat against Filip Hrgovic on Saturday

Davison (left) has been blasted for Itauma (right) subsiding with exhaustion in the ninth round

‘And Ben is now adding the nuances I never knew anything about so I can adapt for the rematch and win this time.’

Warren, however, says: ’Ben and I will have to have a chat. Was there a plan B for when Hrgovic simply refused to be knocked out through eight rounds of punishment?

‘Or did Moses not listen, like footballers who go out on the pitch and don’t do what the manager tells them?

‘Losing happens but they should have managed the fight when so many rounds ahead. Moses should have stayed behind his terrific jab and boxed his way to a decision. He was too obsessed with getting another knock out.

‘So he just kept his foot hard down on the accelerator from start to finish and punched himself out.

‘Of course at 21 Moses can come back to be a world champion but there’s work to be done.’

The unanswered question is whether Davison will be the man doing it.

Sports.title: Emotional Eddie Hearn reveals why he was in 'floods of tears' in build-up to Katie Taylor's retirement fight - and predicts event could be the biggest of ALL time
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn has admitted he was reduced to 'floods of tears' watching the promo video for Katie Taylor's retirement fight, before predicting her final ring walk at Croke Park could become 'one of the greatest moments sport has ever seen'.

Taylor will call time on her glittering career on Saturday night when she faces unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in front of an expected 80,000 fans in Dublin.

The 40-year-old will bid to become a three-time undisputed world champion in the 27th and final fight of her professional career, with the vacant WBC title also on the line alongside her WBO, WBA and IBF belts.

And Hearn, who has promoted Taylor throughout her professional career, is already struggling to contain his emotions ahead of the occasion.

'I've got my daughter with me, and we came through the airport, and it's like every other person knows about Saturday,' he said. 'Everyone knows about Saturday. It sounds like everyone's going. So I just can't wait. I just can't wait to feel it, and it'll be unbelievably emotional.

'I mean, that promo video… I'm not afraid to say it. When I say I cried, I am not exaggerating. This is a bit embarrassing but I bawled my eyes out. Not like, 'Oh, a tear came out', literally floods of tears.

Eddie Hearn (pictured above) has admitted he was reduced to 'floods of tears' watching the promo video for Katie Taylor's retirement fight

Taylor will call time on her glittering career on Saturday night when she faces unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili (pictured on the right) in front of an expected 80,000 fans in Dublin

The 40-year-old (pictured above) will bid to become a three-time undisputed world champion in the 27th and final fight of her professional career

'I can't stop thinking about the ring walk. I truly believe it will be one of the greatest moments sport has ever seen.

'Yes, it's going to be one of the biggest events Irish sport has ever seen, one of the biggest female boxing events ever seen, but honestly I think it could be the biggest sporting event of all time. It's going to be one of those events where everyone's going to go, 'Wow. I can't believe it's happening.'

For Hearn, the scale of the occasion is all the more remarkable given that he once doubted whether Taylor would ever get the chance to fight at Croke Park.

The Matchroom promoter admitted he is disappointed with himself for allowing those doubts to creep in, particularly after previous attempts to Taylor's dream location had failed to materialise.

'I'm disappointed in myself, actually, that I allowed that to happen, because maybe we could have done it earlier,' Hearn said. 'But I probably didn't have the confidence that I had going into it this time, with Peter, with the Serrano three-fight deal and all that.

'If Croke Park had originally gone, 'Yes, this is going to be massive,' I would have gone, 'Wow you're right' and we would have done it. But I was like, 'I don't know' and I was thinking blimey, if they're not sure, do we really want to be gambling with these costs?

'But, they listened, they helped out as well. They were fantastic in the end.

'Saying all of that though, I never thought we'd do 40,000 on a pre-sale. It's honestly blown my mind how passionate the fans are for Katie and how much they support her and show up for her.'

For Hearn, the scale of the occasion is all the more remarkable given that he once doubted whether Taylor would ever get the chance to fight at Croke Park

Taylor pictured inspiring the next generation during her open working in Dublin on Wednesday

The demand has left Hearn wondering just how many more fans could have packed into Ireland's national stadium.

'We're getting hundreds of messages every day from people saying, 'Please, I want to bring my daughter. It's heartbreaking in a way because we'd love for everyone to get a ticket and be there to watch it live but that's just the way it is.'

Hearn is delighted that DAZN will broadcast the fight, while also praising the decision to allow Irish broadcaster RTE to show the event.

'I'm so happy that DAZN are broadcasting the fight,' he said. 'But I think the RTE thing is incredible as well. I was shocked, but very grateful that DAZN allowed that to happen because I think it's very important for Ireland.'

And while her journey to the Olympics and gold medal at London 2012 remains the defining chapter of her amateur career, Hearn believes it is what Taylor has achieved as a professional that will shape her legacy for generations to come.

Taylor won Olympic gold before turning professional, but went on to conquer the sport at the highest level, headlining at Madison Square Garden, fighting on Netflix and beating virtually every major opponent put in front of her.

Hearn believes her battle with Chantelle Cameron, including the rematch in which she avenged the first defeat of her professional career, are particularly underappreciated.

'She won that gold medal, but I think when you look back on everything that she's done, from starting out fighting on the AJ cards to headlining MSG, fighting on Netflix, you know, and she's beaten everybody,' he said.

Taylor won Olympic gold before turning professional, but went on to conquer the sport at the highest level, headlining at Madison Square Garden and fighting on Netflix

She has beaten virtually every major opponent put in front of her - including Amanda Serrano

'By the way, when you look back, you see Chantelle Cameron beat Mikaela Mayer last Saturday. She's a strong, big, big, big girl. And Katie's rematch victory over Chantelle Cameron, I think, is so underrated, especially at the stage in her career that Katie was at.

'There are so many things. I think the Olympics will always be the Olympics, but there are a lot of people that don't remember the Olympics or weren't around in 2012. The younger generation now that are following Katie, I don't think they're necessarily reminiscing about the Olympics.

'These are girls that are eight, 10, 12, 16. They weren't even born when she won the Olympics. So I think what she's done in the pro ranks will be remembered forever. Honestly, it's just everything that she's done across the board. We are so lucky to have had a fighter like her.'

Hearn also believes Taylor has fundamentally transformed women's boxing.

'She changed women's boxing forever,' he said. 'Whether I did it or not, she was going to convince probably someone to do it, right?

'Now, whether they would have done it the same way as us, I doubt it. But this wasn't me going, 'I'm going to try and change women's boxing.' This was me going, 'I believe in you, and I want to come along for the journey.'

'So what led from there is the doors opening and watching…'

Hearn remembers just how different the landscape was when Taylor turned professional.

Serrano and Taylor fighting in their IBF, WBA, WBC, WBO, and Ring super lightweight title bout during Netflix's Katie Taylor vs Amanda Serrano 3 at Madison Square Garden on July 11, 2025

'When she turned pro, there were some weight classes in women's boxing that had four fighters at a professional level,' he said. 'You could fight for the world title in your second or third fight. And now it's really hard to win a world title. There are some brilliant fighters.'

Perhaps most tellingly, Hearn says Taylor has achieved something that goes beyond titles, records and money: she has earned the respect of virtually every fighter in the sport.

'There isn't one female fighter you could find that wouldn't go, 'She's incredible,' he said. 'She's just so loved. And there's no airs or graces. She's not there for the fame. She's not there for the money. It's just pure - purely a faith, the love of the sport, and trying to set an example.'

Yet amid all the emotion and celebration, Hearn knows Taylor cannot afford to lose sight of the woman standing opposite her on Saturday night.

Pili is unbeaten at 12-0 and, while she does not possess Taylor's experience or pedigree, she is younger, strong and willing to trade.

With Taylor fighting for her third undisputed crown and Pili seeking to pull off the biggest upset of her career, Hearn insists the retirement celebrations must wait.

'You know, today really the switch has got to focus on the fight because this girl's decent,' he said. 'She's big. She's 12-0.

'I'm not saying she's got the pedigree of Katie Taylor, but Katie's 40 years old, right? She's fighting a young, strong girl who likes to trade.

Pili (pictured above) is unbeaten at 12-0 and, while she does not possess Taylor's experience or pedigree, she is younger, strong and willing to trade

While Taylor's final fight will inevitably dominate the night, Hearn insists the rest of the card has been designed to make the occasion worthy of Croke Park

'And so does Katie.'

'She's IBO world champion, European champion, decent amateur, who, by the way, can become undisputed herself on Saturday,' Hearn said. 'So I think today there needs to be a little bit of a switch from this whole, 'Oh, euphoric, this is going to be amazing.'

'I just walked into her BBC interview there, and she was saying, 'I need to prepare myself for war here.' Because she can't walk out and get caught up in the emotion. She can't get in the ring and the start of the fight just passes you by.

'She's got to go in there, and prepare for it to be a war from the opening bell.

'And it will be an all-out war because it's the only way she knows how to fight. She's not going to try and box a moon because she'll want to leave it all in the ring.'

And while Taylor's final fight will inevitably dominate the night, Hearn insists the rest of the card has been designed to make the occasion worthy of Croke Park.

There will be major music acts, a host of Irish talent and a series of intriguing fights before Taylor takes her final walk to the ring.

'I'm not going to give too much away… I want you all to see it unfold on the night,' Hearn said. 'But there's definitely people everybody's heard of in this country who are going to be performing on Saturday night, and a number of different things going on during the night.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury delivers brutal verdict on Moses Itauma - and claims agonising defeat against Filip Hrgovic could cost British star £100m
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury delivers brutal verdict on Moses Itauma - and claims agonising defeat against Filip Hrgovic could cost British star £100m

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tyson Fury believes fellow British boxer Moses Itauma fought Filip Hrgovic too soon in a decision that could 'cost him £100million'.

Itauma, 21, fell short in his world heavyweight title bout against the Croat when he was stopped in the ninth round at The O2 on Saturday night.

Britain's talented young boxer was ahead on the cards and looked destined to claim the vacant IBF heavyweight title before Hrgovic, 34, mounted an impressive comeback to stage the shock victory.

Fury, who is gearing up for an expected showdown with long-time British rival Anthony Joshua in November, believes Itauma's first shot at a world title came 'too early' and it could ultimately deny him a huge payday.

'I said it was too early – and it could cost him £100m,' the former heavyweight champion told The Telegraph on Thursday, who famously defeated Wladimir Klitschko to win three world-title belts at the age of 27 in 2015.

'If I had boxed him aged 21, Klitschko would have knocked me out,' the Gypsy King recalled. 'Moses is a brilliant talent. I've had him in camp and sparred him many times.

Tyson Fury (above) believes fellow British boxer Moses Itauma fought Filip Hrgovic too soon

Itauma, 21, lost his world title bout against the experienced Croat at The O2 on Saturday night

'Moses is very talented but also very young and raw. Whatever Moses is at 21, in five years' time, 10 years' time, he'll be 10 times better, 10 times stronger, more experienced. He's an amazing boxer, talented.'

Despite waxing lyrical about Itauma's raw ability, Fury believes he wasn't ready to face a 'battle-hardened veteran' such as Hrgovic, who has fought hundreds of fights at differing levels around the world.

'As we saw for the first six, seven rounds, Moses outclassed him,' the 38-year-old said. 'But when it came to the stretch, the championship distance, the young man wasn't ready to go down the straight with a veteran who trained hard, looked in fantastic shape, dedicated himself, and is in the prime of his life at 34.

'I said to everybody who would listen, this is too soon. This guy needs another four, five fights. What's the rush? He's 21. Not only has it cost Moses the hundred-million-dollar career as a superstar athlete – like (NBA star) LeBron James and all those people – when you've been banjoed like that it's difficult to turn that around mentally.

'It's not rocket science. If you go from not going past four rounds to jumping into a 12-round world-title fight without winning anything along the way... if you look at my career, I won English, Irish, British, Commonwealth, European, every international belt there was along the way and every world-title belt, too: Lineal, Ring Magazine, everything you can think of... I did it the traditional route.'

Itauma, who went into the title fight unbeaten, won every round heading into the second half of the bout before momentum swung drastically in the Croat's favour.

Fury believes he wasn't ready to face a 'battle-hardened veteran' such as 34-year-old Hrgovic

Fellow British boxer Chris Eubank Jr posted on X after his defeat: 'Not sure what happened tonight. Moses was fighting well & then gassed out it seems… at his young age this should simply not be happening.

'Time to rethink his training camp moving forward I think. Congratulations to Filip Hrgovic becoming the new heavyweight champ.'

Sports.title: 'This could put people's lives at risk': The 'deeply worrying' dangers of Olympian boxer Anthony Fowler's Supreme Peptides selling unlicensed 'DIY Ozempic', a mystery London lab and how regulators are cracking down on 'repeat offender'
Sports.content:
Former Olympic boxer turned influencer Anthony Fowler has joined the booming market in cheap 'DIY Ozempic' in a way which scientists have told us could be putting lives at risk, a Daily Mail Sport investigation has found.

Fowler, who we exposed last year for making potentially dangerous claims about his cannabis oil products, has now expanded into peptides, by spinning a new business out of his Supreme CBD firm. The company was willing to sell weight-loss products to a would-be buyer while not disclosing the contents of the product and simply instructing them to inject themselves over several weeks to lose weight and ‘see what results you get’.

After approaching Fowler, 35, who won Commonwealth Games gold in 2014 and boxed for Team GB at Rio 2016, as part of our undercover investigation into his activities, Daily Mail Sport was offered a 40mg dose of a weight loss peptide for £120 by his new Supreme Peptides business and told it had reduced Fowler’s brother’s weight by two stone. We were told the product was ‘similar’ to the licensed weight-loss drug Mounjaro but had ‘no side effects’.

Under UK law, any companies using medical claims to sell products – including those pushing obesity treatments – must have the appropriate authorisation from the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) before selling or supplying it. Daily Mail Sport has found no evidence that Supreme Peptides has any products registered with the MHRA.

The MHRA told us it did not comment on potential or ongoing investigations. It said: 'If a product is classified as a medicine and is not appropriately authorised, we take regulatory compliance action.'

One of the products pictured on Fowler’s Supreme Peptides website – Tesamorelin, used in the US by HIV patients and people looking to shed abdominal fat – is not an MHRA-authorised medicine and selling or supplying it in the UK is illegal. Fowler is offering it for sale at a price of £89.99 for 10mg.

Former Olympic boxer turned internet influencer Anthony Fowler has joined the booming market in cheap 'DIY Ozempic' in a way which scientists have told us could put lives at risk

Fowler, who we exposed last year for making potentially dangerous claims about his cannabis oil products, has now expanded into peptides - pictured with girlfriend Serena Stregapede

Fowler, 35, won Commonwealth Games gold in 2014 and boxed for Team GB at Rio 2016

Channa Jayasena, a professor of medicine at Imperial College London, told us that it was ‘deeply worrying’ to see people, desperate to lose weight but unable to access prescription-only drugs, being offered unlicensed products.

Jayasena, a professor of reproductive endocrinology, which deals with hormone and fertility issues, said: ‘This could put people's lives at risk. You have to make peptides using very strong chemicals and then purify them using more strong chemicals.

'These chemicals are highly toxic and they are purified under incredibly rigorous conditions and standards, that need to be kept. My concern is that these are black market synthesised peptides, which have potential impurity and no guarantee of what is inside them.’

A major investigation by the Daily Mail into ‘DIY Ozempic’ sellers last year found that peptides – the active ingredient in licensed weight-loss drugs – were being sold to people to make cheap home-use kits without the legally required medical checks or monitoring. Scientists told us that customers didn’t know what they were buying or whether the advised dosage was safe.

Potential harms include increased cancer risk and damage to organs. Huge demand for weight-loss injections – now believed to be used by around 2.5 million Britons – has fuelled a booming black market.

Liverpool-based Fowler, who continues to use retired professional footballers Paul Merson, Chris Kirkland, Matt Le Tissier, John Aldridge and Emile Heskey to promote his cannabis oil products, is openly claiming on his social media channels that his peptides should be taken for weight loss. In a post last month he claimed to have 'a lab I use in London’ which tested them. Aldridge and Heskey have been promoting his weight-loss claims.

Katie Price has also been posting about Supreme Peptides, saying this week: 'Only the best from @SUPREMEPEP_1' on a post talking about how 'brilliant' tesamorelin is.

One of Fowler’s Instagram posts depicts a chiselled man bearing a six pack beside a fat man scoffing food, and declares of the health safety authorities: ‘They don’t want you having whats good for you (sic).’

Since setting up his peptides business, which he registered at Companies House in June, Fowler has fallen foul of Instagram rules and the platform suspended his account last month, depriving him of a key way of getting orders and issuing payment instructions to customers. He told his followers that Instagram had ‘grassed' and ‘banned’ him and that he was ‘absolutely fuming’.

Former professional footballer Emile Heskey has been promoting Fowler's Supreme CBD products

Katie Price is a public backer of Fowler's Supreme Peptides brand on social media

One product pictured on Fowler’s Supreme Peptides website – Tesamorelin, used in the US by HIV patients and people looking to shed abdominal fat – is not an MHRA-authorised medicine

The ex-boxer set up an alternative account but Instagram has continued to prevent him from responding to customers’ direct messages. From his sun lounger on holiday, Fowler told his followers on August 27 that his DMs were working, only to state in a later post that he was being ‘harassed’ because they were blocked ‘yet again’.

Amid his Instagram difficulties, Fowler directed followers to the account of an ‘Anthony Lloyd’ whose WhatsApp profile picture is the Supreme Peptides brand, telling them this person would ‘look after you if you want to LOSE WE*IGHT or get in shape’.

Fowler avoids spelling ‘peptide’ and ‘weight’ properly in his posts – posting instead about ‘p*ptides’ and ‘we*ight’. Concerns have been raised that users on Instagram have been deliberately disguising words with asterisks, symbols and altered spellings in an apparent attempt to avoid automated moderation, which will hide posts from a user's feed.

When we approached Lloyd, posing as a buyer seeking a cheaper alternative to Mounjaro for his overweight wife, he immediately took our inquiry off-platform so that we could securely communicate via WhatsApp.

In an exchange there, Lloyd told us that it would be £120 ‘for 40mg’ of the weight loss peptide. He detailed the paraphernalia he was including at that price, including the ‘pen’ – a syringe – with which to inject the drug and an ice pack to keep it at a low temperature. It was 'lab tested' and 'already mixed ready to go,' he said.

At no stage did Lloyd ask the buyer’s wife’s Body Mass Index (which tells doctors whether such a drug may be prescribed) or about any underlying health conditions and he was vague about the quantities, telling us to inject 2mg once a week for three or four weeks and ‘see what kind of results you get’.

When our customer asked if this product was 'similar' to the medically licensed weight loss drug Mounjaro, Lloyd replied: ‘It’s similar mate but this has no side effects.’ Lloyd claimed that Fowler’s brother has ‘already lost two stone’.

We messaged Fowler when he temporarily regained access to his Instagram messages, posing as another customer, ‘Emma’, asking for ‘weight loss if you have a product that works?’ He passed her straight on to Lloyd, who offered the same dosage as our first buyer at the same price and told us he was Fowler’s supplier.

The second customer asked if the product was similar to Ozempic. Lloyd replied: ‘It slows down (your) appetite' and told her that the 40mg dosage should last her ‘two to three months’ if she took 2mg per week.

Fowler's Supreme Peptides website, which makes multiple claims that the products are sold for research only

The former boxer appears prominently on the website's homepage

'Emma' asked for an image of the bottle of the weight-loss drug she was buying, to establish what it contained, but could not get one out of Lloyd. It transpired that the product being sold for weight loss was not among the scores pictured on the Supreme Peptides website. Lloyd told her: ‘All other peptides are on the website but if you wanted that one you would have to contact me.’

She asked: ‘Mind if I ask why this one is different to the ones on the website?’ He seemingly avoided answering, telling her simply: 'This one is a weight-loss peptide.’

When ‘Emma’ again asked Lloyd about the specific chemical ingredients in the weight loss peptide she was being offered, he simply told her it was for ‘research purposes’ and referred her to the Supreme Peptides website, where there is no information.

Supreme Peptides products require a bank transfer for the weight-loss drug, which would entail revealing our identity, so we have not followed through on the £120 purchases.

Fowler appears to be trying to exploit an MHRA loophole, under which certain substances may be supplied for legitimate 'research' without being licensed as medicines, by claiming that he is supplying them for ‘research purposes’.

Professor Jayasena, who has examined Fowler’s Supreme Peptides claims for us, said: ’I find the mention that this is “for research use only” deeply worrying and completely incongruous with what I'm seeing – which is a clear solicitation of members of the public.

'The idea of members of the public who clearly don’t have any likely or plausible role in doing research, such as a university or a government or a private laboratory would have, asking for small quantities of peptides is completely far-fetched. It's inconsistent with conducting research. Researchers do not do mail order delivery with needles or answer emails on how to inject stuff.’

Lynda Scammell, head of borderline products at the MHRA, told Daily Mail Sport: ‘We disregard claims that products are for “research purposes” if it is clear that such claims are being used as an attempt to avoid medicines regulations. If there is evidence within the promotional material that the products are in fact unauthorised medicines intended for human use, we will take appropriate regulatory action.’

Since setting up his peptides business, which he registered at Companies House in June, Fowler has fallen foul of Instagram rules and the platform suspended his account last month

He told his followers that Instagram had ‘grassed' and ‘banned’ him and that he was ‘absolutely fuming’

Many peptides are sold with no medical claim, such as those sold for bodybuilding, so do not fall within MHRA scrutiny. But the huge growth in their use as a cut-price Ozempic alternative has seen the regulator raid a number of premises involved in manufacturing and distributing unlicensed weight-loss medicine this year.

Fowler also repeatedly tells his followers that his products are British-made and superior to substandard Chinese imitations.

Professor Jayasena added: ‘Any drug or high-quality chemical that's made for human consumption, particularly medicine, needs to be subjected to standards – incredibly rigorous standards – which control even the temperature logs of the fridges and the freezers in which the drug is kept.

'You have to show the stability of your compound. You have to show bugs growing in it. You have to show purity. It is a real hole in the head – and that's why only big pharmaceutical companies do this type of stuff – and it doesn't matter where it’s made.'

After our series of exchanges with Anthony Lloyd over a period of ten days, his Instagram account disappeared on August 28. It is unclear whether he removed it, or it was forcibly closed.

From his sunshine holiday location, Fowler has now been directing customers who want to buy peptides from him to the Instagram account of his brother, Peter Fowler. Last week, he set up a new TikTok account to promote his peptides.

Daily Mail Sport can reveal that Fowler's Supreme CBD firm has been put on an Advertising Standards Authority 'non-compliant' list of repeat offenders after the body’s continued censure of him for claiming his cannabis oil supplements can have medical benefits failed to deter him.

That listing is supposed to trigger an investigation by Liverpool Council Trading Standards. But throughout all of our reporting on Fowler, Liverpool City Council has been singularly unwilling to provide us with any sense of whether Supreme CBD has been or might be subjected to its scrutiny.

Former Liverpool and England goalkeeper Chris Kirkland has also promoted Fowler's products

Fowler also repeatedly tells his followers that his products are British-made and superior to substandard Chinese imitations. But he did not respond to any of our questions

The council said: ‘We don’t comment on investigations. Any issues that are raised are investigated as and when they arise.’

Daily Mail Sport approached Fowler and asked him if he knew that MHRA approval was needed to legally sell peptides being marketed as an obesity treatment.

We asked him the nature of the ‘research’ his customers were being told the peptides being sold to them was for. We asked him why he didn’t picture the £120 weight-loss peptides on his website, like all his other peptide products?

We asked him for the name and location of his London ‘testing lab’ and the name of his supplier. He has not responded to our questions.

Sports.title: Jimmy Batten dead at 70: Tributes flood in for British champion boxer who was forced to retire with brain damage
Sports.content:
Jimmy Batten dead at 70: Tributes flood in for British champion boxer who was forced to retire with brain damage

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former British boxer Jimmy Batten has passed away at the age of 70.

The ex-British light-middleweight champion had been battling brain damage from his boxing career, as well as Parkinson's disease.

He made a name for himself in the 1970s and 1980s, and had his most famous fight in 1982 when he lost against Roberto Duran via unanimous decision. Many had expected him to lose early, having been stopped by Mario Maldonado in the first round just six months earlier, but a gutsy performance saw him take it all the way.

Batten was part of Terry Lawless's famous London gym having started boxing at the age of six, with the likes of John H Stracey, Maurice Hope and Charlie Magri hailing from the same place.

Stracey paid tribute to his friend on social media, posting: 'So sad to hear about my dear friend Jimmy Batten passing away.

'My great stablemate and sparring partner of many, many years… God bless you, my friend.'

Former British boxer Jimmy Batten (pictured) has passed away at the age of 70

Batten was famed for going the distance against Roberto Duran in his 1982 defeat

One fan, meanwhile, wrote on social media: 'More sad news. RIP Jimmy Batten. I knew he hadn't been well for a while but such terrible news, aged just 70. A GENUINE British boxing legend.'

Another shared: 'Rest well Jimmy', alongside praying emojis.

Batten's final fight was in 1983, when he was beaten by Prince Rodney to finish competing with a record of 40 wins and nine defeats.

Upon his retirement, Batten took up acting, but started to battle brain damage soon after his retirement and had to attend speech therapy to cope with the effects.

He also worked as a comedian and a doorman, and briefly as a boxing trainer, and spent time in prison after an altercation with three customers while a doorman.

He said of his career, via BoxingScene: 'Why would I change anything? I loved every minute of it. I'm just sad that I can't do it anymore.

'There's not many people who can say they were British champion and went the distance with Duran, is there?'

Sports.title: Time is running out for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: AJ is still yet to sign Battle of Britain deal, reveals Frank Warren
Sports.content:
Time is running out for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: AJ is still yet to sign Battle of Britain deal, reveals Frank Warren

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Joshua has still not signed the contract, so the Battle of Britain against Tyson Fury remains in jeopardy.

Time is running out.

Promoter Frank Warren, who suggested that in reality boxing's longest hatching deal had to be finalised by this weekend, says: 'AJ hasn't signed yet.

'Tyson signed in January. He's training in Miami for the fight in early November and doesn't care where it takes place. '

The original agreement stipulated England, putting Wembley Stadium on alert.

But Netflix, the mega-paymasters for the broadcast, have joined their Saudi partners in insisting on New York's fabled Madison Square Garden so as to maximise US revenue.

Anthony Joshua (pictured) is still yet to sign the deal to fight Anthony Joshua, Frank Warren has revealed

Warren (right) said Tyson Fury (left) has signed and is already in training for a potential bout

Joshua will need at least a two-month training camp for a fight of this magnitude and ideally nine to ten weeks.

It comes after Joshua was given 10 days to agree a deal on August 26 - seven days ago - with Warren previously warning: 'Unless AJ commits by the end of next week I'm afraid this will slip away like so many of those great fights which never happened.'

He added: 'At some point everyone has to say the most important thing is that it happens. Not this bulls*** about money.

'That everyone wants the fight. Does AJ really want it? I don't know. He's been through that tragedy of the car crash which killed two of his closest friends. Only he knows what he wants.'

Sports.title: Ex-British boxing champion Darren Barker shares heartfelt Ricky Hatton message as he sets off on epic 1,800-mile fundraising challenge
Sports.content:
Darren Barker has issued an emotional message about Ricky Hatton as he continues his inspiring 'The Longest Round' fundraising challenge, in memory of the boxing great.

Barker, former IBF world middleweight champion, set off from Edinburgh on Wednesday morning on a mega 1,800-mile endurance challenge to Morocco across land and sea.

The challenge sees him cycle from Edinburgh to Dover, swim the English channel (21 miles), cycle from Calais to Gibraltar before he ends off the adventure with an open-water swim across the Strait of Gibraltar into Morocco (nine miles).

The challenge will push Barker to the absolute limits, testing him both physically and mentally but he's determined to complete it for Ricky and 'for all the people out there suffering'.

Barker is raising funds for suicide prevention charity Campaign Against Living Miserably (CALM), in which Hatton had been an ambassador of.

Darren Barker is currently on a 1,800-mile endurance challenge in honour of Ricky Hatton

And speaking ahead of the challenge, the 44-year-old said: 'Last September, I had the honour and the privilege to speak to Ricky Hatton on a podcast. And days later he wasn't with us, so it really struck home and hit hard. And made me really understand what a terrible illness mental health is. I want to do something for Ricky, I want to do something to spread awareness.

'I feel like I owe this to Ricky. He gave up his time to speak to me, so this is something I need to do for him, and I want to do - and I need to do for the bigger picture. I need to do this for all the people out there suffering, to know that it's OK to not be OK. I want to encourage these people to have these uncomfortable conversations, and hopefully save lives in the future.'

He added: 'He will always be a hero of mine. He was the man that brought the big nights to British boxing. The man that brought the big crowds.

'But away from boxing, he was so likeable - he was the man next door - everyone could relate to Ricky. So funny, charming, just a real good guy with a big heart and someone that people could look up to. He is massively missed.'

Barker spoke from the heart as he explained what 'The Longest Round' and CALM mean to him.

Barker spoke to Hatton on a podcast a few days before his friend was found dead at his home

He continued: 'It means an awful lot. It means that I, along with the team, and everybody else following this - that we have an opportunity to make a real difference here. This is about changing lives, helping people. This is bigger than swimming and cycling, this is a huge opportunity to try and make a difference, and that's what I want to do.

'You, I guess, go through your early stages of life, being selfish, and you're on your own journey, trying to fulfil dreams and aspirations to do this and that, and then you kind of - in my situation anyway - achieve that - and it's about what next. And for me, it feels right to help and just try and raise money and awareness for something now that has really resonated with me.

'Even myself as a retired fighter, grieving the loss of boxing, grieving the loss of my brother, my grandad - understanding that grief is a part of mental health. So along with everyone else, this isn't just me - I may be getting on the bike and in the sea - but this is all of us pulling together and being there for one another. Let's be nice to one another, let's be there, let's support. So much hardship in the world as it is, so if we all pull together - we're halfway there you know.'

Barker is being sponsored by Just Eat, alongside the likes of the Royal Navy, INEOS Grenadier, kp-pharma and Pretty Sailing, and they have been providing the former world champion with food daily to keep him going during this gruelling challenge.

'We've been fuelling heavily. Lots of protein, the carbs have been so important for the energy. Been eating lots and lots throughout the day. It has been quite difficult during the challenge but we've been snacking.

'Lots of gels, lots of electrolytes, just fuelling correctly and it has been pivotal because I could not do it without it. We've also had some brilliant Italians, lots of pasta, lots of chicken. It has been great, it has been thoroughly enjoyable.'

Any donations can be made to: https://www.justgiving.com/page/thelongestround

Sports.title: F1 Italian GP: Russell beats Leclerc to top second practice
Sports.content:
George Russell has topped second practice at Formula 1's Italian Grand Prix, nudging Ferrari's Charles Leclerc off the top of the timesheets.

Russell set a 1m22.559s lap in the second half of the session as part of a mid-session shootout between the Briton, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Russell's Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who filled the top three.

Following tepid laps on hard tyres, also led by Russell, the second practice session came to life after 20 minutes when the frontrunners upped the pace by donning Pirelli's soft tyres, which had only been sporadically used in FP1.

On the red-rimmed tyres, Antonelli set a fastest first sector before diving back into the pits as he was blocked by traffic in the Parabolica, Monza's famed final corner.

On his next attempt, Antonelli was spared of traffic to fire in a 1m22.700s lap to go top, with team-mate Russell then taking over the lead with a 1m22.686s lap.

Leclerc, who had led the way in the first session, responded with a 1m22.679s effort, before Russell immediately claimed the lead back with a more comfortable 1m22.559s.

That time would remain untouched until the end as teams largely switched to long runs, with Leclerc and Antonelli thus finishing second and third.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Reigning world champion Lando Norris, winner of the last two grands prix, was fourth just four tenths behind Russell, while Hamilton was fifth in the second Ferrari narrowly ahead of Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren.

Arvid Lindblad made a strong impression for Racing Bulls, briefly holding third in the opening stages before setting the seventh-fastest time. Oliver Bearman was an encouraging eighth for the struggling Haas team.

FP2 was Max Verstappen's first outing of the weekend after he handed his Red Bull to reserve driver Ayumu Iwasa for a mandatory rookie outing. As is often the case for Red Bull on Fridays, Verstappen was constantly chasing an agreeable balance on his RB22, with a front wing flap change not appearing to improve matters.

Verstappen could only muster ninth as the leading Red Bull driver, with Racing Bulls stand-in Yuki Tsunoda rounding out the top 10. Tsunoda gets a second weekend with his former team as Liam Lawson deputised for the injured Isack Hadjar at Red Bull. In FP2, Lawson placed 12th behind Alpine's Franco Colapinto.

The only incidents of note were a spin for Leclerc in the second chicane, losing the rear of his Ferrari on the high sausage kerbs, and a dangerous impeding case involving Aston Martin's Lance Stroll. As Stroll came out of the pitlane, the Canadian carelessly veered into the path of Norris, who had to take avoiding action. The incident will be investigated by the FIA race stewards after the session.

There was also some concern at Audi over an ill-sounding V6 engine in the back of Gabriel Bortoleto's car, forcing the Brazilian to abandon his run plan early.

Sports.title: Briatore questions Monaco GP appeal integrity in explosive Italian GP press conference
Sports.content:
Alpine Formula 1 boss Flavio Briatore has questioned the fairness of the appeal procedure against the Monaco Grand Prix results, claiming one judge has a close relationship with McLaren.

Pierre Gasly was one of several drivers penalised in Monaco for exceeding the pitlane speed limit, which was later found to be the result of an incorrect measurement by FOM. Gasly lost his third place, but Alpine launched a right of review against the penalties, with the FIA race stewards agreeing to rescind the Frenchman's penalty.

McLaren and Red Bull appealed against that decision, as the other drivers involved had already served their penalties and didn't have the opportunity to get those rescinded.

Following a lengthy procedure, the FIA's International Court of Appeal ruled in favour of the appellants and reinstated Gasly's two five-second penalties, dropping him to seventh as Red Bull's Isack Hadjar reclaimed a podium spot.

Read Also: Formula 1 Gasly loses Monaco GP podium as penalties reinstated following McLaren and Red Bull appeal

In a statement the Alpine expressed "its disappointment and frustration" with the ruling. But in the FIA's Italian Grand Prix press conference on Friday, executive advisor Flavio Briatore went much further, suggesting the hearing had been unfair as he claimed one of the four judges, Italian-American Filippo Marchino, had links to McLaren.

"I think it's very unfair. We accept the decision, but what is very strange was there were four judges on the panel and one of the judges acted like a prosecutor," Briatore said. "It was four judges, and this one was really a prosecutor against the FIA, against us, against FOM.

"Afterwards we found out what is the reason why this guy was so nasty. It's very linked with McLaren. We have a nice picture of this guy [giving a] speech for McLaren in 2018 at MSO Beverly Hills. He has a foundation, it's called One Drop Foundation and McLaren gave two or three McLaren cars, and this was quite unfair.

Flavio Briatore, Executive Advisor of Alpine F1 Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We accept the decision, we accept everything, but it's quite strange to have one guy in the panel linked to the team. This is unfair. The judge normally needs to be independent completely."

Sitting alongside Briatore, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella was visibly taken aback by those accusations.

"I find that this conference is going in a direction that is quite insulting for McLaren, for the reputation of a team that deserves a lot of respect," Stella shot back. "And if anybody makes these kinds of allegations, which seem quite serious, they are going to have to take the responsibility for what they are saying in a public forum.

"The hearing, the whole International Court of Appeal was conducted to the highest standards, and we should not question this case like it's been done."

Commenting on the Monaco appeal outcome, which also moved up McLaren driver Oscar Piastri up from fifth to fourth and earned the two additional championship points, Stella said: "It's a decision that definitely we welcome. It's very important, because it adds clarity in relation to the application of Article 1.1.1 of the International Sporting Code of the FIA, which is foundational for anything that derives from there.

"We appealed because we wanted to make sure that this clarity was sought. We had concerns which were beyond the fact that we might have lost two championship points. Probably these two championship points are not going to make any difference. We were concerned about the application of sporting equality and fairness. This is important and this is not only important for McLaren.

Andrea Stella, McLaren Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

"In fact, not only Red Bull applied, but all teams were present in the hearing because this was a very important moment in terms of clarification as to how we apply the rules, as to how we apply consistency, and also in the specific case, consistency is related to the methodologies that are valid through our race weekend."

Briatore returned to F1 in June 2024 as an executive advisor to then-Alpine CEO Luca de Meo. Earlier in his career, the Italian helped steer the Benetton and Renault teams to consecutive world championships, with Michael Schumacher and Fernando Alonso respectively.

But he was subsequently handed a lifetime paddock ban for his instrumental role in the 2008 Singapore 'Crashgate' scandal. Briatore had been implicated in a plot that involved his driver Nelson Piquet Jr crashing deliberately to cause a safety car intervention that helped his team-mate Alonso win. That lifetime ban by the FIA was overturned in 2010, with the Italian a regular paddock presence as a dealmaker until his official return with Alpine.

Sports.title: Why Norris wanted to set up his own single-seater race team
Sports.content:
Lando Norris says he hopes establishing his own junior team and driver programme can help guide underfunded talent all the way to the Formula 1.

On Wednesday Norris announced two separate projects; a single-seater race team called LN4 Fusion and the LN4 Legacy programme which aims to support a young driver's career through the FIA's ladder.

LN4 Fusion will be run by former long-time Prema team boss Rene Rosin, with Dan Hazlewood running the team's UK arm, and is working on fielding cars in F2, F3 and British F4.

LN4 Legacy Programme, led by former Alpine sporting director Julian Rouse, is a fully-funded programme aimed at supporting young talents all the way to the top. Norris says he was keen to give back to the sport in the face of the spiralling costs of single-seater racing.

"The legacy programme is more to pick out individuals, people that we believe can get to Formula 1 and try and help them one at a time. That's our initial goal," Norris explained. "The fact that drivers have to kind of go out of their way to do it is, I think, an acknowledgement of how difficult it is."

Given the finances involved, LN4 Legacy Programme is starting by backing one yet-to-be-named junior driver, but Norris is hoping he can raise the backing to scale up the programme in the future.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"The scale we're talking about, you're talking tens of millions to start projects like this. And you need good backing from a lot of investors, things like that. And that can easily be and will be a longer-term project," he said.

"We've got to start somewhere. And I'm happy that I'm trying to help at least one to begin with, and then we'll work on two and then three and then four and five."

On the team side, Norris said former Prema chief Rosin was the ideal candidate to lead LN4 Fusion after racing against the Italian's powerhouse team for years, and Rosin surprisingly became available after ceding control of the family-owned team last winter.

"I've known Rene for many years, since I started to go into single-seaters," Norris explained. "We wanted to put together a group that is experienced and knows how to lead a team and not just create one good team, whether that's just in F3 or just in F2, but be able to put together a project and something long term.

"I've also been able to experience over the course of the last seven years what makes a good leader, what makes a good team. A lot of it starts with the person at the very top and he is that person. He was the inevitable choice."

Norris revealed Rosin had received plenty of interest from various corners to join LN4 Fusion, with the project getting a positive reception from around the industry.

Doriane Pin, PREMA Racing, Rene Rosin of PREMA Photo by: Sam Bloxham / Motorsport Images

"The reactions have been great. Rene said he got over a few hundred job requests within the space of an hour or so of the announcement," Norris said. "So, there's a lot of attraction from a range of drivers, but also mechanics, engineers, all the people that make a team. I'm proud that we've been able to put something very special together."

Norris credited the team he had built around him for helping him take on projects like this, meaning he can still focus on his day job at McLaren and pitch in whenever he is available.

But he was also conscious that it will take much more than his project, or fellow world champion Max Verstappen's GT3 race team, to make a lasting impact, as he called upon the FIA and on F1 management to help bring the exorbitant costs on the single-seater ladder.

"If you want to help bigger areas and economies that are just worse to kind of start racing and allow people to start their dream, it's much bigger than just me doing my job and trying to help out on that," he said. "That takes the sport itself. That takes a lot more work from F1, from FIA, from karting companies.

"It's just simply too expensive, so you cannot rely on people just to fund more people. You have to find other ways to make it more friendly for people to start racing and especially financially. You've got to lower the costs somehow of teams, of the ability to go testing, of just signing up to do Formula 2. F2 is over €2million euros, I think, to start.

"You've got to start somewhere. My ability is starting with one and that's already a big project. Hopefully, over time and with more partners coming on board and more money, more support, we can turn it into a way of helping more people from around the world."

Sports.title: F1 Italian GP: Leclerc heads Ferrari 1-2 in opening practice
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc led a Ferrari 1-2 to set the fastest time in first free practice at Formula 1's Italian Grand Prix.

Leclerc's time of 1m23.008s, set on medium tyres, was quick enough to pip team-mate Lewis Hamilton on a hot summer afternoon at the historic Monza circuit.

Leclerc set his time halfway through the first of three practice sessions, boosting expectations from the partisan home crowd in Italy.

Sporting a throwback livery paying tribute to Michael Schumacher's first season with Ferrari in 1996, Ferrari came to its home track with its latest suite of upgrades. Those updates include a refined low-drag rear wing and the Scuderia's second permitted engine upgrade that aims to help slash its power unit deficit to Mercedes.

Read Also: Formula 1 Ferrari to bring upgraded engine to Italian GP under ADUO

Reigning world champion Lando Norris had been leading the early running before the session was interrupted by Colton Herta's stricken Cadillac. The American was asked by his team to park the car with hydraulic issues, bringing out the red flag.

Test driver Herta had been hunting another superlicence point with his practice outing, but due to his lack of mileage the former IndyCar ace will not get one for his Monza run.

The session resumed with 34 minutes on the clock, with Mercedes' George Russell dipping below Norris' time before Leclerc took charge with a 1m23.008s on medium rubber.

Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Hamilton followed Leclerc through in second, shipping 0.173s to his team-mate on the same medium compound, as Russell reclaimed third with a 1m23.312s lap on soft tyres, three tenths down on the leading Ferrari.

Liam Lawson, who returned to Red Bull as regular driver Isack Hadjar continues to recover from his wrist injury, set fourth ahead of championship leader Antonelli.

Antonelli faces a back-of-the-grid penalty for a full power unit change, meaning the championship leader is fully focused on optimising his race set-up.

The Italian demoted Norris to sixth ahead of Racing Bulls man Arvid Lindblad and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto. Alpine duo Franco Colapinto and Paul Aron, performing rookie FP1 duties in Pierre Gasly's car, rounded out the top 10.

In the second McLaren, Oscar Piastri was 11th ahead of Yuki Tsunoda, who received a second opportunity to fill Lawson's temporarily vacated Racing Bulls seat.

Herta and Aron were just two of four rookie drivers out on track in FP1. Ayumu Iwasa took place in Max Verstappen's Red Bull and Williams young driver Luke Browning got a run in Alex Albon's car as teams took the opportunity to satisfy one of the four mandated rookie FP1 runs for the season on a non-sprint weekend.

With temperatures soaring above the agreed threshold of 31 degrees and expected to do so for every on-track session, the FIA declared a heat hazard for this weekend's running, forcing drivers to either wear cooling vests or carry additional ballast.
