World.title: Murkomen reaffirms IG Kanja's command of National Police Service
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has reaffirmed that the Inspector General of Police retains constitutional command of the National Police Service, saying the government will continue to respect the independence of the office.

Speaking during the passing-out parade of new Administration Police recruits in Nairobi, Murkomen said the Inspector General has authority over key operational matters within the service, including investigations, promotions and deployment of officers.

“Your Excellency, the Inspector General of Police retains the command of the National Police Service, especially on matters of investigation, promotion and deployment of officers without interference from anyone, including the Cabinet Secretary. We will continue respecting Article 245 of the Constitution,” Murkomen said.

His remarks come amid public debate over the relationship between the Interior Ministry and the National Police Service, particularly allegations that political leaders sometimes issue direct instructions to police officers.

Murkomen dismissed criticism directed at the office of the Inspector General, describing some of its proponents as tribalists and propagandists. He maintained that the Inspector General is carrying out his responsibilities and said he had confidence in the leadership of the police service.

“I have full faith in the IG and believe that every act that is done by the National Police Service is guided by the Constitution,” he said.

The Cabinet Secretary also addressed concerns over his role in directing the police, saying that his responsibility is primarily to provide policy direction rather than interfere with the operational command of the service.

“When required to give policy direction, I always give it in writing and we will continue to support the independence of the National Police Service from external interference,” Murkomen said.

During the ceremony, Murkomen also cautioned the newly graduated officers against corruption, excessive alcohol consumption and conduct that could undermine the reputation of the police service.

He urged the recruits to uphold discipline and protect the dignity of the police uniform, noting that the respect they receive from members of the public would depend largely on their conduct.

The Cabinet Secretary encouraged the officers to understand the responsibility that comes with joining the National Police Service and to discharge their duties within the confines of the Constitution and the law.

The passing-out ceremony marked the entry of the new recruits into the police service that made the CS use the occasion to emphasize professional conduct and respect for the constitutional framework governing policing in Kenya.

World.title: Ruto assures Kajiado residents of full control of Amboseli National Park
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto inspects the Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project in Kajiado County on September 3, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

President William Ruto has assured Kajiado residents that they will soon have full control of the management of Amboseli National Park, following his decision to return the park to the county in November 2025.

However, he said the transfer has been temporarily halted by the court.

The President hit out at those he accused of frustrating the move, saying they will be in for a rude shock.

“They took us to court over the Social Health Authority and the Affordable Housing Programme, but these programmes are progressing well. Similarly, I want to assure the people of Kajiado that, before the end of this year, Amboseli will be fully in the hands of Kajiado County,” he said.

Speaking in Kajiado County on Thursday during his development tour, President Ruto reiterated that he will not relent in his pursuit of equity and inclusive development across Kenya, saying that longstanding inequalities have unduly benefited certain regions at the expense of others.

He revealed that the securitisation of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund and the Sports Fund has enabled the Government to clear pending bills in the roads sector and construct 6,000km of new roads, and accelerate the construction of 32 new stadia across the country.

"The Road Maintenance Levy Fund was misused to only build roads in some parts of the country. Those opposing securitisation are unhappy that we are advancing equity," he said.

The President began his tour at Oloirien in Kajiado South Constituency by inspecting progress of the 67km Illasit-Rombo-Chala-Njukini-Taveta road, which is 48 per cent completed.

The Sh9.4 billion project will cut travel time between Kajiado and Taita-Taveta counties from two hours to just 40 minutes, thus easing the movement of goods and people.

The Head of State announced that eight new roads of 220km are being built across Kajiado County at a cost of Sh13 billion to open up the region and improve transport.

The President commissioned Sh221 million Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project, which is expected to enhance livelihoods and boost irrigation in the area.

He also inspected progress of the Sh2.2 billion Loitoktok Affordable Housing Project, and laid the foundation stone for the Sh220 million Loitoktok Kenya Medical Training College student hostels with a 580-bed capacity.

At Kimana, in Kajiado South Constituency, President Ruto commissioned the Sh2.7 billion Sultan Hamud-Loitoktok 132kV Transmission Line and Loitoktok Sub-Station, which will serve the residents of Kajiado South and parts of Makueni County.

He inspected construction of the Kimana modern market, which is aimed at giving traders dignified working environment.

At Namanga, Kajiado Central Constituency, the President commissioned the Namanga Sub-Station, a project of the Kenya Electricity Transmission Company (KETRACO), which is part of the 132KV Machakos- Konza-Isinya-Namanga Transmission Project.

Namanga Modern Market, which is under construction at a cost of Sh50 million, will benefit 120 traders at the border town.

In Kajiado town, the President toured the construction of the Kajiado Affordable Housing Project, a Sh473 million investment that will deliver 196 housing units, as well as the 100-unit police housing project at a cost of Sh137 million.

He also inspected the progress of the 580-bed student hostels at Maasai National Polytechnic, which is being built at a cost of KSh216 million.

Ruto ordered the closer of Tata Chemicals, saying the government will identify a new and responsible investor to take over soda ash mining operations at Lake Magadi.

The President said Tata Chemicals had failed to adequately modernise the plant, create sufficient employment opportunities for residents, and deliver meaningful economic benefits to the people of Kenya.

“It is unfair for one company to dominate the ownership and operations of Magadi Soda for years, yet it has done little to improve the factory or create employment opportunities for our youth,” he said at Rombo in Kajiado South Constituency.

He added: “Because they have been unable to do anything meaningful with the plant for more than 100 years, I have directed them to pack up and go.”

The Ministry of Mining suspended the company’s mining operations in July 2026 over concerns relating to regulatory compliance, value addition and licensing.

The ministry also ordered the closure of the company’s depot in Kajiado Town for contravening environmental regulations.

In addition, the company has been unable to reach an agreement with the Kajiado County Government over a land rates dispute following the expiry of its operating licence in 2023.

The plant produces soda ash, or sodium carbonate, a key industrial mineral used in the manufacture of glass, soap and laundry detergents, among other products.

Despite being Africa’s largest soda ash producer, President Ruto noted that the operation had not delivered commensurate benefits to Kenyans over its more than 100-year history, particularly because much of the soda ash produced is exported for processing and consumption in overseas markets.

The Government, the President said, would therefore prioritise an investor capable of modernising the facility, expanding local value addition, creating jobs for young people, and ensuring that Kenya derives greater economic value from its natural resources.

World.title: IG Kanja orders probe into abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Standard Group PLC Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered immediate and transparent investigations into the alleged abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich in Gilgil.

The National Police Service (NPS) said it had taken note of reports that Kiprotich was allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday and had moved swiftly to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

NPS spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said the police service treats kidnapping and abduction with the utmost seriousness, describing the offences as a threat to the lives, liberty and security of Kenyans.

“The Inspector General of Police has accordingly ordered immediate investigations to determine what transpired, including the identity of the heavily armed individuals reportedly seen ordering occupants out of their vehicle,” Nyaga said in a statement.

The NPS said its Anti-Abduction Unit, established to investigate abductions and disappearances, had taken up the matter and would work to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“We unequivocally condemn any act of kidnapping, abduction, or intimidation intended to interfere with press freedom or any other constitutional right,” Nyaga said.

The police service assured the public that the investigation into the Gilgil incident would be conducted transparently, stressing that no one was above the law.

The development comes amid growing condemnation of Kiprotich’s alleged abduction, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also calling for an immediate investigation.

CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal described the incident as a “shameful indictment” of the Kenya Kwanza administration, raising concerns over the safety of journalists and press freedom in the country.

“The attempt to forcibly disappear Alex Kiprotich, three days after President William Ruto railed against The Standard Group, reflects the growing dangers that journalists face in Kenya, despite the president’s earlier promise to allow the press to work freely,” Quintal said.

The New York-based press freedom organisation further expressed concern over what it described as an escalation in cases of abductions and enforced disappearances in Kenya.

World.title: Trumpets of reforms blow louder as Kenya marks 16 years under 2010 Constitution
World.content:
The Constitution, Kenyan flag and the National anthem. [PCS]

On Thursday, August 27, a group of people largely composed of the youth gathered under some trees at Jeevanjee Gardens in Nairobi, carrying Kenyans flag, and banners and placards inscribed with "implement the constitution. Kenyans first" words.

These were in protests against what they believed is deliberate failure of those in authority to fully implement the 2010 Constitution.

World.title: Ruto allies hit back at Gachagua over IEBC tender concerns
World.content:
The Kenya Integrated Elections Management System (KIEMS) kit. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto’s allies led by National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula have launched a scathing attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and the Opposition over their criticism of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), citing blackmail by the Opposition.

The leaders warned that attempts by politicians to dictate how the electoral agency procures technology and other election materials could undermine public confidence in the 2027 General Election.

World.title: IEBC rejects Gachagua's claims, defends 2027 polls preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC dismissed Gachagua's claims of political interference, graft and voter suppression in 2027 polls.

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has dismissed allegations of political interference, corruption and voter suppression surrounding preparations for the 2027 General Election, terming the claims false, unsubstantiated and aimed at undermining public confidence in the electoral body.

In a statement issued on Thursday, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the allegations followed statements made by Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a press briefing on Wednesday.

The commission specifically rejected claims that politicians had purchased a house for its chairperson to influence him, saying the allegation had changed from an alleged Sh80 million property to one worth Sh200 million.

"The allegations that a house has been purchased for the Chairperson of IEBC by some politicians for purposes of influencing him are unfortunate, unfair and unsubstantiated to date," Ethekon stated.

The commission also challenged Gachagua to provide evidence, including the location of the property, sale and transfer documents, payment receipts and details of the parties involved, and submit them to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission for investigation.

The electoral body also dismissed claims of improper staff changes, saying deployment and redeployment of employees was part of its normal administrative functions and was guided by its human resource policies and public service regulations.

"The Commission complies with its Human Resource policies, guidelines and other relevant instruments under the larger public service when engaging employees," the statement read in part.

It further denied allegations of malpractice against the chairperson and vice-chairperson, describing them as fabricated claims intended to damage the reputation of the commissioners and the commission.

Magarini by-election

On the Magarini by-election, IEBC said the poll was conducted in a free, fair and credible manner and was not challenged through an election petition. The commission added that it had successfully conducted several by-elections and was prepared to oversee the 2027 General Election.

At the same time, IEBC also defended its procurement process for election technology and ballot papers, saying all tenders were being conducted in accordance with Chapter 12 of the Constitution and the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015.

"Two key tenders, one for the Integrated Elections Management System, hardware and accessories, and another for ballot papers and other election materials, have temporarily been halted following a request for review filed before the Public Procurement Administrative Review Board," IEBC stated.

According to IEBC, documents for the technology tender were uploaded on its website and the Public Procurement Information Portal on August 11, 2026.

The commission said the technical specifications were generic and performance-based and open to all qualified suppliers. It stressed that the procurement process was still at its initial stages and that no company had been awarded the tender.

Voter register protected

The commission also dismissed claims that voter registration data could be manipulated or shared with external parties, insisting that the Register of Voters remained under its exclusive custody.

"Voter registration involves several stages, including in-person registration, verification of identity, collection of biometric and biographical data, transmission to a central database and automated biometric deduplication," IEBC added.

Flagged records are subjected to data cleaning, validation and adjudication before valid records are incorporated into the register.

The register will subsequently undergo a 30-day biometric verification exercise, followed by an independent audit before it is finalised and certified for use in an election.

IEBC said allegations of bribery, predetermined tender awards and voter suppression were false and potentially harmful to public confidence in the electoral process.

World.title: Ruto hands Sh2.6bn to Mau Forest evictees
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto also announced the lifting pf the caveat that had been placed on land bordering the Mau Forest. [PCS]

President William Ruto has announced the payment of Sh2.6 billion to 13,000 families evicted from the Mau Forest in Narok six years ago, marking what he described as the closure of a long chapter.

Each beneficiary received Sh200,000 through M-Pesa to help them resettle and rebuild their lives away from the water tower.

Speaking at Sogoo in Narok South Constituency on Wednesday, during the final day of his two-day tour of Narok County, Ruto said the Government had taken steps to address the longstanding Mau Forest resettlement problem.

He noted that in 2023, the Government gave Sh300,000 each to 2,000 families living in tents in the Mau Forest to enable them to leave the water tower and purchase land elsewhere.

“We are today officially closing the long and painful chapter of people who were removed from the Mau Forest, which the County Government of Narok will now manage,” Ruto said.

The President criticised politicians who, he said, had continued to politicise the Mau Forest issue without providing lasting solutions.

“Many politicians have talked of the Mau question, but I talked of the Mau answer. This is why we are here today closing this chapter,” he said.

Ruto also announced that the Government had purchased 5,800 acres of land to settle families who have been living as squatters on property previously owned by the family of former Provincial Commissioner Isaiah Cheluget.

“We are processing title deeds of the people living on the land after buying the Cheluget farm,” he said.

Construction of Johanna Ng'eno University

The President also announced the allocation of Sh1.2 billion for the construction of Johanna Ng’eno University in Emurua Dikirr Constituency.

Speaking during the laying of the foundation stone, Ruto said the institution would fulfil a pledge to residents while expanding access to higher education for students from across the country.

“You told me, as residents of Emurua Dikirr, that you want a university. Today, I have brought KSh1.2 billion to construct the university that will be named after our brother Johana Ng'eno,” he said.

He said the university would create employment opportunities and attract new investments to the region.

At the same time, Ruto maintained that his administration had fulfilled at least 80 per cent of the pledges contained in its 2022 campaign manifesto.

“Kenyans will elect leaders based on their development record. Sloganeering will not make Kenyans vote for them. They have a long way to go,” he said.

The President further launched the construction of the 18-kilometre Mogondo-Cheramgoi-Mogor-Soit road in Emurua Dikirr, saying the project would improve connectivity and unlock economic opportunities in the region.

“This new road will strengthen connectivity and unlock greater economic opportunities in the region,” Ruto said.

World.title: European Triathlon Cup in Northern Ireland excludes Israeli team over Palestinian crisis
World.content:
Organizers of the European Triathlon Cup in Londonderry have barred a four-member Israeli delegation from competing in this weekend’s event, citing an outright refusal to normalize Israel’s standing on the global sporting stage while the Palestinian people continue to suffer.

The Northern Ireland Triathlon Club, which hosts the multi-sport competition featuring sequential swimming, cycling, and running legs, pulled the plug on the Israeli athletes immediately after reviewing the provisional entry list published by World Triathlon.

In a formal statement, the host club confirmed it lodged a sharp, unequivocal objection to the World Triathlon governing body, asserting that no Israeli representation would be permitted at the venue. Organizers underscored that the ban does not target individuals based on religion or ethnicity, but rather serves as a principled stand against official state representation during an ongoing humanitarian crisis.

The decision follows mounting security concerns and planned demonstrations near the venue. According to Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth, local police in Northern Ireland actively monitored calls on social media rallying protesters against the delegation’s arrival.

The boycott mirrors a broader wave of resistance sweeping international sports fixtures involving Israeli teams. UEFA recently moved upcoming UEFA Nations League matches involving Ireland and Israel to neutral venues, with Ireland’s home leg slated for Serbia behind closed doors and the return fixture scheduled in Hungary.

World.title: Seoul Korea breaks silence on secret Strait of Hormuz deployment reports
World.content:
South Korea’s presidential office dismissed media reports on Friday claiming Seoul is preparing an immediate military deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, clarifying that “nothing has been decided” and that internal evaluations remain underway.

Refuting reports that South Korea was gearing up to send forces to the strategic waterway, a presidential official told The Guardian that the claims “differ from reality,” emphasizing that the government continues to conduct close consultations with international partners to determine practical ways to support freedom of navigation and regional stability.

The denial follows domestic media reports citing military sources that claimed Seoul planned to seek National Assembly approval to deploy a P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft, a logistics support ship, and an explosive ordnance disposal unit.

The surrounding debate comes against a backdrop of heightened pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, who criticized South Korea over its reluctance to commit military assets to the region and subsequently scaled back the duration of the joint “Ulchi Freedom Shield” military exercises.

South Korea remains acutely vulnerable to supply disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, relying on the vital maritime passage for over 90 percent of its primary energy and approximately 70 percent of its crude oil imports. Officials noted that any future military deployment would strictly require a formal review by the National Security Council, cabinet approval, and final ratification by the National Assembly.

World.title: Four-story building collapses in Minya, casualties reported
World.content:
A four-story residential building collapsed on Al-Mu’assasa Street in the Ezbet Shaheen district of Minya city on Friday, triggering a major multi-agency search and rescue operation as casualties were reported, local officials confirmed.

The operational headquarters of the Minya Local Unit raised the alarm following the structural failure, prompting security authorities led by Minya Security Director Major General Ahmed Izzat to immediately deploy civil defense forces, heavy machinery, and fleet ambulances to the scene.

Emergency teams established a security cordon around the perimeter to protect bystanders while heavy equipment cleared debris in a bid to reach survivors. Rescue workers continue to search through the rubble for trapped residents and victims.

Formal legal proceedings have been filed, and investigations into the cause of the collapse are ongoing.

World.title: Egypt to raise entry visa fees starting January 2027
World.content:
The Egyptian government has established a standardized administrative fee of $15—or its equivalent in foreign currencies—for entry visas, transit visas, and select consular services provided by Egyptian diplomatic missions abroad, effective January 1, 2027.

Issued under Prime Minister Decree No. 2553 of 2026 and published in the Official Gazette on Sunday, August 30, the measure unifies consular service fees globally while repealing all conflicting provisions.

Under the new regulatory framework, the $15 administrative surcharge will be levied on top of base visa charges. Consequently, the final cost for travelers will vary depending on the specific visa category and its associated baseline fee. The move follows an earlier adjustment in March 2026, which raised the visa-on-arrival fee for foreign tourists from $25 to $30.

Egypt will continue operating its digital entry infrastructure, issuing electronic visas equipped with a quick response (QR) code for automated border verification. Currently, citizens from 118 nations qualify for visas on arrival as part of broader national initiatives designed to boost international tourism and streamline arrivals.

Officials framed the standardized fee structure as a key step toward simplifying consular procedures across all Egyptian missions overseas prior to the 2027 implementation date.

World.title: Mohamed Salah reveals drive behind Trabzonspor move for the first time
World.content:
Egyptian superstar Mohamed Salah has opened up on his high-profile move to Trabzonspor, citing an ongoing hunger for new challenges and a compelling project presented by club president Ertuğrul Doğan as the primary catalysts for his decision.

The 34-year-old winger, who finalized a two-year free agent deal through 2028 after a trophy-laden nine-year tenure at Liverpool, detailed his motivations in an interview published by Turkish outlet Sporx.

Reflecting on the factors behind his sustained success at the highest level, the Egyptian forward emphasized a lifelong need for self-reinvention. Searching for a fresh spark after achieving domestic and European glory at Anfield, where he earned legendary status among the supporters, he viewed a move to the Süper Lig as the ideal next chapter.

The persuasive vision of Trabzonspor’s leadership proved decisive during negotiations, with Doğan’s ambitions for the club convincing the veteran winger to commit to the Turkish outfit. That conviction was instantly reinforced upon arrival, as thousands of ecstatic fans greeted him at Istanbul airport—a reception that stunned even his former Liverpool teammates.

According to statements carried by Ajansspor, several ex-Anfield colleagues reached out shortly after his landing, admitting they had rarely witnessed such fanatical support.

Looking ahead, the veteran attacker has set his sights on silverware, identifying both the Süper Lig title and the UEFA Conference League as primary targets. Calling on Trabzonspor supporters to maintain their fervent backing through inevitable high and low points of the season, he pledged that the squad would spare no effort to deliver trophies to the city.

World.title: Hesham Maged comedy play ‘Khayal Mareed’ to run in New Capital
World.content:
The hit theatrical comedy “Khayal Mareed” (Sick Imagination) is set to stage a limited run at the Drama Theater inside the New Administrative Capital’s Arts and Culture City, featuring performances on September 24–25 and October 1–2.

The upcoming run follows a sold-out summer season, marking a key cultural expansion for the New Capital as it transforms from an administrative hub into a regional destination for live arts and entertainment.

Starring Hesham Maged, “Khayal Mareed” follows Dr. Taha, an eccentric psychiatrist whose unconventional methods with patients trigger a series of comedic misunderstandings. The production features a prominent ensemble cast, including Mohamed Abdel-Rahman, Hanady Mehanna, Ahmed El-Rafei, Dina Diab, Nagham Saleh, Mohsen Mansour, Waleed Abdel-Ghani, Reham Ezzat, and Nora Soliman.

Written and directed by Mohamed Hamdy, the play is produced by Yara Hassan’s Fikr Production Company.

World.title: UAE President pardons Abdul Rahman Youssef Al-Qaradawi following cybercrime conviction
World.content:
UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan has granted a presidential pardon to convict Abdul Rahman Youssef Al-Qaradawi, state news agency WAM reported on Friday.

The executive clemency follows an August 27 ruling by the Cybercrime Circuit of the Abu Dhabi Federal Court of Appeal, which sentenced the 53-year-old to 10 years in prison and imposed a fine of AED 200,000 ($54,450) upon conviction of charges brought against him. Authorities confirmed that all necessary legal procedures have been initiated to carry out the pardon.

Al-Qaradawi was extradited to the UAE in January 2025 after Lebanon’s caretaker Cabinet authorized his deportation. Lebanese authorities originally detained him on December 29, 2024, at the Masnaa border crossing upon his entry from Syria, following the overthrow of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad.

At the time of his arrest, Lebanese Prosecutor General Judge Jamal Al-Hajjar stated that Al-Qaradawi—traveling on a Turkish passport—was detained pursuant to an Arab Interior Ministers Council notice issued via Interpol. The red notice stemmed from an in absentia verdict issued by Egyptian judicial authorities on charges related to broadcasting false news and inciting violence and terrorism.

World.title: InstaPay users warned of new phishing scam targeting bank accounts
World.content:
Cybersecurity expert Mostafa Rahim has issued a stern warning over rising AI-powered phishing scams targeting users of financial applications, particularly Egypt’s digital payment platform InstaPay, alongside major banking channels.

Scammers are leveraging advanced artificial intelligence to craft convincing replicas of official bank websites and interfaces, Rahim explained during a televised interview on Sabah El-Balad. Fraudsters distribute malicious links via messaging platforms, luring victims into entering sensitive credentials on fake pages designed to mirror legitimate portals.

The schemes heavily target elderly citizens and individuals with limited digital literacy, peaking ahead of monthly pension distributions. Attackers exploit these timing windows by sending fraudulent messages promising pension increases or special government relief initiatives in exchange for personal information.

To mitigate exposure, Rahim urged consumers to follow core digital safety practices:

Never Share OTPs: One-Time Passwords must remain confidential; financial institutions and telecom providers will never request OTPs via phone calls or SMS.

Verify Web Addresses: Cross-check suspicious URLs using free threat-detection tools like Google Safe Browsing or VirusTotal before clicking.

Avoid Unsolicited Media: Refrain from opening links or downloading images sent from unrecognized numbers.

Confirm Directly: Validate any promotional offer or account inquiry through official bank hotlines or verified customer service channels.

World.title: Co-Defendant Challenges Judge’s Ruling Granting Ex-VP Taylor House Arrest, Calls It Unlawful
World.content:
MONROVIA — A day after Criminal Court “C” ordered former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor moved from Monrovia Central Prison to guarded house detention on medical grounds, a co-defendant in the same narcotics case has formally challenged the ruling, arguing that Judge Ousman F. Feika had no legal authority to grant it and asking him to reverse himself.



In a filing captio ned “Exceptions to His Honor Ousman F. Feika’s Ruling in Granting Co-Defendant Jewel Howard Taylor Compassionate Release,” Garpue K. Wonlue takes issue with the September 4 order on six separate grounds, most of them turning on a single argument: that the law Judge Feika relied on does not apply to someone in Taylor’s position.



The Case So Far



Taylor, Liberia’s vice president from 2018 to 2024, was arrested at Roberts International Airport on August 19 in connection with what officials have described as a transnational narcotics trafficking investigation tied to a record cocaine seizure earlier this year.

She was formally charged over eight counts, including unlicensed importation, unlicensed sale and trading, and illicit trafficking of drugs, along with money laundering and abuse-of-office allegations.



Her lawyers spent the following weeks trying, without success, to keep her out of the general prison population.

A Monrovia City Court magistrate denied an initial request for compassionate detention, ruling that granting it fell within the authority of the Ministry of Justice rather than the judiciary the defense’s follow-up appeal to the Supreme Court challenging that denial did not stop Taylor from being remanded to Monrovia Central Prison. She entered custody on September 2.



The case then moved to Criminal Court “C,” the circuit with jurisdiction over major drug offenses, where Judge Feika ordered Taylor’s immediate transfer from prison to 24-hour guarded house detention at her residence, converting her pre-trial custody into house arrest pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

Feika was explicit that the order rested solely on medical grounds and carried no bearing on guilt, writing that the release “shall therefore not constitute dismissal, acquittal, pardon, immunity, or termination of the criminal proceedings.

The judge also noted that the State itself had not opposed the request.



The Challenge



Wonlue’s filing does not dispute that Taylor has a medical condition. Instead, it argues that the court used the wrong statute to address it — and in doing so, exceeded its authority. The exceptions raise six points:



1. Jurisdiction: The filing argues that Chapter 34, Section 34.20 of the Criminal Procedure Law — the provision Judge Feika relied on — applies only to people who have already been indicted, tried, convicted, sentenced and committed to prison. Taylor, still awaiting trial, doesn’t fit that description, the filing contends, and Wonlue asks the court to rescind the ruling and have her returned to custody at Monrovia Central Prison.



2. No such remedy exists: The Criminal Procedure Law provides for bail under Chapter 13 for the accused, and for commitment under Chapter 34 for the convicted, the filing says — but nothing in between for a pre-trial detainee seeking release on medical grounds. Granting “compassionate leave” from pre-trial detention, it argues, is a remedy the court created rather than one the statute authorizes.



3. Consent doesn’t create jurisdiction: The fact that the State did not oppose Taylor’s request doesn’t change the analysis, the filing argues — parties cannot agree to give a court power the statute doesn’t grant it.



4. Equal treatment. This is the filing’s broadest argument: that granting one high-profile, pre-trial detainee a form of release unavailable to others sets up a two-tier system, at odds with the fairness-in-administration standard in Section 1.2 of the Criminal Procedure Law and Article 11 of the 1986 Constitution. The filing points out that many pre-trial detainees at Monrovia Central Prison have untreated medical conditions of their own, and argues the proper remedy was to order the Bureau of Corrections to provide adequate care in custody — not to release one defendant from it.



5. The nature of the charges and the cost of enforcement: Given that Taylor faces serious felony charges — importation of controlled drugs, money laundering and abuse of office, as the filing describes them — Wonlue argues the release conditions impose an unfunded, unauthorized burden on the State, which must now provide round-the-clock security at her residence. Surrendering travel documents, the filing adds, doesn’t eliminate flight risk on its own.



6. The inquiry should have ended sooner: Once the court determined that Section 34.20 doesn’t apply to pre-trial detainees, the filing argues, that finding should have ended the motion rather than being followed by relief anyway. It maintains the appropriate avenue for a detainee with medical concerns is a bail motion under Chapter 13 — with bond, sureties and monitoring conditions — not compassionate leave.



What’s Being Asked



The filing asks Judge Feika to reverse course: to rule that Section 34.20 doesn’t apply to pre-trial detainees, to direct the Bureau of Corrections and Ministry of Health to provide Taylor medical treatment at JFK Medical Center or another approved facility while she remains in custody, and — if release is warranted at all — to take it up as a bail application under Chapter 13, with a substantial bond and formal sureties, rather than as compassionate leave.



Judge Feika has not yet ruled on the exceptions. Taylor remains under house arrest at her residence pending the outcome. All defendants in the case, including Taylor, are presumed innocent, and the charges against them remain allegations that have not been tested at trial.

World.title: Liberia Champions Key Discussions on Preventive Diplomacy and a Robust E10 Voice at the 9th E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue in Panama
World.content:
Panama – Liberia’s Political Coordinator to the United Nations Security Council, Cllr. Aloysius Jappah assumed an active role in the 9th E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue, hosted by the Republic of Panama in Panama City from 1 to 2 September 2026, delivering substantive interventions on preventive diplomacy, Council effectiveness, and the responsibilities that come with elected membership of the UN Security Council.

Since 2019, the Dialogue has convened annually to unite the ten elected members of the Council (the E10) with the five incoming members (the I5) to enhance institutional memory, coordinate priorities, and bolster the Council’s ability to uphold international peace and security.

This year’s event was inaugurated and concluded by Panama’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Javier Eduardo Martínez-Acha Vásquez, and honored at its closing by former President H.E. Mireya Moscoso.

The current E10 for 2026 includes Bahrain, Colombia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Liberia, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia.

Starting on 1 January 2027, the newly elected I5 will consist of Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, and Zimbabwe, replacing Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia as their mandates end on 31 December 2026.

Speaking during the session on “Preventive Diplomacy in Action,” moderated with the support of the Dag Hammarskjöld Foundation and its presenters Sigrid and Henrik, Cllr. Jappah anchored Liberia’s contribution in the letter of the United Nations Charter — Chapter VI (Articles 33–38) on the pacific settlement of disputes, Chapter VIII (Article 52) on regional arrangements, and Article 99 on the Secretary-General’s early-warning authority.

“The best Council intervention is a crisis that diplomacy prevents,” Cllr. Jappah affirmed, adding that “the Charter calls on us to extinguish the spark of conflict before it becomes a blaze. When we subscribed to this organization, we pledged to fulfill that obligation.”

Commenting on the operational challenge of moving from early warning to early action, the Political Coordinator emphasized what he called the prevention paradox — that when preventive diplomacy succeeds, the crisis does not occur, and success is therefore less visible than failure.

He cautioned that sovereignty concerns and geopolitical divisions frequently delay Council action, resulting in inaction until violence erupts. He warned that “Early warning without early action,” he warned, “is only a forecast of failure.”

Drawing on Liberia’s own post-conflict experience, Cllr. Jappah stressed that peace agreements close a chapter but do not, by themselves, remove the grievances, institutional weaknesses, or local tensions that can reignite conflict.

He called for the sustained deployment of good offices, mediation support, regional engagement, inclusive dialogue, confidence-building measures, early-warning capacity, and local peace infrastructures — with the consent and ownership of the country concerned.

“Peace agreements close a chapter; preventive diplomacy helps keep the next chapter from reopening the war,” he said, noting that sustained international, regional, and national engagement has been decisive in consolidating and protecting Liberia’s hard-won peace.

Contributing to Session V on reinvigorating the Council’s role in preventive diplomacy, Cllr. Jappah observed that the Dialogue offered members a valuable opportunity to internalize how a hasty drawdown of peacekeeping operations can leave a country vulnerable.

He was speaking in response to interventions on how transnational organized crime — including transcontinental drug trafficking — can undermine governance in states just emerging from conflict, where institutions remain fragile.

On the question of how the E10 should engage the incoming Secretary-General, Cllr. Jappah urged elected members to first conduct an honest internal assessment and to invest deliberately in strengthening themselves as a caucus.

He proposed that the E10 build the discipline and coordination required to create what he described as a collective “veto,” together with the guardrails to use that leverage responsibly. He observed that, over a two-year tenure, “before an elected member really gets to understand the Council and its dynamics, it is time to exit,” and he called on the E10 to systematically leverage the institutional memory of what he termed the “Farewell Five” — the five outgoing members concluding their terms each year — so that hard-earned experience is transferred rather than lost.

He further cautioned that the Council too frequently holds briefings and open meetings at which statements are made that contain useful antidotes but are followed by no concrete action.

He urged that the traditional E10 luncheons move beyond merely setting the agenda for the Secretary-General’s luncheon with Permanent Representatives, and instead become a forum in which elected members act with one voice on decisive issues before the Council.

Cllr. Jappah welcomed the newly elected members—Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, and Zimbabwe—emphasizing the importance of continuity in preventive practice, disciplined coordination among members, and adherence to the Charter as the Council’s composition changes.

“Prevention is not an abstract ideal,” he concluded. “It is the disciplined practice of acting before choices disappear.”

The E10 & I5 Annual Dialogue, established in 2019, gathers incoming, serving, and outgoing UN Security Council members to enhance institutional memory and align objectives. Panama, holding a non-permanent seat, hosted the 9th edition during its term, ending on December 31, 2026.

World.title: Liberia Elevates Diplomatic Standing as August E10 UN Security Council Coordinator
World.content:
NEW YORK — Liberia has successfully concluded its leadership as Coordinator of the Ten Elected Members (E10) of the United Nations Security Council for August 2026, marking a historic milestone in its global diplomatic resurgence.

Stepping into the helm of the E10 alongside Bahrain, Colombia, DRC, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Panama, Somalia, and Pakistan, Liberia strategically projected African leadership, unified non-permanent members, and shaped critical debate on pressing global peace and security files.

Key Achievements and Diplomatic Interventions

High-Level Security Council Diplomacy: Hosted UN Secretary-General António Guterres and E10 Ambassadors for a strategic luncheon centered on accelerating humanitarian interventions in Gaza and the West Bank.

Regional & Crisis Resolution:

Chaired the Political Coordinators’ Meeting to align consensus on the Libyan political process, security dynamics across West Africa and the Sahel, and the E10 Joint Statement on Security Council Working Methods.

International Judicial Oversight: Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary Lewis G. Brown II convened high-level negotiations with International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) President Judge Graciela Gatti Santana, driving resolution terms on judicial archives, institutional downsizing, and UN oversight sensitivities involving Rwanda and Tanzania.

🇹🇿 Humanitarian Advocacy & International Law: Spearheaded expert briefings on the Ukraine humanitarian crisis and led targeted press interventions demanding the immediate release of illegally detained UN and aid personnel in Yemen.

Council Reform & Strategic Alignment: Championed reform of Security Council Subsidiary Bodies to streamline operations and ensure unified diplomatic alignment between the E10 and the Permanent Five (P5).

A Lasting Legacy on the World Stage

Liberia’s month-long tenure as Coordinator demonstrated strategic leadership, robust policy alignment, and an elevated ability to forge consensus among diverse international partners. Upon concluding its leadership, the E10 alliance formally commended Liberia for its decisive steering of the Council’s thematic priorities throughout August.

Meanwhile, Pakistan has assumed the E10 Coordination role for September, while Liberia remains positioned as an influential, principled voice on the Security Council, committed to driving international peace, stability, and multilateral cooperation.

World.title: Liberia: Ex-Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor to Receive Medical Care at Residence Under Restrictions as Drug Case Continues
World.content:
MONROVIA — Former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor is set to receive medical attention outside detention under strict conditions imposed by Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika amid ongoing concerns about her health.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The court’s decision comes after Howard-Taylor’s lawyers raised medical concerns and sought her release from detention to allow her to receive treatment.

Under the court’s directive, Howard-Taylor is required to surrender all travel documents, effectively restricting her ability to leave the country while the case remains pending.

The former vice president will also be subject to limitations on visitors at her residence, with access restricted to a family member and her physician or physician’s assistant.

Howard-Taylor remains entangled in an ongoing investigation and prosecution involving allegations connected to an alleged transnational cocaine-trafficking operation.

Her legal team has maintained that her medical condition requires appropriate care, while the case continues to attract public attention because of the seriousness of the allegations.

The court’s latest action provides for medical considerations while maintaining judicial controls over Howard-Taylor as proceedings continue.

World.title: Liberia: Judge Feika Grants Jewel Howard-Taylor Compassionate Release
World.content:
Monrovia — Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika has granted former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor’s request for compassionate release from detention on medical grounds.

The ruling follows concerns raised by Howard-Taylor’s legal team about her medical condition and their request that she be permitted to receive medical care outside detention.

Under the court’s ruling, Howard-Taylor is required to surrender all travel documents to the court as part of the conditions of her release.

The court also ordered that visits to her residence be limited to a family member and her physician or physician’s assistant.

Howard-Taylor is facing criminal charges in connection with an ongoing narcotics investigation. She has denied the allegations.

The court’s decision allows her to leave detention while the legal proceedings continue.

This is a developing story.

World.title: Liberia: LIS Officer Thomas Kesselly Reportedly Shot in Foya
World.content:
MONROVIA — Thomas Kesselly, a member of the Liberia Immigration Service (LIS), was reportedly shot on Thursday, September 3, 2026, with conflicting accounts emerging over the incident.

Kesselley was reportedly shot at the LIS Academy in Foya.

While initial reports said Kesselly was shot, another account claims he shot himself.

However, family sources have expressed doubts about the self-inflicted shooting claim and are seeking clarity on what happened.

Kesselly’s condition and the circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear as authorities have yet to provide a definitive account.

World.title: Liberia: Witness Alleges Howard-Taylor Link to Cocaine Trafficking Investigation and Political Plot
World.content:
Monrovia — A police investigator has testified in court about an alleged cocaine-trafficking operation in Liberia, telling the court that former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor was allegedly approached over a proposed protection arrangement and that discussions also involved an alleged plan targeting the administration of former President George Weah.

The testimony was given by Raphael Wilson, Acting Commissioner of Police for the Crimes Services Division, who said he supervised the investigative team that conducted the probe.

Wilson told the court that investigators traced the alleged network to meetings involving Liberians and foreign nationals in Dubai and Liberia, beginning around 2021.

According to his testimony, a Liberian identified as Sheikh Bashir Kanti met individuals in Dubai who expressed interest in returning to Liberia to resume business activities.

Wilson alleged that the individuals later disclosed plans to establish a cocaine-trafficking operation, with Liberia allegedly intended to serve as a transit point.

The witness further testified that the foreign nationals sought protection from a senior government official to facilitate their activities in Liberia.

According to Wilson, meetings were subsequently arranged in Liberia involving Bashir, the foreign nationals and individuals identified in the investigation as Tony and Maga.

He said investigators secretly recorded at least one of the meetings using cameras and written notes as part of their investigation.

Wilson testified that cocaine trafficking and the use of Liberia as a transit route were discussed during the meeting.

The witness further alleged that participants wanted assurances that their activities would receive protection from influential government officials.

According to Wilson, Jewel Howard-Taylor agreed to provide the requested protection but indicated that she would first return to Liberia and discuss the matter with her superior.

The testimony forms part of the prosecution’s effort to establish Howard-Taylor’s alleged connection to the broader investigation.

Alleged Political Plot

Wilson also testified about discussions that, according to the prosecution, involved an alleged plan directed against the government of former President George Weah.

The witness said the discussions surrounding the alleged protection arrangement were connected to a broader political plan involving senior political figures and an alleged attempt to undermine or overthrow the government.

However, Wilson’s testimony did not establish in court who allegedly initiated the plan, the specific actions contemplated or the precise role Howard-Taylor allegedly played.

Those matters remain subject to further evidence and examination by both the prosecution and defense.

Wilson said the alleged operation continued during the Weah administration and that investigators expanded their inquiry after some of the individuals involved returned to the region.

Foundation Mentioned in Testimony

The court also heard testimony concerning an alleged connection between some of the individuals under investigation and the Jewel Starfish Foundation, an organization associated with Howard-Taylor.

Wilson said one of the participants mentioned that Howard-Taylor operated the foundation.

The witness further testified that an individual identified as Nicholas expressed willingness to assist with the foundation.

The prosecution is presenting the alleged connection as part of the broader relationship it says existed between political figures and individuals under investigation.

US$45,000 Allegedly Delivered

Wilson also testified about an alleged cash delivery during one of the meetings.

According to the witness, a shopping bag was handed over during the meeting, and investigators later received information that approximately US$45,000 had been placed inside the bag.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged payment, including its intended recipient, purpose and connection to the alleged drug-trafficking operation, remain issues for the court to determine.

Investigation Continued After Weah Presidency

Wilson told the court that the investigation continued after the conclusion of the Weah administration in 2024.

He said investigators later determined that some of the individuals under investigation had returned to the region in 2025, prompting further investigative activity.

According to the witness, intelligence officers subsequently identified additional individuals allegedly connected to the investigation.

Wilson maintained that the investigation relied on intelligence gathering, recorded meetings and information obtained during the probe.

The testimony places several issues before the court, including the alleged cocaine-trafficking operation, claims of political protection, financial transactions and an alleged plan targeting the former Weah administration.

However, the allegations remain matters to be tested through evidence and cross-examination.

Howard-Taylor’s alleged involvement has not been established merely by Wilson’s testimony. She remains entitled to the presumption of innocence unless and until a competent court determines otherwise.

The defense is expected to challenge aspects of the investigation, including the credibility and interpretation of the witness’s account, the alleged recordings, meetings, financial transactions and claims concerning the political plan.

The court will ultimately determine whether the prosecution has produced sufficient admissible and credible evidence to establish the charges against Howard-Taylor and the other defendants.

World.title: Liberia Agricultural Company Expands School Transport with New Buses
World.content:
Compound Three, Grand Bassa County – The Liberia Agricultural Company (LAC) has commissioned two new school buses and a heavy-duty TATA truck as part of efforts to improve education and operational services across its plantation.

The vehicles were commissioned over the weekend by LAC General Manager Naveen Madan on behalf of the company’s board, shareholders and management, ahead of the 2026–2027 academic and operational year.

LAC operates 11 schools serving about 7,750 students, with girls accounting for approximately 45% of total enrolment.

The company provides free access to education for employees’ dependants and has also admitted about 348 students from 46 surrounding communities. It additionally runs an adult education and literacy programme.

The new buses are expected to improve transportation for students who travel across the plantation to attend school.

LAC management says the additional vehicles will reduce students’ walking time, help them arrive home earlier and potentially give them more time for studying.

The company also expects the expanded school transport fleet to provide greater flexibility and reduce vehicle downtime, helping to ensure that school transportation remains reliable.

At the commissioning ceremony, General Manager Naveen Madan urged drivers to take proper care of the company’s vehicles and warned students against damaging or destroying bus seats and other property.

He called on both drivers and students to use the vehicles responsibly and strictly for their intended purposes.

Mr Madan also said the latest investment was part of a broader effort to improve services across the plantation, assuring staff and communities that further improvements were expected.

Alongside the two school buses, LAC commissioned a new heavy-duty TATA truck for rubber collection, extraction and other logistical operations.

The company says the investment in both education and plantation logistics is intended to strengthen its operations while improving services for employees, students and surrounding communities.

World.title: Should the Opposition Put Justice or “Bitterness Aside”?: A Moral Critique of Fr. James Phiri of CCZ
World.content:
By Kapya Kaoma

When Father James Phiri, General Secretary of the Council of Churches in Zambia (CCZ), reportedly called on the opposition to “put bitterness aside” and focus on the next election, Jesus’ words came to mind:

“You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot” (Matthew 5:13).

I never thought these words would apply so directly to Zambia’s religious and political reality.

Speaking to ZNBC, Fr. Phiri said that “it is painful to lose elections, but the opposition must set aside their bitterness, as the church is praying for them.” This statement amounts to a major moral betrayal. He expects the opposition to quietly move on to the next electoral cycle without addressing the severe injustices of the vote that just concluded.

Fr. Phiri appears to misunderstand the concept of justice. Courts operate on the principle of injury: there must be an aggrieved party, and the recent election left the opposition with a list of grievances. Asking them to swallow their pain while their leaders remain behind bars and countless supporters face politically motivated charges before biased courts is insulting.

Contrary to Fr. Phiri’s suggestion, the opposition did not just fail despite doing “their best”—they were actively denied justice. As Fr. Phiri himself noted in pre-election statements, the opposition was forced to campaign in a hostile environment, starved of legal protections, and repeatedly persecuted by state security across the nation.

Demanding that the opposition look toward a future vote without addressing the systemic flaws engineered by this regime is both illogical and suspect. Religious leaders would be better off applying directly for political favors than using the church as a shield for a partisan agenda.

Is Fr. Phiri himself not bitter about injustice? Is he not bitter about innocent musicians being arrested simply for performing for their preferred candidates in Mongu? Is he not bitter about citizens being assaulted for exercising their right to vote, courts being locked down, or the military being deployed to tallying centers?

Fr. Phiri knows that Zambians deserve answers and that those responsible must be held accountable. If these immoral violations go unaddressed, what is the point of holding another election at all?

Moreover, it is disgraceful that foreign entities—including the United Nations, the European Union, and the Anglican Church of Southern Africa—have shown the courage to denounce abuses that Zambian church leaders seem too afraid to confront. Why is there such a gaping chasm between the findings of international observers and the narrative Fr. Phiri is pushing? As the old saying goes: “He who pays the piper calls the tune.”

I agree with Fr. Phiri on one point: “It’s not over for them until God says so.” But I refuse to pray for the opposition to quietly bottle up its bitterness. Instead, they must demand justice—from God, through local, regional, and international legal channels, and from the people of Zambia. This is both their democratic duty and their fundamental right.

After all, righteous indignation can be the very foundation of justice; only those who have been wronged can demand redress. Philosophers of liberation have long endorsed Jean-Paul Sartre’s argument that outsiders and beneficiaries of power have no moral right to dictate how victims of oppression should respond to their oppressors.

Fr. Phiri was not the victim of police or military brutality. He did not risk his livelihood on a campaign, nor did he shed blood. He lost nothing. From the comfort of his office, it is easy to tell victims to blindly place everything in God’s hands. But is this what Kafwaya’s widow wants to hear? What about the families of Bishop Trevor Mwamba, Mundubile, or Makebi? Behind these elections are human wounds and shattered lives that can never be rebuilt. Fr. Phiri’s lack of empathy is appalling.

Besides, if prayers alone sufficed, why would we need laws or courts?

As a theologian, Fr. Phiri knows that God demands active justice for the oppressed. Instead of placating the powerful, he should have urged the opposition to seek redress through the legal system. He should have called on the courts to act with strict impartiality—for the law must never wear political regalia. He should have demanded an independent inquiry into the military’s presence at tallying centers, as well as the immediate arrest and prosecution of all perpetrators of political violence, including state security officers.

Furthermore, he should have called for an independent, international investigation into the irregularities surrounding the G20 forms and result tallies to restore a shred of legitimacy to our republic’s democratic processes. Finally, he should have challenged the President to make the ongoing treason trials public, allowing Zambians to see the evidence for themselves.

Had he taken these steps, his interview would have reflected an independent moral voice. As it stands, it was a devastating letdown.

World.title: Democracy and The Incumbency Advantage: The Case of Zambia
World.content:
By Venus N Msyani

On August 13, 2026, Zambians lined up across the country to elect their next president. Election day itself unfolded calmly, with voting generally conducted efficiently. According to the preliminary findings of the EU Election Observer Mission, voters were offered a competitive choice.

However, the mission also noted that restrictions on campaigning and advantages associated with incumbency contributed to an uneven playing field, a challenge familiar in many democracies.

It was after the polls closed that events took a troubling turn. As vote counting and tabulation began, the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) abruptly suspended the process nationwide for several hours without providing a clear explanation. The suspension occurred at a moment when President Hakainde Hichilema was reportedly trailing. During this period, the military took control of several tallying centers, officially to secure ballots. Some observers allege they were removed from these centers, raising concerns about transparency.

When counting resumed, Hichilema began to take the lead. Allegations soon surfaced claiming ballot box seals had been tampered with and figures altered to favor the incumbent. These claims, though not yet independently verified, fueled widespread suspicion and deepened public anxiety about the integrity of the process.

Amid these irregularities, opposition leader Brian Mundubile announced his intention to challenge the election results. Immediately afterward, his home was raided by the military in an operation authorities described as targeting an alleged militia group. The raid resulted in the death of former Minister of Transport Hon. Mutotwe Kafwaya. Mundubile and his running mate, Makebi Zulu, were subsequently charged with treason; a move that has prompted the United Nations to call for their release.

The situation escalated further on the final day of the petition window. Courts across the country were closed, preventing Mundubile from filing his challenge. This unprecedented action left many Zambians questioning whether their copper‑rich nation, long regarded as a beacon of democracy in Southern Africa, still holds that reputation.

On September 1, 2026, Hakainde Hichilema was inaugurated. Supporters argue that it is time for the country to move forward, noting that no democracy is perfect. The congratulatory messages Hichilema has received from governments, organizations, and international partners reinforce this view and suggest continued global recognition of Zambia’s leadership.

Others, however, struggle to accept the legitimacy of his presidency. They point to the military’s involvement in the electoral process and the nationwide closure of courts that prevented the election petition. To them, these events amount to military interference. They warn that allowing a president to assume office under such circumstances sets a dangerous precedent for future elections.

They emphasize that Zambia’s constitution must be respected for the country to remain a regional democratic leader. The nation’s election cycle is meant to be straightforward: campaigning, voting, declaration of results, resolution of disputes, and inauguration.

In 2026, they argue, this cycle was broken. Disputes remain unresolved, and the courts were closed at the critical moment when they were meant to address them. From this perspective, Hichilema’s presidency is viewed as constitutionally compromised. And unless Zambia confronts what happened in 2026, the precedent set today may haunt every election to come.

World.title: Zambia Records Progress Against Financial Crimes
World.content:
Zambia has made progress in its fight against money laundering and financial crimes after three areas of its anti-money laundering framework were upgraded under Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards.

Attorney-General Mulilo Kabesha says the upgrade was secured during the 52nd Eastern and Southern Africa Anti-Money Laundering Group (ESAAMLG) Task Force of Senior Officials Plenary Meeting and the 26th Council of Ministers meeting held in Kigali, Rwanda.

In a statement made available to ZNBC News today, Mr. Kabesha said the development means Zambia is now compliant or largely compliant with 38 of the 40 FATF Recommendations.

The three areas upgraded are transparency and beneficial ownership of legal persons, regulation and supervision of financial institutions, and regulation and supervision of designated non-financial businesses and professions, commonly known as DNFBPs.

Mr. Kabesha, who is also Chairperson of the Anti-Money Laundering Authority, said the progress was the result of efforts by public and private institutions to combat money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

He has since challenged Zambian institutions to shift their focus from compliance with requirements to ensuring the effectiveness of measures against financial crimes.

World.title: FRA smashes maize purchase target
World.content:
The Food Reserve Agency (FRA) has beat its maize purchase target in Central Province by more than 150 percent, buying over 102,000 metric tonnes of maize against a target of 40,000 tonnes.

Central Province Principal Public Relations Officer Tobias Phiri says the FRA has so far purchased 102,964.20 metric tonnes of maize through 139 satellite depots across seven districts.

Speaking at a press briefing in Kabwe, Mr Phiri said the province has exceeded its target by 157 percent.

He stated that Serenje is leading in maize purchases with over 23,560 metric tonnes, followed by Kapiri Mposhi with 14,453.20 tonnes, Kabwe with 14,051.40 tonnes and Chibombo with 13,233.20 tonnes.

Luano and Chisamba have contributed 9,355.20 and 8,821.90 metric tonnes, respectively.

Mr Phiri says government has already paid farmers more than K90 million for maize supplied to the FRA.

He has commended farmers for responding positively to the maize marketing programme, but urged them to keep enough grain for household consumption, especially with a drought projected in the coming farming season.

Mr Phiri says the high maize purchases will help strengthen national food security while providing farmers with a ready market for their produce.

World.title: ZCCM-IH announces proposed listing
World.content:
ZCCM Investments Holdings Plc (ZCCM-IH) has announced that it is progressing with its proposed Listing Optimisation Project, which involves the Company’s listings on the Lusaka Securities Exchange (“LuSE”), Euronext Access Paris and the London Stock Exchange (“LSE”).

The Company first announced the proposed project on July 10, 2026 and subsequently issued a further cautionary announcement on August 28, 2026.

ZCCM-IH Chief Executive Officer Kakenenwa Muyangwa explained that as part of the Listing Optimisation Project, the company is considering a proposed Odd-Lot offer for shareholders holding 100 or fewer ZCCM-IH shares.

Mr Muyangwa said as at July 20, 2026, ZCCM-IH had approximately 5,013 shareholders across its three share registers, of whom 3,637 representing 72.55 per cent held 100 or fewer shares, collectively representing approximately 0.05 per cent of the company’s total shares in issue.

He said the proposed Odd-Lot offer is intended to simplify and optimise the shareholder registers.

“What the proposed offer means for small shareholders subject to the required legal, regulatory and shareholder approvals and the final terms of the Offer, eligible shareholders will have the opportunity to either sell their Odd-Lot holdings to ZCCM-IH for cash or retain their shares,” Mr Muyangwa said.

He said the proposed offer is intended to provide shareholders with a straightforward liquidity option where the small size of their holdings may otherwise make it difficult or uneconomic to sell their shares through the market.

Mr. Muyangwa said the move is about making ZCCM-IH simpler, more efficient and easier to invest in.

He added that the proposed Odd-Lot offer is intended to give eligible shareholders a fair and straightforward cash option if they wish to realise their investment, while ensuring that one shareholder who wishes to remain invested in ZCCM-IH can retain their shares.

“Almost three quarters of our shareholders hold 100 shares or fewer, and every one of them matters to us. For holdings of this size, however, the costs and practical considerations associated with selling through the market can be disproportionate to the value of the investment,” he said.

This is contained in a statement issued to the media by ZCCM-IH Corporate Affairs Manager Loisa Mbatha.

World.title: NW Royal Establishment celebrates HH victory
World.content:
The Kapijimpanga Royal Establishment in Solwezi District of North-western Province has congratulated President Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election in the August, 13, 2026 general elections.

Speaking during a media briefing in Solwezi today, where he was flanked by other traditional leaders, Sub-Chief Mbonge said the re-election of President Hichilema is well deserved.

The traditional leader has also commended voters across the province for turning out peacefully and exercising their constitutional right, adding that the conduct of the electorate demonstrated maturity and commitment to peace which must be sustained beyond the election period.

He has also appealed to supporters of all parties to remain calm and remain united and avoid actions that could disrupt peace regardless of their political affiliation.

He has further called for peace and unity among the newly elected leaders, to achieve national development regardless of their political affiliation.

And Sub Chief Kajoba said the election period is over and it is time to develop the province and ensure it has a university and airport infrastructure development among others.

World.title: Mufulira Mayor ready to deliver
World.content:
Mufulira Mayor-Elect Tsindikai Mudemba has pledged to work closely with small-scale traders in the district to ensure that the town maintains high standards of cleanliness.

Mr Mudemba who stood on the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) ticket, stated that he greatly acknowledges and appreciates the hard work small-scale traders put into conducting their daily business.

He noted that rather than condemning street vending, he wants to work hand in hand with the vendors to ensure they maintain the town’s cleanliness.

Mr Mudemba explained that his plan involves actively engaging street vendors to reach a mutual agreement, requiring them to keep their trading spaces clean.

“Under this approach, vendors will clean up after themselves at the end of each day’s trading in a given area to ensure no litter remains on the street,” he said.

Mr Mudemba noted that it is important to embrace the traders, as vending serves as the primary livelihood for many vulnerable families and poor women.

Additionally, Mr Mudemba thanked the people of Mufulira district for having confidence in his leadership.

He stated that he is committed to being a servant of the people who listens to their needs, emphasising that he does not want to impose top-down plans for the district.

“I want to listen to the people as they are the ones who understand their needs best and I will work closely with the people,” Mr Mudemba said.

The Mayor pledged to ensure that the district remains clean and green, assuring the electorate that he is fully committed to fulfilling his campaign promises and not letting them down.

World.title: SC encourages Smart Office platform utilisation
World.content:
Secretary to the Cabinet, Patrick Kangwa, has directed all government institutions to prioritise the adoption and utilisation of the Smart Office Platform in their operations.

Mr Kangwa has further instructed the Smart Zambia Institute to submit a progress report to his office by end of October, on the onboarding of ministries, provinces, spending agencies, state-owned enterprises and other public institutions.

He has emphasised that the Smart Office Platform, a flagship digital government solution is designed to transform how public institutions conduct business, manage records, process workflows and deliver services.

Speaking during the handover of the Smart Office Management System to the Zambia Airports Corporation Limited (ZACL) in Chongwe, Mr Kangwa underscored digital transformation as a strategic imperative for national development.

“Ministries, provinces, spending agencies, state-owned enterprises and other public institutions are directed to work closely with the Smart Zambia Institute, towards accelerating the implementation of the smart office and other related digital government solutions”, the Secretary to the Cabinet stressed.

Speaking at the same event, Smart Zambia Institute National Coordinator, Percy Chinyama, explained that the platform will enable seamless workflow automation, secure electronic records management, paperless governance and improve transparency and accountability.

He noted that ZACL stands to benefit from significant operational cost savings by reducing expenditure on stationery, printing and manual records management.

“These benefits demonstrate the value of digital transformation in modernising institutional operations and enhancing organisational performance,” he said.

And ZACL Managing Director, Urvesh Desai, echoed similar sentiments, noting that the system would improve turnaround times while strengthening transparency and accountability at the institution.

He added that it would also support more efficient decision-making and enhance service delivery across the Corporation.

“Technology can only transform an organisation when its people are committed to making it work. I am happy to confirm that 100 percent of head office staff have been trained and 406 more in other stations will be trained by end of November 2026,” he disclosed.
