World.title: Georgian businessman Elizbarashvili charged over alleged threats
World.content:
Elizbarashvili charged with making threats

Prosecutors have charged businessman and animal rights activist Tamaz Elizbarashvili, who is known for his outspoken criticism of the government, with making threats. He is accused of an offence under Article 151, Part 1 of the Criminal Code, which carries a maximum prison sentence of one year.

According to Elizbarashvili’s lawyer, Lekso Svimonishvili, seven alleged victims are involved in the case. Prosecutors say Elizbarashvili threatened them and that they regarded the threats as genuine.

Svimonishvili said his client categorically rejected the charges and maintained that he was completely innocent.

What do investigators accuse Elizbarashvili of?

According to the Georgian Prosecutor’s Office, an investigation by the Interior Ministry established that at around 2340 on 30 August, Tamaz Elizbarashvili and one of the alleged victims encountered each other by chance at a restaurant in Tbilisi. A verbal altercation broke out over a comment Elizbarashvili had previously posted on social media about the individual and his family.

According to investigators, during the altercation Elizbarashvili threatened the alleged victim and the people accompanying him. In particular, he allegedly said he would not let the matter rest and would return in about 30 minutes, while demanding that they remain at the restaurant.

“Since the alleged victims knew that Tamaz Elizbarashvili possessed a weapon that could be used against them, they had reasonable grounds to fear for their lives and safety and therefore decided to leave the restaurant.

At around 0020, Tamaz Elizbarashvili returned to the scene intending to carry out his threat. He was armed and attempted to enter the restaurant, conspicuously keeping his hand on a weapon tucked into his waistband. He also continued to threaten and insult the alleged victims. Those who had not managed to leave and remained near the restaurant had reasonable grounds to fear that the threat would be carried out.

Despite being barred by security staff, Tamaz Elizbarashvili nevertheless entered the restaurant premises. After establishing that the alleged victims were no longer there, he left,” the Prosecutor’s Office said.

What does the lawyer say?

According to Elizbarashvili’s lawyer, prosecutors cite comments previously made by the businessman on social media as the reason for the confrontation. However, the defence says the indictment makes no mention of any personal conflict between Elizbarashvili and the alleged victims.

“Mr Tamaz does not admit guilt, and his account of what happened is radically different [from the one presented]. During the incident, he left his wife and children at home to shield them from any potential confrontation and returned alone, believing that if anyone had questions, they could put them to him in person. However, no-one was there when he arrived,” Svimonishvili said.

The case materials also refer to a firearm, although Elizbarashvili denies possessing one illegally. According to his lawyer, he has not at this stage been charged with the illegal acquisition, possession or carrying of a firearm.

Svimonishvili said the only firearm seized during a search of Elizbarashvili’s apartment was officially registered in his name and had been sent for forensic examination.

The defence will ask the court not to impose any pre-trial restrictions on Elizbarashvili. Alternatively, the lawyer will request that he be released on bail.

Prosecutors have not yet specified what pre-trial measure they will ask the court to impose.

Background

On 1 September 2026, Elizbarashvili was placed under administrative arrest for allegedly failing to comply with a lawful police order. His arrest followed searches of his car and home conducted as part of an investigation launched under Articles 151 (threats) and 236 (illegal acquisition, possession and carrying of firearms) of the Criminal Code.

Elizbarashvili said the complaint against him had been filed by employees of the Imedi TV channel, with whom he had a verbal altercation at a restaurant on 30 August. He alleged that the Imedi employees had initiated the confrontation and threatened him over his political views.

World.title: Ex-Georgian PM questioned in prison over his statements on a human rights defender who died by suicide
World.content:
Georgia: Gharibashvili questioned in Jorbenadze case

As part of the ongoing investigation into the death of Lazare Jorbenadze, law enforcement officers questioned former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili at Prison No. 12 in Rustavi on September 3.

Jorbenadze had publicly criticised current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze. Gharibashvili recently published a letter expressing doubts about the officially stated cause of the human rights defender’s death — suicide.

Following several hours of questioning, prosecutor Medea Tsiramua and Gharibashvili’s lawyer, Natia Tamazashvili, spoke to journalists.

Former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili was sentenced to five years in January 2026 for legalising illicit income on a particularly large scale. He pleaded guilty and reached a plea deal with the prosecution. On August 24, he was charged with a second offence — accepting a particularly large bribe. Gharibashvili denies the new charge.

What the lawyer and prosecutor said

How it started. On September 1, 2026, Irakli Gharibashvili published another letter from prison on social media, calling on government officials to answer questions about the true circumstances of Lazare Jorbenadze’s death. Gharibashvili pointed out that Jorbenadze, a former human rights defender, had criticised current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze in an article by journalist Dito Chubinidze and died by suicide shortly after its publication. Gharibashvili also noted that the newspaper Asaval-Dasavali, where the article was published, had publicly questioned the suicide theory.

According to the prosecution, Gharibashvili’s public suspicions about the circumstances of Jorbenadze’s death have no direct factual basis. The prosecutor said the former prime minister provided investigators with no new or significant information.

She said the questioning showed that Gharibashvili was neither a direct witness to Jorbenadze’s death nor someone with specific information about it.

“Gharibashvili’s public letters were based solely on information from various publications, rather than any specific facts. He categorically stated that he has no specific information about Lazare Jorbenadze’s suicide,” prosecutor Medea Tsiramua said.

Gharibashvili’s lawyer, Natia Tamazashvili, who is his wife’s sister, said the former prime minister’s questions arose after he read specific publications while in prison and later learned of Jorbenadze’s death.

“His questions arose after he was sent a letter containing an article by journalist Dito Chubinidze in Asaval-Dasavali. The article was critical of Irakli Kobakhidze. Gharibashvili later learned about Jorbenadze’s death, put the facts together and raised questions publicly. During the questioning, he repeated the same questions he had raised in his public letter,” the lawyer said.

According to the defence, Gharibashvili was not trying to provide investigators with previously unknown sources or information. His questions were based on suspicions about a possible connection between the articles published in the media and Jorbenadze’s sudden death.

Series of interrogations in the Lazare Jorbenadze case

Before Gharibashvili was questioned, politicians and public figures were questioned at the Digomi police headquarters in Tbilisi. They were asked about the former prime minister’s letter published on social media.

Investigators questioned Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the opposition coalition For Change, analyst Gia Khukhashvili and several activists.

Gvaramia said he had no information about the details of the case and knew only what had been published on social media.

Opposition politicians Khatia Dekanoidze and Tazo Datunashvili, as well as journalist Nanuka Zhorzholiani, refused to appear for questioning at the police station. They told investigators they would give evidence only in court, in the presence of a magistrate judge.

World.title: ‘If Russia decides to withdraw its military base, we will not object’ – Pashinyan
World.content:
Pashinyan on the withdrawal of Russia’s military base from Armenia.

“If Russia decides to withdraw its military base from Armenia, we will not object. But if they want to stay, we are ready to discuss that too,” Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said during his regular weekly briefing.

He also said Yerevan does not consider the presence of Russia’s 102nd military base in Armenia vital.

Putin raised the issue after his meeting with Pashinyan in Bishkek, although the Armenian prime minister says they did not discuss the issue either during those talks or before them. Putin said:

“If Armenia believes that Russia’s military base is not needed in Armenia, we will leave tomorrow if necessary. Is Armenia ready for that? Fine, we will not impose anything on anyone. But if the Armenian people want some kind of Russian military ‘wing’ there, we will stay. We will work and cooperate.”

Pashinyan also commented at the briefing on the issues he discussed with Putin in Bishkek. In particular, he once again explained Armenia’s position on its membership in the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union, Russia’s concession to operate Armenia’s railways and the construction of a new nuclear power plant.

Armenia cannot be forced to hold a referendum

“And who said that all EAEU member states swore allegiance and would remain members of the EAEU for their entire existence?”

That was Pashinyan’s answer to a question about Armenia’s membership in the Russian-led EAEU. He gave it among the first answers at the briefing. The issue also dominated the open part of the Pashinyan-Putin talks.

For several months, Russia has been calling at various levels for Armenia to hold a referendum on membership of the EAEU or the European Union. The Russian president also insisted on this at the meeting in Bishkek.

“The adoption of the law to begin Armenia’s accession to another organisation amounts to a declaration that it is leaving ours,”* Putin said.

Pashinyan explained to the Russian president, and repeated at the briefing, that under the union’s charter, a country must give six months’ notice before ending its membership. However, Armenia has no such intention for now.

He said he continues to explain this to his Russian partners, trying to make Armenia’s position “clearer and more acceptable”.

One journalist who raised the issue described Putin’s tone towards Pashinyan as “harsh”. He said Moscow was taking a tough line and forcing Yerevan to choose between the EAEU and the EU. Armenia’s prime minister replied:

“I am also giving the Russian president a tough choice. I say: this cannot continue, the issue of the railway concession must be resolved. Why is there no headline saying ‘Pashinyan gives Russian president a tough choice’?”

Pashinyan himself believes Armenian media do not use such headlines because the country still follows the “logic of subordination to the Central Committee of the USSR”. In his view, that logic produces the following reaction: “They called from Moscow, we urgently need to bring out the cognac.”

At the same time, the prime minister stressed his position: Armenia cannot be forced to hold a referendum.

He said the country’s Constitution requires a referendum before joining a supranational organisation. However, Armenia should hold one only when the issue “is ripe”. This would mean, in particular, when Armenia applies for EU membership or at least sets out its roadmap. Holding a referendum before that, he argued, would mean asking citizens to go to polling stations before anyone has formulated the question or decided what answers they can choose.

Selling the railway concession is the best solution

Pashinyan said he discussed the future of South Caucasus Railway with Putin. This issue is, incidentally, more important to the Armenian side. For a long time, Armenia’s authorities have been telling their Russian partners that the country is losing its competitive advantage in developing regional railway links because Russia controls the Armenian railway.

Since 2008, the company South Caucasus Railway has operated Armenia’s railway under a concession agreement. Russian Railways owns 100% of the company. The agreement grants the concession for 30 years. However, since 2008, freight traffic on Armenia’s railways has halved, some routes have stopped operating, and the investment commitments have remained unfulfilled.

The Armenian prime minister therefore proposed selling the concession to a third country that is friendly to both Armenia and Russia. Russian partners described the proposal as “strange and largely unacceptable”.

However, Pashinyan said the following about the outcome of his meeting with Putin:

“We reached an understanding that the current situation cannot continue for much longer. We need to resolve this issue somehow. Both Armenia and Russia understand that one possible solution would be to sell the concession rights to a third party acceptable to both Armenia and Russia. Frankly, I think this is the best solution. The other options seem unrealistic.”».

Moscow to present proposals for building a new nuclear power plant

According to Pashinyan, Rosatom CEO Alexei Likhachev will visit Armenia in September.

“He will present Armenia with proposals on what Russia can offer today for the construction of a new nuclear power plant. I have already said that we do not see the nuclear power plant as a geopolitical choice. We need the best value for money. We will go with whoever makes the best offer,” the prime minister said.

He said Armenia would consider all possible options, whether a small modular reactor proposed by Western partners or a conventional Russian nuclear power plant:

“We have never said that the Russian proposal cannot be the best one, including in terms of modular reactors. It is not the case that Russia has no proposal for modular reactors. However, there are a number of important factors: the price, the payback period, the construction time and the financing arrangements.”

Nikol Pashinyan said work on the issue had intensified and that Armenia should make a decision within a year.

He said Armenia initially favoured a small modular reactor, but “desire is one thing and reality is another”.

The problem is that experts are concerned about the lack of experience in building modular nuclear power plants and the potential risks.

According to the prime minister, if there are no operating or licensed modular nuclear power plants anywhere in the world when Armenia makes its decision, this will create “uncertainty” and make the decision very difficult.

At the same time, he said work was continuing to extend the operating life of the existing Metsamor nuclear power plant beyond 2036.

No plans to introduce visas for Russian citizens

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said that “if Armenia suddenly introduces visas as well, it will not introduce them against us — it will introduce them against its own citizens”. She also said the move would affect Russian citizens who have relatives in Armenia.

Importantly, no one in Armenia had suggested introducing a visa regime for Russian citizens before her statement.

“We have absolutely no such intention, and never have. It has never even crossed our minds. We are very happy to welcome tourists from Russia. We can see that they have now become very active in promoting Armenia’s tourism attractions. Society also welcomes these people. And they themselves seem to feel quite comfortable in Armenia. We are happy to have them, just as we are happy to welcome tourists from other countries,” the prime minister said.

Pashinyan on the withdrawal of Russia’s military base from Armenia

World.title: Georgian politicians questioned after ex-prime minister’s claims about Lazare Jorbenadze’s death
World.content:
Death of Georgian human rights defender Lazare Jorbenadze

Georgian politicians have been summoned for questioning over public statements by former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili about the death of Lazare Jorbenadze.

According to the Georgian Prosecutor’s Office, investigators have confirmed the suicide theory without ambiguity following investigative work into Jorbenadze’s death on 4 April 2026 and interviews with members of his family.

Nevertheless, because convicted former prime minister Irakli Garibashvili and others have made public statements about the case, investigators will question several political figures further: Irakli Garibashvili himself, Nika Gvaramia, Irma Inashvili, Nanuka Zhorzholiani, Khatia Dekanoidze, Tazo Datunashvili, Gia Khukhashvili, Giorgi Liluashvili, Zaza Davitaia and Ermile Nemsadze.

What happened

On 1 September 2026, former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili published another letter from prison. He called on the authorities to answer questions about the circumstances surrounding the death of Lazare Jorbenadze, a human rights defender who had criticised Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze.

Garibashvili writes that Jorbenadze died by suicide shortly after journalist Dito Chubinidze published an article based on an interview with him.

The newspaper Asaval-Dasavali, which published the interview, questioned the suicide theory. In his letter, Garibashvili stresses that the public should receive an answer about the true cause of Jorbenadze’s death.

The former prime minister says he decided to speak publicly about the issue after comparing the contents of a letter he received from government representatives in February with other circumstances.



Lazare Jorbenadze

According to Garibashvili, on 12 February, officials acting on the instructions of Irakli Kobakhidze and Deputy Prime Minister Mamuka Mdinaradze gave him an article that the newspaper Asaval-Dasavali had published on 2 February 2026.

The article featured a conversation between Dito Chubinidze and Lazare Jorbenadze. Garibashvili says it focused mainly on criticism of Kobakhidze and serious allegations against him.

The former prime minister says the message he received suggested that he was behind the article. “I received a message expressing the suspicion — based on a completely false assumption — that I was behind the article in question,” Garibashvili writes.

Garibashvili says he categorically rejected the accusation and told government representatives that he had never engaged in publishing “commissioned articles”.

What do politicians say?

Khatia Dekanoidze, one of the leaders of the United National Movement, said she would appear in court to testify in the Lazare Jorbenadze case. She said Bidzina Ivanishvili bears responsibility for the system he created, so investigators should question him as well.

“Bidzina Ivanishvili created a system in which people fight for positions and money, testify against each other, fabricate cases and, of course, are deeply involved in corruption. That is why Bidzina Ivanishvili, Kobakhidze, Mdinaradze and everyone who fabricates all sorts of dirt for money should be summoned for questioning. As for the investigation itself, I have made my position clear: I will go to court,” Dekanoidze said.

Political analyst Gia Khukhashvili said he did not understand why authorities had summoned him for questioning in the Lazare Jorbenadze death case, as he had made no specific statements about Jorbenadze and only learned of his existence after his death.

“I only learned of Jorbenadze’s existence after his death. I did not comment specifically on the situation involving Jorbenadze. I spoke more broadly about suicide cases that raise questions. Kobakhidze and Mdinaradze should be here instead of me, because Garibashvili named them, but they are not being summoned — I am. And now this has turned into nothing more than a tragicomedy,” Khukhashvili commented.

According to Nika Gvaramia, leader of the Coalition for Change, investigators did not ask him about any other subjects during his questioning in the Jorbenadze death case. Gvaramia believes the case may serve two purposes: one could be political propaganda, while the other could involve bringing new charges against the former prime minister.

“The next step, I am sure, will be to bring new charges against Garibashvili, under the article concerning illegal wiretapping. As far as I know, investigators are currently questioning him in prison. Mdinaradze and Kobakhidze should themselves be concerned about such allegations if they are true, although Garibashvili should also provide further explanations,” Gvaramia said after the questioning.

Death of Georgian human rights defender Lazare Jorbenadze

World.title: Social assistance is shrinking in Azerbaijan: Is poverty falling, or are low-income people losing support?
World.content:
Targeted social assistance in Azerbaijan

In Azerbaijan, the authorities have raised the income threshold for classifying families as low-income. It would be logical to expect this to increase both the number of people receiving assistance and the amount of support they receive. However, official statistics show the opposite trend: both the number of families receiving targeted state social assistance and the amount paid per person are falling.

According to the State Statistics Committee, as of 1 July, 349,300 people from 78,900 families received targeted social assistance. A year earlier, the system covered 353,300 people from 80,300 families. This means that over the year, the number of families receiving assistance fell by 1,400, while the number of recipients fell by 4,000.

The decline becomes even more striking over the longer term. In mid-2017, 498,400 people received this type of assistance. Over nine years, that figure fell by 149,100, or about 30%. Meanwhile, the country’s population increased during the same period.

These figures raise an important question: have the incomes of low-income families increased enough for them to no longer need social assistance, or has the system stopped reaching some people who still need support?

The income threshold has risen, but social assistance has fallen

Targeted social assistance is not a fixed payment. The authorities calculate it as the difference between the needs-based threshold for all family members and the family’s average monthly income. The calculation takes into account income from the previous 12 months.

In 2025, the needs-based threshold stood at 285 manats (approx. $167.65) per person. In 2026, the authorities raised it to 300 manats (approx. $176.50), an increase of 5.3%. Despite this, the average payment per person fell from 100.37 to 97.94 manats (approx. $59 to $57.70). In nominal terms, the payment fell by 2.43 manats (approx. $1.43), or 2.4%.

Applying the current formula to the average figures suggests that the system calculated recipients’ average monthly income per person at 184.63 manats (approx. $108.60) in 2025 and 202.06 manats (approx. $118.90) in 2026. This represents a nominal increase of 9.4%. Mathematically, the lower payments reflect the fact that, according to the system’s calculations, family incomes grew faster than the needs-based threshold.

However, these figures do not prove that the financial situation of all low-income families has improved. The average for families that remained in the system in mid-2026 is being compared with the average for families that received assistance a year earlier. Families whose payments stopped or whose applications were rejected no longer form part of the new average.

Our calculations, based on official data, show that total monthly payments to recipients fell from about 35.46 million (approx. $20.86 million) to 34.21 million manats (approx. $20.12 million). The government therefore reduced its monthly spending on this group by about 1.25 million manats (approx. $735,300), or 3.5%, in nominal terms.

The assistance has lost even more purchasing power

According to July 2026 data, annual inflation stood at 5.8%, while food inflation reached 7.3%. After taking price rises into account, the purchasing power of the 97.94-manat payment fell by about 7.8% compared with the 100.37-manat payment a year earlier. If we consider only food price increases, the decline approaches 9%.

After receiving assistance, the system brings a family’s calculated income per person up to the needs-based threshold of 300 manats. However, this represents only a 5.3% increase from last year’s level of 285 manats. That increase falls short of overall inflation and especially of food price growth. As a result, even the minimum income of families that remain in the social assistance system has not increased in real terms.

The number of people receiving assistance is not the number of people living in poverty

The State Statistics Committee’s final data for 2025 put the poverty line at 286 manats (approx. $168.20) and the poverty rate at 5.2%. With a population of 10.26 million, this amounts to roughly 534,000 people.

At the end of the same year, 336,000 people received targeted social assistance, or about 3.3% of the population. The authorities use different methodologies and reporting dates to calculate these figures, so we cannot directly compare them. Nevertheless, the gap of about 198,000 people clearly shows that the number of assistance recipients cannot serve as a measure of poverty in the country.

Moreover, earning less than 300 manats does not in itself qualify a person for assistance. Under the rules, a family must show that factors beyond its control have caused its low income. The official criteria allow authorities to reject an application if the family owns or uses a car, has two properties of the same type at different addresses, or has carried out purchase or sale transactions worth more than 12 times the subsistence minimum over the previous 12 months. Authorities can also reject an application if an able-bodied family member has turned down two suitable job offers.

Based on the 2026 subsistence minimum, the threshold for purchase and sale transactions stands at 3,600 manats (approx. $2,118). Authorities can also reject assistance if a family spends 45 manats (approx. $26.50) or more per person each month on utilities and communications. For a family of four, that amounts to 180 manats (approx. $106) in total. The authorities also count money and gifts from relatives, as well as estimated income from a household farm or garden, when calculating family income.

These criteria may help identify hidden income and assets. However, the same rules can exclude a family with a low cash income if it owns an old car, faces high utility bills or mainly survives on financial support from relatives.

The number of pensioners is falling, while more people receive age-related benefits

Another question arises when we examine other social security figures. On 1 July 2025, Azerbaijan had 1,103,300 pensioners. A year later, the figure had fallen to 1.1 million. At the same time, the average pension rose by 10.5% to 594.4 manats (approx. $350). However, the number of pensioners fell by 3,300.

Meanwhile, the number of people who do not qualify for a labour pension but receive a 220-manat age-related benefit (approx. $130) rose from 166,200 to 177,500. We cannot say that the changes in these two groups involve the same people. However, the fall in the number of pensioners as the elderly population grows, alongside the rise in recipients of a lower benefit, requires a separate explanation in terms of access to labour pensions.

What data the government should disclose

To treat a decline in the number of assistance recipients as evidence of falling poverty, we need more than one headline figure. The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection of the Population should report how many families entered the system over the past year, how many stopped receiving assistance, how many applicants faced rejection and why authorities rejected their applications.

The government should also report how many families failed to qualify under each criterion, including car ownership, purchase and sale transactions, utility costs, discrepancies in income data and refusal to accept an offered job. It should also disclose how many decisions authorities reviewed following complaints and what share of assistance recipients are children.

Without this data, we cannot conclude that poverty has fallen. So far, the official statistics show only this: the number of people covered by targeted social assistance has fallen, the average payment has declined in nominal terms, and its purchasing power has fallen even further.

Targeted social assistance in Azerbaijan

World.title: Uzbekistan’s Andijan unveils ambitious China-backed water, logistics plans
World.content:
Photo: the telegram channel of the Governor of Andijan region

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. Uzbekistan’s Andijan region and China’s CHINA CAMCE discussed several major investment and infrastructure projects, including a drinking water treatment plant, a main water pipeline, and a cross-border industrial and logistics center.

This was reflected in a statement by the Governor of Andijan Region on his Telegram channel, following a video meeting between Governor Shuhratbek Abdurahmonov and Wang Bo, chairman of CHINA CAMCE.

According to the information, among the proposals discussed was building a drinking water treatment plant with a capacity of 100,000 cubic meters per day at the Kampirovot water intake facility. The sides also considered building an 81.4-kilometer main water pipeline along the Khanabad-Asaka route.

Another proposal involves establishing the Andijan Transboundary Industrial, Trade and Logistics Center, which is intended to support industrial, trade and logistics activity in the region.

"Views were also exchanged on the modernization of Andijan city's wastewater treatment facilities and the construction of a modern central stadium in Babur city," the statement said.

The projects reflect Andijan’s efforts to attract investment into water infrastructure, urban utilities, logistics and public facilities while strengthening cooperation with Chinese companies.

The sides exchanged views on the proposed projects and discussed measures needed to move them toward implementation. They agreed to expand cooperation and define practical steps for advancing the initiatives.

CHINA CAMCE is a Chinese engineering and infrastructure company involved in the development and implementation of large-scale projects in international markets. Its participation in the proposed Andijan projects could contribute to the modernization of the region’s water and urban infrastructure and the development of new trade and logistics capacity.

World.title: Kazakhstan approves $700-MW power plant project in Kurchatov
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. The Kazakh Government has approved an investment agreement with Kurchatov GRES LLP for the construction of a 700-MW thermal power plant in Kurchatov, Abai region.

This was announced by the press service of the Kazakh government.

According to the information, the agreement was approved as part of the implementation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s instructions to develop coal-fired power generation. The relevant resolution was signed by Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov.

"The project is expected to become a key part of Kurchatov’s energy infrastructure, where major scientific facilities are concentrated, including the National Nuclear Center, Nuclear Technology Park, research reactors, laboratories and Kazakhstan’s KTM thermonuclear tokamak. The total cost of the project is estimated at 881 billion tenge. The plant will comprise two 350-MW power units, with commissioning planned in stages by 2032,'" the government’s press service said.

Once fully operational, the plant is expected to generate up to 5 billion kWh of electricity annually and create around 4,400 jobs.

According to the government, the plant will be equipped with modern steam-power equipment designed to operate at elevated pressure and temperature parameters, using clean-coal technologies.

The project will also include gas-cleaning, emissions filtration, and dust-suppression systems to reduce environmental impact in line with Kazakhstan’s Environmental Code and best available techniques requirements.

"The implementation of the project will improve the reliability and quality of electricity supply to Kurchatov and provide additional generating capacity for the further development of scientific, industrial and urban infrastructure," the government said.

World.title: Baku to host 4th Climate Week of UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. The fourth Climate Week (CW4) of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) will be held in Baku on September 7–11, 2026, hosted by the Republic of Azerbaijan and organized by the Azerbaijani Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Baku Climate Action Week 2026 (BCAW 2026) will also be held on the same dates.

Having become an important international platform for the climate agenda, Baku will host discussions on the practical implementation of climate decisions, the expansion of international cooperation, and further strengthening global climate action ahead of COP31 as part of these events.

Representatives of governments and international organizations, experts, financial institutions, the private sector, and civil society from various countries are expected to attend the events.

The fourth Climate Week and Baku Climate Action Week will feature a series of sessions, panel discussions, and other events focusing on climate change, climate finance, sustainable development, and accelerating climate action.

The events will further strengthen Baku’s active role in the global climate agenda and make an important contribution to strengthening international climate cooperation ahead of COP31.

The events will be held at the Baku Convention Center.

World.title: VDMA identifies agriculture as key area for German machinery in Kyrgyzstan (Exclusive)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 5. Agricultural machinery, food processing, and packaging are currently the most promising areas for German machinery and industrial technologies in Kyrgyzstan, the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA) told Trend.

"From the viewpoint of the German mechanical engineering industry, Kyrgyzstan remains a small but gradually developing market. At present, the most promising areas for German machinery and industrial technologies appear to be agricultural machinery, food processing, and the packaging industry," VDMA said in response to questions.

The association also sees potential for deeper cooperation in other segments of Kyrgyzstan’s industrial sector.

"There is also potential for deeper cooperation in other segments of industry, including the mining and construction sector," VDMA added.

Meanwhile, Kyrgyzstan has a significant agricultural sector, which remains one of the key areas of the country’s economy. The government is focusing on increasing the level of agricultural mechanization, upgrading the machinery fleet and introducing modern technologies in agricultural production and processing.

The country is also taking steps to develop its processing industry, including food production. Expanding production capacity and introducing modern technologies are seen as important measures to increase value added and strengthen export potential.

In addition, Kyrgyzstan has significant mineral resources, supporting interest in the development of its mining sector. At the same time, projects in construction and infrastructure are creating additional opportunities for suppliers of industrial equipment and technologies.

World.title: Melbourne soccer club says girls' match moved to make way for boys
World.content:
A Melbourne soccer club is taking a stand amid claims one of its junior girls' team's matches was stopped at half-time, with players forced to take to an inferior pitch to make way for a boys' team.

In a statement on social media, the Boroondara Eagles Football Club said an under-12 girls' match at Caloola Reserve, in Oakleigh, was halted so that an under-11 boys' team could use the field.

"After a lengthy delay [40 minutes], the girls were directed to an alternative field that was substantially different to the original playing surface, waterlogged and unsafe, resulting in the match being abandoned," the club posted on Facebook.

The club said it was deeply concerned about the impact the July 12 incident had on its players, families and coaching staff.

"One of our young female coaches left the venue in tears, and many players and parents were left questioning why a girls' points match was not afforded the same protection and importance as the u11 boys fixture?"

The club has declined to participate in a rescheduled fixture against Monash City Villarreal FC scheduled for tomorrow.

It has asked Football Victoria (FV) to investigate the incident and clarify whether the events constituted gender discrimination under its policies and frameworks.

In a statement this morning, FV said it acknowledged the concerns raised, and "the distress caused to the players, coaches and families involved".

"The matter is now being handled through FV's formal Member Protection process. To ensure it is considered fairly, FV can not comment further while that process is underway," the statement said.

"FV is also reviewing the expectations on clubs regarding match-day decisions, communication regarding abandonments, pitch use, fixture clashes and referee support to identify any improvements required.

"We remain committed to ensuring women and girls feel valued, respected and supported at every level of the game."

The football club said on social media that it had lodged the matter with Football Australia's core integrity team, and with the City of Monash, which runs Caloola Reserve.

The Boroondara Eagles said they remained committed to respectful participation in football and the continued growth of the women's and girl's game.

"Our position is that no player should ever feel that their match, their team or their opportunity to participate is less important because they are girls."

World.title: Teen guilty of 'heinous' murder loses sentence appeal
World.content:
A Brisbane teenager convicted of the violent murder of a man with a large hunting knife has had his bid to reduce his time behind bars rejected.

The teenager, who previously admitted to being "addicted to stabbing", pleaded guilty to attacking 19-year-old Abddullahi Ahmed Iyow in the arm, hand and leg and three times in the stomach and abdomen at Acacia Ridge in May 2024.

He was 17 at the time of the attack and can't be named under Queensland's youth justice laws.

Police at the crime scene in Acacia Ridge, in Brisbane's south, in 2024. (ABC News: Victoria Pengilley)

Police said the pair had been walking together to a park when they got into a fight, with the killer later admitting to police that he stabbed Mr Ahmed Iyow for smashing his phone earlier in the day.

He told them the damage to his phone had caused him to lose his drug dealing contacts.

Teen sentenced for murder of friend A teenage boy who attacked his friend with a hunting knife for "no legitimate reason" was "addicted to stabbing", a court has heard.

According to a court judgment, the teenager said Mr Ahmed Iyow "deserved that shit", he "should have done it earlier" and that he hoped the victim had learned his lesson.

He said "did not give a f***" if the victim died because he had "disrespected him".

Mr Ahmed lyow was rushed to hospital soon after the attack for emergency surgery and was placed on life support, but died on June 18 as a result of his injuries.

Attack 'particularly heinous'

In April 2025 a judge sentenced the teenager to 12 years' imprisonment, requiring him to serve at least 70 per cent before he could be released.

He concluded that attack had been "particularly heinous" due to it being effectively unprovoked.

During the hearing, Abddullahi Ahmed Iyow's brother allegedly grabbed a pen from a lawyer's desk and lunged at the teenager, causing minor injuries to his back.

The teenager, who cannot be named, was sentenced in the Supreme Court last year. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

The 22-year-old was charged with assault occasioning bodily harm.

At the time, Mr Ahmed lyow's family said their lives had been "shattered" by the brutal attack, which had "cruelly stolen" the life of a "vibrant teenager with his whole life ahead of him".

'Addicted to stabbing'

According to a psychiatrist report tendered in court, the teenage killer had described stabbing people as "joyful", saying it felt good and he was "addicted to stabbing because of my past trauma".

It said in the two days leading up to the stabbing, he had been consuming alcohol, Xanax, cannabis and codeine syrup, a psychiatrist report stated.

While he had no official criminal history, the teenager admitted to being involved in previous gang-related crimes, including a kidnapping that had not come to police attention.

The psychiatrist concluded he had a severe conduct disorder with "antisocial personality traits", PTSD, oppositional defiance towards his family and authority, and met the criteria for having an intellectual disability.

The report said the teenager was also at above-average risk of carrying out another violent offence.

Sentence kept

In July this year, the teenager applied to the Court of Appeal to reduce the length of his sentence, arguing it was not a "particularly heinous" crime, as the sentencing judge had found at the time.

The application argued the judge had failed to consider the steps the teenager had since taken to rehabilitate himself, and that requiring him to serve 70 per cent of his 12-year sentence was "manifestly excessive".

However, this week Court of Appeal justices David Boddice, Shane Doyle and Debra Mullins AO jointly refused the application and upheld his original sentence.

World.title: What could happen next as Clancy triple-murder case declared a mistrial
World.content:
The six-week criminal trial of Lindsay Clancy has collapsed without a verdict, with the judge declaring a mistrial.

Warning: This story contains details of a crime that may be distressing for some readers.

The Massachusetts mother was charged with three counts of first-degree murder over the deaths of her three children at their Boston home on January 24, 2023.

But after weeks of conflicting testimony, jurors were unable to reach a consensus.

Here is what to know about what comes next.

First, catch me up

The trial was to determine whether Ms Clancy was criminally guilty of her children's murders.

While she did not deny killing her children, her defence team argued she had been suffering from postpartum psychosis after the birth of her youngest son and should not be held criminally responsible.

They said the condition left her "begging for help" and spiralling for months.

The prosecution argued she was a "functioning" mother who meticulously planned the murders.

Ms Clancy was facing life in prison without parole if convicted, while a not guilty verdict would have seen her committed to a state mental health facility.

What is postpartum psychosis? Read more Read more Postpartum psychosis is a rare mental illness linked to the stress, sleep deprivation and hormonal changes that follow childbirth, affecting roughly one in 1,000 women after giving birth. It often occurs in the first few days or weeks after the birth, and women with a prior diagnosis of bipolar disorder are at a higher risk. Centre of Perinatal Excellence (COPE) spokesperson Nicole Highet told the ABC in August that the condition could cause sufferers to experience hallucinations or delusions. "Typically, we think of the person being disconnected from reality and having those symptoms on an ongoing basis," Dr Highet said. "But the tricky thing with postpartum psychosis is that these symptoms can sort of wax and wane. "You might one moment be presenting quite well and then have these delusions or hallucinations." Looking for help or worried about someone you know? COPE has resources for new, hopeful and expectant parents via their website or on their directory. Ready to COPE is a free weekly guide to prepare and support parents through pregnancy and early parenthood, including issues often stigmatised.

On the day the children were killed, Patrick Clancy, Ms Clancy's then-husband, returned home from running errands to find her lying paralysed in their backyard, having attempted to take her own life by jumping from their second-storey bedroom window.

He found their two eldest children dead from strangulation in the family basement. Their youngest, who was eight months old at the time, died in hospital a few days later.

The televised trial spanned six weeks and heard more than four weeks of witness testimony, reviving long-standing debates about how postpartum mental health is treated in the US.

US mum on trial for murder says voice told her to 'kill the children' A mother who says she was suffering postpartum psychosis when she killed her three children and attempted to take her own life is now on trial for their murder.

But the 12-person jury, which was made up of nine women and three men, was unable to reach a unanimous verdict after deliberating for almost 40 hours.

It was revealed in court that the jury had complained that one among them had refused to follow the law on "reasonable doubt".

It is not clear exactly how the jury reached an impasse, but Kevin Reddington, a defence lawyer for Ms Clancy, suggested the lone juror stood in the way of an acquittal.

"They know they were robbed by one man, for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful," he said outside the courthouse.

"You could see how defeated they were sitting there. I got a funny feeling they would have gone on for another week if they had to. So I hope that guy can sleep well at night."

Judge William Sullivan said on Friday, local time, he had "no choice" but to declare a mistrial.

Loading...

What does a mistrial mean?

A mistrial is when a trial ends without a verdict.

It does not mean the case is closed, though, and prosecutors are free to start a new trial with a new jury.

Will the prosecution retry Clancy?

Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz told reporters after the mistrial that no decision had been made on whether prosecutors would retry the case, but that his goal was always "getting justice for those three little babies".

Timothy Cruz says it is not yet decided whether the prosecution will continue its case against Lindsay Clancy. (AP: Charles Krupa)

Still, New York Law School professor Heather Ellis Cucolo told the Associated Press that prosecutors would need to weigh several factors, including the potential expense and the likely outcome.

"I know the prosecutor stated openly that he would not allow public opinion to sway his decision, which is accurate, but the prosecution serves the public," she said.

"If it is believed that justice must be served by another trial, that is something the prosecutor's office will take into account and weigh very heavily."

Mr Reddington also noted it would be difficult to find another set of jurors, given the level of attention the first trial garnered.

"I don't know if we will ever be able to get jurors that aren't aware of this case anywhere," he said.

"New York, Washington, Georgia, Japan, India, I don't know anywhere."

Jurors need to start a trial with little to no outside knowledge of a case to ensure a fair and impartial trial.

Lindsay Clancy watched on as the judge declared a mistrial. (Reuters: Greg Derr/Pool )

Boston-based defence lawyer Randy Gioia, who was not involved in the trial, told the Associated Press that in his view, prosecutors should not put Ms Clancy through another trial.

"Why put everyone through the trauma again: 16 to 18 jurors, all the witnesses, Patrick Clancy," he said.

"What's to be served here when we've had a long trial and long deliberations? You don't have a strong case. You almost lost the case."

So, what happens now?

Mr Sullivan has set a hearing for September 29 at which time Mr Reddington will likely ask him to declare Ms Clancy not guilty, though such a request is believed to be unlikely to succeed.

It's also where prosecutors could reveal whether they will move to put Ms Clancy on trial again.

Prosecutors could also choose to seek a plea deal or drop the case entirely.

Ms Clancy has been confined at a state psychiatric hospital before and during the trial. She would remain in custody through a second trial.

World.title: Harley Reid opens up on celebrity, free kicks and the AFL's 'WA tax'
World.content:
Harley Reid was living in the spotlight even before he was an AFL player.

In his draft year, the then-17-year old was the centre of intense debate about where he would end up playing, and since his debut with West Coast in 2024 the now 21-year old is still the centre of attention everywhere he goes.

"I think that's probably still something I'm trying to work on. It is hard, don't get me wrong," Reid told 102.5 ABC Perth's SportsTalk program.

"I've been lucky enough to get out of Perth a few times, go camping or whatnot, to reset.

"It is probably something I'm still trying to get my head around and understand."

Reid has produced a stunning season, averaging more than 24 disposals per game. (Getty Images: Paul Kane)

Such was the hype around his arrival in Western Australia, the state's daily paper featured him 25 times on its back page — before he had played a game.

No player before or since has been more hyped prior to their debut.

"You do definitely notice it but I just try not to let it affect me too much," Reid said after being awarded the Geoff Christian Medal as the ABC's best WA-based player.

Harley Reid was awarded the Geoff Christian medal for the 2026 season. (ABC News)

"I feel like you do get that pressure, but I feel like if my mental state's there and I've prepared well, the pressure isn't there.

"I know I've done the work. It's all about that preparation as well."

Paying the 'WA Tax'

Reid was crowned West Coast club champion on Friday night when he claimed the John Worsfold Medal and is coming off his best season, but Eagles fans will have to wait until round three in 2027 to see the midfielder in action.

West Coast unsuccessfully challenged his two-game suspension for a dangerous tackle on Hawthorn's Jai Newcombe.

"It's that WA tax. If I was playing in Victoria I reckon we'd have had a different outcome," Reid quipped.

"I was pretty disappointed with the outcome."

Reid plays the game on the edge, but is trying to rein in some of his off-the-ball antics. (Getty Images: Paul Kane)

It was the latest controversy for Reid, who has given away more free kicks than any other player by this stage of their career.

He also holds the Eagles' record for free kicks conceded in a season.

"I think playing with aggression and bringing that competitive edge is a big part of my game," Reid said.

"I feel at times, me playing on the edge compared to other players, I feel like I've been targeted a lot more in different areas.

"It's just about making sure I'm using my aggression in the right areas and winning the contest, tackling hard and competing for the footy without letting it take me away from my job."

Doing the extra work

Reid is one of the Eagles young stars that the club hopes, along with the likes of Willem Duursma and Reuben Ginbey, will lead them back to the top of the AFL mountain.

The Eagles hope Willem Duursma and Reid are the young stars that will lead them back to the AFL Finals. (Getty Images: James Wiltshire)

And they are doing everything they can to do just that, including establishing the Matt Priddis Academy, named in honour of the 2014 Brownlow medallist, which sees the first-to-fourth year players do a session together each week.

"That's created a great camaraderie between the group and I think it's going to hold us in good stead for the years to come," Reid said.

"For us, it's extra education, extra skills for our mental and physical [sharpness] and just more of the game plan so we keep filtering it through.

"Sometimes it's harder to learn in a massive group so it's just more bringing that group closer together and making sure that education and knowledge that gets passed through is getting soaked into us."

World.title: Explosion at Bolivia military base kills at least 10
World.content:
At least 10 people have been killed and dozens more were injured after an explosion at a military barracks in the Bolivian municipality of Viacha, about 30 kilometres from La Paz.

Loading...

The blast occurred about 2:30pm on Friday, in an area used to store pyrotechnic material, local authorities said.

While the cause has yet to be established, officials say the blast originated from the defence ministry's fireworks stockpile.

Viacha health director Rita Nebraska told local media that between 10 and 15 people were believed to have died in the incident, while 62 people were injured.

Fourteen of the wounded were transferred to hospitals in La Paz, including a girl with third-degree burns, she said.

Police said more than 50 people were injured and dozens of homes damaged, largely by windows shattered in the blast.

Firefighters are warning that there is a chance of another explosion, due to a lingering heat source at the site. (AFP: APG Noticias)

Ambulances, medical teams and police were deployed to the military complex to assess the damage and evacuate the wounded to health centres.

The shockwave from the explosion shattered windows and structurally damaged dozens of nearby civilian homes.

Nebraska said firefighters had warned that a heat source remained at the site, raising the risk of another explosion.

Local residents near La Paz felt the impact of the blast. (Reuters: Red Siglo XXI)

She urged residents to stay at least 150 metres away.

Bolivia is a landlocked nation located in central South America, bordered by Brazil, Peru, Chile, Argentina, and Paraguay.

It has a diverse population of about 12 million people.

Reuters/ABC

World.title: Devils VFL season ends after loss in first ever home finals clash
World.content:
The finals dream has ended for the Tasmania Devils in their inaugural VFL season, going down by 27 points in a slippery match against Essendon in North Hobart.

A win today would have secured Tasmania a place in a VFL preliminary final.

Tasmania Devils daring to dream The Devils weren't supposed to make the VFL finals. They were barely even supposed to be in the league.

Essendon got to a strong start early in the match, though the Devils worked to narrow the gap to just 8 points going in to the second half.

However, the Dons, who were on a seven-game win streak, proved too strong to overcome, finishing with 101 points to the Devils' 74.

Optimism on dreary day

As gates opened at North Hobart on Saturday, the enthusiasm from fans decked out in green, donning raincoats and racing to get undercover seats, wasn't to be dampened.

Lee and Lucy Edwards have full confidence the Devils have what it takes to get a win over the Bombers. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

For Lee and Lucy Edwards, there was nowhere else they would rather have been.

"I don't care — rain, hail or shine, let's go," Ms Edwards said before the match.

"We played really well earlier in the year in York park when it rained cats and dogs, and we got over the line there."

Mr Edwards said for the club to make it this far in their first season was an achievement in itself.

" For a new team, this is fantastic. Tassie go on, come on! "

Decked out in her beanie and wet weather gear, Devils fan Ann Sigley was hoping she had a secret weapon with her in the stands — a bear in hand-knitted kit, named "mini Rum'un".

She said it took her four days to make the mini mascot, which is just one in her AFL collection.

Ann Sigley spent several months making a little Rum'un to show support for the Devils. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

"He shouts loud," she said, with a smile. "Goes up in the air a few times."

Among the sea of green, there were a few flickers of red and black. One of the brave Bombers supporters was Wynyard man Manassa Walker.

He said he was feeling confident going into the match, with the Essendon side including 18 AFL listed players, including former Devil, Jackson Artemis.

Manassa Walker from Wynyard is not scared to be surrounded by a sea of green and hopes the Bombers come away with a win. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

Mr Walker said, with a few Wynyard boys in the Tassie side he would also be barracking for them, but ultimately he was a "bomber at heart".

It was a similar sentiment shared by James Rogerson, who, wearing a Devils jumper and a Bombers scarf, was in for a win either way.

"I think football wins for the day," he said.

The dreary weather wasn't enough to stop droves of passionate supporters attending the clash. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

He said the Devils making it into a semi final, played at home, was a feat in itself.

"It's well above expectations, I think.

"They're doing really well. They've really gelled together as a team after only one pre-season together. I think they're doing really well."

Sophie Davis is among the thousands of Tasmanians supporting the Devils at North Hobart Oval today. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

For the young Davis family, watching their team was the perfect way to start the morning.

Daughter Sophie said she never doubted that the Devils would make it to to the semi finals.

"Of course. They're the Devils!"

World.title: Ambulance system incident not a failure, QAS says amid claims of late arrivals
World.content:
NationalQueenslandQueensland Health Ambulance system incident not a failure, QAS says amid claims of late arrivals Dominique Tassell Updated September 5, 2026 — 3:28pm ,first published 2:08pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Queensland Ambulance Services have said it is inaccurate to describe this week’s incident as a system failure, as politicians continue to clash over its impacts. The QAS’ computer-aided dispatch (CAD) system was upgraded on Thursday, but resulted in staff having to manually relay important information to ambulances by radio. Health Minister Tim Nicholls. Courtney Kruk Triple Zero calls were not impacted and QAS said it has not received any reports of adverse impacts to patients from the transition. A QAS spokesperson said Queenslanders can be confident they will receive ambulance services if they call Triple Zero.



“Our systems are working as intended following the transition to our new CAD system,” they said. “All Triple Zero calls are being answered and resources are being dispatched in a timely manner, with the most urgent cases prioritised.” The possible impact on the system during the transition was anticipated and accounted for, the QAS spokesperson said. Loading “Business continuity processes were enacted during the transition … this included rostering additional staff and validating all incidents to ensure they received an appropriate response,” they said.



While there have been reports in the media of ambulances arriving significantly late or not arriving at all, health minister Tim Nicholls said this was completely untrue. “There was an alternative system in the event that the changeover didn’t go exactly according to plan,” Nicholls said. Nicholls said it was “absolutely disingenuous and really quite despicable” for the state opposition to claim services were impacted. “We’re not aware of any reports that anyone has made that they’ve had to drive themselves because they were unable to get through to Triple Zero,” he said. “Now, there might be people who called through and weren’t either a category one, two, or three. That might be the normal course of events, but certainly nothing as a result of the changeover in the system has led to that delay that I’m aware of.”



Nicholls said QAS staff are used to the manual system and it was regularly used during updates to the old system. However, the state opposition has maintained the incident was more serious than is being communicated, claiming that ambulances became stuck in a queue due to dispatch issues and could not reach people quickly. Opposition leader Steven Miles once again slammed the state government for the system failure on Saturday. Opposition Leader Steven Miles said the state government is not being truthful about a QAS systems incident on Thursday (file photo). William Davis “We’re calling for a full investigation, a full review of what went wrong with the systems upgrade, why they weren’t able to roll back to the legacy system that was stable and working, and what they will put in place to ensure that this never happens again,” Miles said.



“The people talking to us say that they have never experienced a shutdown of the dispatch system like what occurred this week. “[Premier] David Crisafulli once said that ambulances not arriving on time was incomprehensible in a modern Queensland, but it is precisely what we’ve seen this week under this. “And yet the government and the ambulance service seems determined to not tell Queenslanders how many people waited for an ambulance, how many people never had, how many people were so sick and in such pain that they drove themselves to hospital rather than wait for an ambulance that. “It’s about time the health minister came clean with Queenslanders about what really happened during the week with ambulance dispatches.” Nicholls labelled these comments appalling, and said he would not stand for the opposition labelling QAS liars.



“Labor’s shameful efforts to politicise this much-needed system upgrade shows just how little respect they have for our hardworking paramedics and QAS staff,” he said. “After a decade of decline, Labor left the QAS with outdated legacy systems that were not fit-for-purpose, following their decision to disband the Public Sector Business Agency.” On Saturday morning, Miles said Queenslanders are rightly very proud of our ambulance service. “Our Ambos do a fantastic job,” he said. “People come from around the world to see how the Queensland Ambulance Service operates, but we need to keep it that way.



“These kinds of rushed system upgrades that have caused the outage on Thursday will only cause Queenslanders to doubt the quality of their ambulance service.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: Munster set to test value on open market after stalling on Storm offer
World.content:
Key points Eels five-eighth turns down Bulldogs to stick with Parramatta

Newcastle close in on new Dom Young deal

Knights prop Saifiti receives four-game ban

Cameron Munster is poised to test his value on the open market after informing Melbourne he won’t immediately be accepting the club’s two-year extension offer. Munster will become one of the highest-profile free agents on November 1, the date players coming off contract at the end of 2027 can begin fielding offers from opposition clubs. Munster’s management informed the Storm of Munster’s decision, but the Victorian club remains hopeful of retaining his services. Cameron Munster is weighing up his future after more than a decade at the Storm. Getty Images Munster was granted permission to negotiate with PNG, although the Chiefs opted to put talks on hold in case the likes of Nathan Cleary, Sam Walker and Zane Harrison became available. The Maroons and Kangaroos star has also been linked to Perth, but the Bears haven’t given him any consideration given he is not yet a free agent. The Broncos have been mooted as a potential destination, while several other clubs will be watching the situation with interest.



Munster last month said his chances of staying at Melbourne hinged on whether coach Craig Bellamy would continue in the role. Bellamy confirmed he will coach again in 2027, but gave a strong indication it would be his last year with the clipboard. ‘We’re in the risk business’: How Isaah Yeo got to the brink of a remarkable comeback Dan Walsh Panthers coach Ivan Cleary “wouldn’t have even bothered” pushing most players through the recovery Penrith co-captain Isaah Yeo is attempting as he edges closer to a remarkable four-week comeback from a pectoral tear. Isaah Yeo trains this week ahead of a possible return on Sunday. Panthers Digital



Cleary acknowledged on Friday that “we’re in the risk business” as Yeo prepares to undergo fitness and range-of-motion tests on the right pectoral he injured against the Warriors in round 23. The 31-year-old will be put through his paces in a Friday night training session and again on Saturday morning and is, according to his coach, “definitely a chance” of playing limited minutes from the bench in Sunday’s dead-rubber clash against Wests Tigers. While most pec ruptures are treated with surgery and a typical 10-12 week recovery timeframe, Yeo and the Panthers targeted a pre-finals hit out against the Tigers as an ambitious first checkpoint in a best-case rehabilitation plan for the star No.13. Even if Yeo is kept on ice this week, his likely availability for the finals is a huge boost for the premiership-heavyweights as Cleary marvelled at the Australian, NSW and Penrith captain’s resilience. “I think it’s fair to say we wouldn’t have even bothered [attempting Yeo’s rehabilitation] with a lot of players based on their experience and age,” Cleary said.



“Every situation is different. But I think the main thing is he was always on board with it and at any stage if he wasn’t, then we would have just pulled it.” Cleary conceded there are elements and movements of a game that cannot necessarily be replicated in training and fitness tests without risking the injury, particularly for a middle player like Yeo, who regularly plays 70-plus minutes and averages more than 35 tackles a match. Will Panthers captain Isaah Yeo suit up on Sunday? NRL Imagery “We’ve tried to give him as many of those scenarios as we can in training,” Cleary said. “There’s going to be some things happening in a game that we’re not quite sure about. But we feel like our process has been rigorous enough to at least get him to make the decisions [on his fitness] well. “We’re not talking about a five-game rookie here… If he gets through the next few days, then he’s ready to give it a shot, anyway”.



While Yeo pushes to return, hooker Mitch Kenny is a confirmed starter against the Tigers in his first game since suffering a badly broken leg in mid-April. Cleary, meanwhile, also gave special thanks to the Warriors after he and his family were welcomed by the rival club to watch son Jett’s memorable NRL debut last Sunday against Newcastle. Jett, Ivan and Nathan Cleary. Getty Images Cleary’s comments marked an easing of recent tensions between the two premiership favourites. Penrith had been unimpressed that the Warriors had initially baulked at granting Jett’s early release request to join the Panthers, where he will play under Ivan in his final season as coach next year. Penrith had granted James Fisher-Harris a compassionate grounds release with no questions asked when he had wanted to return to New Zealand in 2025.



“It was an awesome day,” Cleary said, having tried not to envisage potentially coaching against his youngest son in a finals clash. “I want to say thanks to the Warriors, they really looked after us as a family, and they’ve done a great job with Jett, too… I wouldn’t have supported him going to any other club, I don’t think. “I trust those guys [Warriors coach Andrew Webster and assistant David Tangata-Toa] implicitly. It’s a great club on the rise. I think they’ve done a great job with him, and I’m very thankful that they’ve allowed him to come back”. ‘Earned this opportunity’: Volkman signs new Eels deal Adrian Proszenko



Parramatta have re-signed Ronald Volkman, who turned down Canterbury to jostle with incoming recruit Jarome Luai for the No.6 jersey next season. Volkman has signed a two-year contract extension after a sparkling run of form alongside captain and halfback Mitchell Moses. Ronald Volkman has earned a new Eels deal. Getty Images The former Warriors playmaker is one of the most improved players in the NRL this season, and his form piqued the interest of the Bulldogs. It appeared the impending arrival of PNG-bound Tigers star Luai at the Eels for a one-year stopover in 2027 would result in Volkman leaving the blue and golds. However, the parties have come back to the negotiating table to ensure the 24-year-old stays put until at least the end of 2028. Luai is currently on a deal worth $1.2 million at the Tigers, while Volkman is playing well above his annual pay cheque of just $150,000. The latter has earned an increase in his new deal, but still represents great value for money for the rebuilding Eels.



“The positive environment which [coach] Jason Ryles has created at the club has provided some stability for Ronald where he is playing his best football of his career,” said Parramatta general manager of football Mark O’Neill. “He has earned this opportunity with some wonderful individual and team performances, and he will only continue to improve.” Elsewhere, Perth have confirmed the signing of Bulldogs winger Jonathan Sua on a three-year deal. “This is a massive opportunity for me, and I can’t wait to get started,” Sua said. “Being part of a brand-new club, building something from the very first day, isn’t something a lot of players get the chance to do. I want to make the most of it and show what I can do on a bigger stage.



“I’ve worked really hard over the last few seasons to get to this point, and I feel like my footy is in a really good place right now. I know there’s still so much more improvement in my game. I’m ready to put in the work to become the best winger I can be.” Las Vegas combine winner exits Knights as Young closes in on new deal Chris Barrett, Adrian Proszenko Las Vegas combine winner Marcus D’Acre has left Newcastle to sign with Israel Folau’s former team in Japanese rugby as the Knights close in on a new long-term deal for prolific winger Dominic Young. Newcastle are about to embark on their fifth finals series in seven years, rebounding from the wooden spoon last season under new coach Justin Holbrook.



Young, who has scored 20 tries in 23 appearances, has starred in his second season back in the Hunter and the parties are close to finalising a deal that will keep him in Newcastle until at least the end of 2030 While the 25-year-old is going nowhere, D’Acre has quietly departed after being granted a release. Marcus D’Acre in action for Newcastle against Penrith in the NSW Cup this season. NRL Photos A Hong Kong and Canada rugby representative at under-age level, he arrived at the Knights on a two-year contract after impressing talent scouts during the NRL’s week-long exhibition in the United States in 2025. World.content:

Warning: This story contains images and the name of a deceased Indigenous person. To the boxing world, Anthony “Tony” William Mundine was a champion without peer. As the only fighter to hold Australian titles across four weight divisions — middleweight, light heavyweight, cruiserweight and heavyweight — in the 1970s and 1980s, Mundine occupied rare air. Anthony “Tony” William Mundine’s casket leaves Redfern Oval on Saturday. James Brickwood But to his loved ones, he was much more: he was a pillar of strength; an example of how to live; a devoted father; a doting grandfather; and a patriarch at the centre of his family’s universe.



Hundreds gathered on Saturday at Redfern Oval, the home of Mundine’s beloved Redfern All Blacks rugby league club, to farewell the 75-year-old, who died on Sunday from a heart attack. “Most of you know him as Tony Mundine the boxer. We know him as Tony Mundine the man: the husband; the father; the brother; the pop; the uncle; and the friend,” Mundine’s nephew, Craig Madden said. Tony Mundine during a 1973 training session. Keith Edward Byron/Fairfax Media “Uncle Tony was the backbone of our family. Steady, loyal, always there when we needed him.” Mundine was remembered on Saturday as not only a trailblazing athlete, but a mentor for Indigenous youth; it was outside the ring that Mundine had the greatest impact on his community.



“He built sanctuaries of hope for generations of community and young people, especially Aboriginal youth seeking direction, safe housing, or a second chance,” said another of Mundine’s nephews, Matthew Mundine. “Above all his titles and accolades, Tony’s heart belonged entirely to his family, culture and community.” A victorious Mundine in 1972. Martin Brannan Mundine playing for the Redfern All Blacks in 1975. Keith Edward Byron/Fairfax Media Mundine’s son Anthony, the former world boxing champion, recalled the kindness his father showed those battling substance abuse and homelessness during trips to Kings Cross in the 1980s.



“They all loved him,” he said. “The admiration and respect they gave this man, I was in awe.” Tony Mundine and son Anthony Mundine at the Elouera Tony Mundine Boxing Gym in 2016. Louise Kennerley Johnny Lewis, the legendary boxing trainer, said Mundine was considered the greatest Australian fighter to have never won a world championship. “To me, he was a world champion,” Lewis said. “We’re very, very lucky to have someone as good in the ring and out of the ring as Tony Mundine.” The large crowd gathered at Mundine’s funeral was testament to his impact on the Redfern community.



The suburb, where he and his brother Mick Mundine first arrived from Grafton in the 1960s, houses the Elouera Tony Mundine Boxing Gym – opened in 1985 in The Block, Redfern’s historic Indigenous neighbourhood before being relocated during the redevelopment of the estate. Related Article Vale Vale Tony Mundine, a champion fighter and a great Australian Up the street from Mundine’s boxing gym is Cafe Abercrombie where he would drink a honey-infused cup of tea every Friday. It closed on Saturday as a sign of respect. Friends recall starstruck admirers cautiously approaching Mundine at the cafe for a photograph. They were met with endless generosity and kindness. There, like other places Mundine spent time, he was simply Uncle Tony. As mourners said their goodbyes on Saturday, Mundine’s casket snaked its way through the streets of the suburb his life and legacy was built upon.



“We made sure we brought Dad back here to Redfern where it all started,” Mundine’s daughter, Kelly Mundine said. Among his final stops was The Block and his beloved boxing gym, where a bouquet was placed on the door before Tony Mundine left Redfern for the last time.
